doneWhen.es: Every student has ten tokens on their desk.

watchFor.en: Tokens going straight into pockets. They need to be visible on the desk.
watchFor.es: Tokens going straight into pockets. They need to be visible on the desk.

description.en: Each student receives 10 tokens (start equal). Tokens represent relative worth, not money.
description.es: Each student receives 10 tokens (start equal). Tokens represent relative worth, not money.

sayThis.en: "A trade is fair when the tokens balance. Three for three. Or a one plus two tokens. You can argue about the price — but you both have to agree before anything changes hands."
sayThis.es: "A trade is fair when the tokens balance. Three for three. Or a one plus two tokens. You can argue about the price — but you both have to agree before anything changes hands."

doneWhen.en: One trade has been demonstrated in front of everybody.
doneWhen.es: One trade has been demonstrated in front of everybody.

watchFor.en: Blank faces. Do one trade at the front with a volunteer before releasing the room.
watchFor.es: Blank faces. Do one trade at the front with a volunteer before releasing the room.

description.en: Teacher explains: "To make a trade fair, the tokens must balance. A 3-token item trades for another 3-token item, or for a 1-token item plus 2 tokens, or you can negotiate. Both people must agree the token balance is fair."
description.es: Teacher explains: "To make a trade fair, the tokens must balance. A 3-token item trades for another 3-token item, or for a 1-token item plus 2 tokens, or you can negotiate. Both people must agree the token balance is fair."

sayThis.en: "Go. Agree the tokens before you swap. If you can't agree, walk away. That's allowed and it isn't rude."
sayThis.es: "Go. Agree the tokens before you swap. If you can't agree, walk away. That's allowed and it isn't rude."

doneWhen.en: At least half the room has completed one trade.
doneWhen.es: At least half the room has completed one trade.

watchFor.en: The loud trader cornering quiet students. Stand near them. Also the student who trades nothing; ask what their price would have to be.
watchFor.es: The loud trader cornering quiet students. Stand near them. Also the student who trades nothing; ask what their price would have to be.

description.en: Open trading. Students must negotiate token values before swapping items.
description.es: Open trading. Students must negotiate token values before swapping items.

sayThis.en: "Stop. Does anybody feel like they got a bad deal? Tell us the trade and we'll vote on whether it was fair."
sayThis.es: "Stop. Does anybody feel like they got a bad deal? Tell us the trade and we'll vote on whether it was fair."

doneWhen.en: One trade has been put to the class and voted on.
doneWhen.es: One trade has been put to the class and voted on.

watchFor.en: Nobody speaking. Ask instead: who got the best deal in this room, and why?
watchFor.es: Nobody speaking. Ask instead: who got the best deal in this room, and why?

description.en: Pause. Anyone feel they got an unfair trade? How do we decide? Class votes on one disputed trade — was it fair?
description.es: Pause. Anyone feel they got an unfair trade? How do we decide? Class votes on one disputed trade — was it fair?

sayThis.en: "Same rules. But you can re-price the item you've got now, based on what you just learned."
sayThis.es: "Same rules. But you can re-price the item you've got now, based on what you just learned."

doneWhen.en: At least three students have changed a price on a card.
doneWhen.es: At least three students have changed a price on a card.

watchFor.en: Prices that never move. Ask them directly: did anyone want it at that price?
watchFor.es: Prices that never move. Ask them directly: did anyone want it at that price?

description.en: Continue trading. Students may re-value the item they have now based on what they learned.
description.es: Continue trading. Students may re-value the item they have now based on what they learned.

sayThis.en: "Three columns. The item. What you said it was worth. What it actually traded for. Everybody puts up one row." Then: "Circle every row where those two numbers don't match."
sayThis.es: "Three columns. The item. What you said it was worth. What it actually traded for. Everybody puts up one row." Then: "Circle every row where those two numbers don't match."

doneWhen.en: Every student has a row and the board is sorted into went up, went down, never traded.
doneWhen.es: Every student has a row and the board is sorted into went up, went down, never traded.

watchFor.en: Students skipping the third column because their item never traded. That's a row too — write zero. It's the most interesting line on the board.
watchFor.es: Students skipping the third column because their item never traded. That's a row too — write zero. It's the most interesting line on the board.

description.en: Build a value board on the class board: item, tokens it was first worth, tokens it actually traded for. Every student adds one row. Circle every row where the two numbers differ. Ask the traders in those rows what changed their mind. Then sort the board: which items went up, which went down, which never traded at all. Ask why the untraded items did not move, and whether a thing is worth anything if nobody wants it.
description.es: Build a value board on the class board: item, tokens it was first worth, tokens it actually traded for. Every student adds one row. Circle every row where the two numbers differ. Ask the traders in those rows what changed their mind. Then sort the board: which items went up, which went down, which never traded at all. Ask why the untraded items did not move, and whether a thing is worth anything if nobody wants it.

sayThis.en: "Count your tokens in and out. Did you come out ahead? Now the real question. Is something worth anything if nobody wants it?"
sayThis.es: "Count your tokens in and out. Did you come out ahead? Now the real question. Is something worth anything if nobody wants it?"

doneWhen.en: Every log shows tokens at the start and now, and two students have answered the untraded-items question out loud.
doneWhen.es: Every log shows tokens at the start and now, and two students have answered the untraded-items question out loud.

watchFor.en: "Profit" being read as winning. Ask whether the person who traded nothing lost.
watchFor.es: "Profit" being read as winning. Ask whether the person who traded nothing lost.

description.en: Each student writes a trade log on scrap paper: what they traded, tokens at the start (ten) and tokens now — did you "profit"? Whole-class debrief.
description.es: Each student writes a trade log on scrap paper: what they traded, tokens at the start (ten) and tokens now — did you "profit"? Whole-class debrief.

description.en: Each student counts their tokens and says if they have more than ten, fewer than ten, or ten. They draw what they traded on scrap paper. Whole-class talk.
description.es: Each student counts their tokens and says if they have more than ten, fewer than ten, or ten. They draw what they traded on scrap paper. Whole-class talk.

sayThis.en: "Count your tokens. Do you have more than ten, fewer, or the same? Draw what you traded." Then: "If nobody wants a thing, is it still worth something?"
sayThis.es: "Count your tokens. Do you have more than ten, fewer, or the same? Draw what you traded." Then: "If nobody wants a thing, is it still worth something?"

watchFor.en: Kids who think more tokens means they won. Ask if the child who kept their item lost.
watchFor.es: Kids who think more tokens means they won. Ask if the child who kept their item lost.

doneWhen.en: Every child has counted their tokens out loud and two children have answered the question.
doneWhen.es: Every child has counted their tokens out loud and two children have answered the question.

discussionQuestions: Was it harder to trade something you really liked? Why?
Did token values seem 'right' to everyone? What does that tell us about value?
Mr. Mason said 'reusing things means nothing goes to waste.' How is trading better for the environment?
How is Ellis's token system like money? How is it different?
If one item was very popular, did its value go up? What does that remind you of?
extensionIdeas: Run a class-wide trading post for a full week — add new items Monday, trade by Friday
Compare barter to modern "Buy Nothing" groups or Craigslist Free sections
Research: what did people in ancient civilizations trade? What was the first known currency and why was barter replaced?

beforeClass.en: Send a paper note home a day ahead asking each student to bring one item. Tear scrap paper into 200 small tokens and plain paper into 20 value card squares. Count out ten tokens per student into envelopes before the lesson. Doing it live burns five minutes and half of them end up on the floor. Keep the backup trade box ready for anyone who forgot. Decide your ruling in advance for a trade that goes wrong, because one will.
beforeClass.es: Send a paper note home a day ahead asking each student to bring one item. Tear scrap paper into 200 small tokens and plain paper into 20 value card squares. Count out ten tokens per student into envelopes before the lesson. Doing it live burns five minutes and half of them end up on the floor. Keep the backup trade box ready for anyone who forgot. Decide your ruling in advance for a trade that goes wrong, because one will.

runningLongOrShort.en: Long: cut Trading Round 2 to four minutes and keep the value board whole; the board is where the learning is. Short: add a third round where students may only trade with someone they haven't traded with yet.
runningLongOrShort.es: Long: cut Trading Round 2 to four minutes and keep the value board whole; the board is where the learning is. Short: add a third round where students may only trade with someone they haven't traded with yet.

beforeClass.en: Send a paper note home a day ahead asking each student to bring one item. Tear scrap paper into 200 small tokens and plain paper into 20 value card squares. Count out ten tokens per student into paper cups from home before the lesson. Doing it live burns five minutes and half of them end up on the floor. Keep the backup trade box ready for anyone who forgot. Decide your ruling in advance for a trade that goes wrong, because one will.
beforeClass.es: Send a paper note home a day ahead asking each student to bring one item. Tear scrap paper into 200 small tokens and plain paper into 20 value card squares. Count out ten tokens per student into paper cups from home before the lesson. Doing it live burns five minutes and half of them end up on the floor. Keep the backup trade box ready for anyone who forgot. Decide your ruling in advance for a trade that goes wrong, because one will.

focus: Bring one item and make a simple value card (draw it)
Make a fair one-for-one trade with help
Practice: "Do you want to trade?"
Words: trade, fair, mine, yours
Create value cards with a sentence frame
Negotiate a trade both people agree to
Explain why a trade felt fair
Vocabulary: negotiate, value, exchange, agree
Make multi-item trades and justify the value
Vote on whether a disputed trade was fair
Record each trade and whether it was fair
Vocabulary: barter, transaction, worth, compromise
Run a trading post and track all transactions
Re-price your item after seeing what it trades for
Reflect on what makes a trade fair to both sides
Vocabulary: supply, demand, transaction, perceived value

ell.label: English Language Learners
strategies: Teach three phrases with thumbs up and down: "Do you want to trade?" "Yes, deal." "No, thank you."
Let value cards be a drawing plus a token number instead of words.
Model one trade at the front with gestures before anyone trades.

learningDifferences.label: Students with Learning Differences
strategies: Use one simple value rule: small item, one token; big item, three tokens.
Give a trade buddy who helps make and answer offers.
Let a student watch one round before they start trading.

advanced.label: Advanced Students
strategies: Build trades that balance with tokens, like a 5-token item for a 3-token item plus two tokens.
After trading, tally which items people wanted most and explain why their value went up.
Write one new rule that would make the trading post fairer and explain it to the class.

title.en: Map It! Classroom Expedition & Blueprint Challenge
title.es: Map It! Classroom Expedition & Blueprint Challenge

description.en: Students create a simple map of their classroom or school, mark "points of interest," and then lead a partner through an expedition using only their map as a guide. The activity builds on observation, planning, and the insight that curiosity — not money — unlocks discovery.
description.es: Students create a simple map of their classroom or school, mark "points of interest," and then lead a partner through an expedition using only their map as a guide. The activity builds on observation, planning, and the insight that curiosity — not money — unlocks discovery.

20.label: 20 Minutes

fromScratch.costPerStudent: $0 — everything is free or from home
fromScratch.description: Each student draws a room map on plain paper with a pencil and crayons. The teacher draws the room outline on the board.
items: Plain paper — 25 sheets, one per student for the map, plus a few with the room outline drawn in for students who need it
Pencils — 20, one per student for drawing the map
Crayons — 4 boxes, shared, for the map shapes and pictures
Board — teacher, for the classroom outline

basicClassroom.costPerStudent: $0 — uses supplies the school already has

description.en: Ask: "Benny found an old map. What did it help him do?" (Find the creek. Go somewhere new. Discover things.) "Today you'll make a map of our classroom."
description.es: Ask: "Benny found an old map. What did it help him do?" (Find the creek. Go somewhere new. Discover things.) "Today you'll make a map of our classroom."

sayThis.en: "Benny found an old map. What did it help him do? Today you'll make a map of our classroom."
sayThis.es: "Benny found an old map. What did it help him do? Today you'll make a map of our classroom."

watchFor.en: Kids not sure what a map is. Point to your board outline and say, "This is our room, seen from up high."
watchFor.es: Kids not sure what a map is. Point to your board outline and say, "This is our room, seen from up high."

doneWhen.en: A student has said the map helped Benny find the creek.
doneWhen.es: A student has said the map helped Benny find the creek.

description.en: Students draw a simple top-down map of the classroom from memory — just the major shapes (door, windows, desks, board). No detail required. Label 3 spots with an X: one place that's always useful (e.g., the pencil sharpener), one that's interesting (a display on the wall), one that most people overlook.
description.es: Students draw a simple top-down map of the classroom from memory — just the major shapes (door, windows, desks, board). No detail required. Label 3 spots with an X: one place that's always useful (e.g., the pencil sharpener), one that's interesting (a display on the wall), one that most people overlook.

sayThis.en: "Draw our room like a bird sees it from the ceiling. Door, windows, desks, board. Then three X's: one useful spot, one interesting spot, and one spot nobody looks at."
sayThis.es: "Draw our room like a bird sees it from the ceiling. Door, windows, desks, board. Then three X's: one useful spot, one interesting spot, and one spot nobody looks at."

watchFor.en: Kids drawing every chair and running out of time. Say, "Big shapes only. Get your X's on."
watchFor.es: Kids drawing every chair and running out of time. Say, "Big shapes only. Get your X's on."

doneWhen.en: Every map has the big shapes and three X's.
doneWhen.es: Every map has the big shapes and three X's.

description.en: Students look around the room and draw a simple map of it from above with a pencil — just the big shapes (door, windows, desks, board). Then they draw 3 X's: one useful spot, one fun spot, and one spot nobody looks at. By each X they draw a small picture with crayons instead of writing a label.
description.es: Students look around the room and draw a simple map of it from above with a pencil — just the big shapes (door, windows, desks, board). Then they draw 3 X's: one useful spot, one fun spot, and one spot nobody looks at. By each X they draw a small picture with crayons instead of writing a label.

sayThis.en: "Look around our room. Draw it like a bird sees it from the ceiling. Door, windows, desks, board. Now draw three X's. Draw a little picture next to each X."
sayThis.es: "Look around our room. Draw it like a bird sees it from the ceiling. Door, windows, desks, board. Now draw three X's. Draw a little picture next to each X."

watchFor.en: Kids drawing every chair and running out of time. Say, "Big shapes only. Now your X's."
watchFor.es: Kids drawing every chair and running out of time. Say, "Big shapes only. Now your X's."

doneWhen.en: Every map has the big shapes, three X's, and a picture by each X.
doneWhen.es: Every map has the big shapes, three X's, and a picture by each X.

description.en: Swap maps with a partner. Can they find all 3 X spots using only the map?
description.es: Swap maps with a partner. Can they find all 3 X spots using only the map?

sayThis.en: "Swap maps. Use only the map. Can you point to all three X spots in our room?"
sayThis.es: "Swap maps. Use only the map. Can you point to all three X spots in our room?"

watchFor.en: Mapmakers pointing for their partner. Tell them to sit on their hands; the map has to do the work.
watchFor.es: Mapmakers pointing for their partner. Tell them to sit on their hands; the map has to do the work.

doneWhen.en: Every student has tried to find the X spots on a partner's map.
doneWhen.es: Every student has tried to find the X spots on a partner's map.

description.en: Swap maps with a partner. Can they point to the two X spots using only the map?
description.es: Swap maps with a partner. Can they point to the two X spots using only the map?

sayThis.en: "Swap maps. Look at your partner's map. Can you point to the two X spots in our room?"
sayThis.es: "Swap maps. Look at your partner's map. Can you point to the two X spots in our room?"

doneWhen.en: Every student has pointed at two spots in the room.
doneWhen.es: Every student has pointed at two spots in the room.

description.en: "What would happen if you went exploring without a map or a plan?"
description.es: "What would happen if you went exploring without a map or a plan?"

sayThis.en: "What would happen if you went exploring with no map and no plan?"
sayThis.es: "What would happen if you went exploring with no map and no plan?"

watchFor.en: Only "you get lost." Take it, then ask what else could go wrong.
watchFor.es: Only "you get lost." Take it, then ask what else could go wrong.

doneWhen.en: Two different answers have been said out loud.
doneWhen.es: Two different answers have been said out loud.

discussionQuestions: Did your partner's map make sense? What was missing?
Benny and his friends had never seen the creek up close, even though it was nearby. What free things exist near our school that most people haven't noticed?
How is a map like a plan for a project or a purchase?

beforeClass.en: Draw the classroom outline on the board with the door and the board marked, so kids see what a map from above looks like. Set out plain paper, pencils and crayons.
beforeClass.es: Draw the classroom outline on the board with the door and the board marked, so kids see what a map from above looks like. Set out plain paper, pencils and crayons.

runningLongOrShort.en: Long: in Draw Your Map, mark only two X spots, and give Partner Share one try. Short: in Partner Share, have partners swap back and fix one spot that was hard to find.
runningLongOrShort.es: Long: in Draw Your Map, mark only two X spots, and give Partner Share one try. Short: in Partner Share, have partners swap back and fix one spot that was hard to find.

description.en: Students draw a map of the classroom AND the hallway outside (or the school common area). Mark 5 Points of Interest with symbols: a star for "most useful," a heart for "most interesting," a question mark for "something I've never looked at closely."
description.es: Students draw a map of the classroom AND the hallway outside (or the school common area). Mark 5 Points of Interest with symbols: a star for "most useful," a heart for "most interesting," a question mark for "something I've never looked at closely."

sayThis.en: "Draw our room and the hallway outside. Mark five spots. A star is most useful. A heart is most interesting. A question mark is something you've never looked at closely."
sayThis.es: "Draw our room and the hallway outside. Mark five spots. A star is most useful. A heart is most interesting. A question mark is something you've never looked at closely."

watchFor.en: Maps full of stars and no question marks. Ask, "What do you walk past every day and never look at?"
watchFor.es: Maps full of stars and no question marks. Ask, "What do you walk past every day and never look at?"

doneWhen.en: Every map shows five marked spots, with at least one question mark.
doneWhen.es: Every map shows five marked spots, with at least one question mark.

description.en: Students take their map and walk to at least 3 of their marked spots. At each spot, they write one entry in their Discovery Log: "I found ___. It's ___ (free / useful / interesting). I notice it because ___."
description.es: Students take their map and walk to at least 3 of their marked spots. At each spot, they write one entry in their Discovery Log: "I found ___. It's ___ (free / useful / interesting). I notice it because ___."

sayThis.en: "Take your map. Go to at least three of your spots. At each one, write: I found ___. It's free, useful, or interesting. I noticed it because ___."
sayThis.es: "Take your map. Go to at least three of your spots. At each one, write: I found ___. It's free, useful, or interesting. I noticed it because ___."

watchFor.en: The whole class crowding one spot. Send each student to the spots on their own map first.
watchFor.es: The whole class crowding one spot. Send each student to the spots on their own map first.

doneWhen.en: Every Discovery Log has at least three entries.
doneWhen.es: Every Discovery Log has at least three entries.

description.en: Students take their map and their Discovery Log and walk to at least 3 of their marked spots. At each spot, they draw what they found in the log with a pencil or crayon, then say one word about it to a partner.
description.es: Students take their map and their Discovery Log and walk to at least 3 of their marked spots. At each spot, they draw what they found in the log with a pencil or crayon, then say one word about it to a partner.

sayThis.en: "Take your map and your log. Go to three of your spots. At each one, draw what you found. Then tell a partner one word about it."
sayThis.es: "Take your map and your log. Go to three of your spots. At each one, draw what you found. Then tell a partner one word about it."

watchFor.en: The whole class crowding one spot. Send each child to the spots on their own map first.
watchFor.es: The whole class crowding one spot. Send each child to the spots on their own map first.

doneWhen.en: Every Discovery Log has at least three drawings.
doneWhen.es: Every Discovery Log has at least three drawings.

description.en: Back at desks, compare discovery logs with a partner. "Did you notice the same things? Different things? Why?"
description.es: Back at desks, compare discovery logs with a partner. "Did you notice the same things? Different things? Why?"

sayThis.en: "Show your partner your log. Did you notice the same things? Different things? Why?"
sayThis.es: "Show your partner your log. Did you notice the same things? Different things? Why?"

watchFor.en: Partners just reading lists at each other. Ask each pair to find one thing only one of them noticed.
watchFor.es: Partners just reading lists at each other. Ask each pair to find one thing only one of them noticed.

doneWhen.en: Every pair can name one thing only one partner found.
doneWhen.es: Every pair can name one thing only one partner found.

description.en: Teacher asks: "How many of you found something interesting you walk past every day?" (Expect hands.) "That's what Benny did — he found the creek. It was always there."
description.es: Teacher asks: "How many of you found something interesting you walk past every day?" (Expect hands.) "That's what Benny did — he found the creek. It was always there."

sayThis.en: "Hands up if you found something interesting you walk past every day. That's what Benny did. The creek was always there."
sayThis.es: "Hands up if you found something interesting you walk past every day. That's what Benny did. The creek was always there."

watchFor.en: Hands staying down. Ask one student to name their question-mark spot.
watchFor.es: Hands staying down. Ask one student to name their question-mark spot.

doneWhen.en: Hands have gone up and one student has named a find.
doneWhen.es: Hands have gone up and one student has named a find.

discussionQuestions: What did you discover that surprised you?
How is being curious a kind of resource? What does it cost?
What free things are in our school that new students might miss?
Benny had a plan (the map). How did having a plan make the expedition go better?

beforeClass.en: Walk the hallway or common area and decide how far students may go. Set out plain paper, pencils, crayons, and scrap paper for Discovery Logs. Draw the three symbols on the board: star, heart, question mark.
beforeClass.es: Walk the hallway or common area and decide how far students may go. Set out plain paper, pencils, crayons, and scrap paper for Discovery Logs. Draw the three symbols on the board: star, heart, question mark.

runningLongOrShort.en: Long: cut the Expedition to two spots and have each partner share one find in Return & Compare. Short: in the Expedition, have students visit all five spots.

sayThis.en: "Before you move, plan. Where are you going? What route? What do you think you'll find? Then draw the map with your route on it."
sayThis.es: "Before you move, plan. Where are you going? What route? What do you think you'll find? Then draw the map with your route on it."

doneWhen.es: Every planning sheet has a route drawn on it.

description.en: Students complete an Expedition Planning Sheet: "Where will I go? What route will I take? What do I expect to find?" Then draw their map with a marked route.
description.es: Students complete an Expedition Planning Sheet: "Where will I go? What route will I take? What do I expect to find?" Then draw their map with a marked route.

sayThis.en: "You're hunting three kinds of thing. Something that's there but people ignore. Something free to use. Something you've never noticed. At every stop write it in your Discovery Log — found this, worth this."
sayThis.es: "You're hunting three kinds of thing. Something that's there but people ignore. Something free to use. Something you've never noticed. At every stop write it in your Discovery Log — found this, worth this."

doneWhen.en: Every log has at least three finds written in it.

description.en: Teams of four combine their four maps into one classroom guidebook page on a shared sheet. Ask what made the winning one easy to follow — and whether their own solo map would have made sense to a stranger.

discussionQuestions: How did having a plan change your expedition compared to just wandering?
Mr. Mason gave Benny a notebook so he could draw his own maps. Why is making your OWN plan important?
The stepping stones across the creek were 'stable' — meaning safe and trustworthy. What makes a plan stable? What makes it unstable?
Benny found the creek because he found a MAP, not because he bought anything. What else do people discover without spending money?
What would happen if you planned a purchase the same way you planned this expedition — making a map before spending?
extensionIdeas: Create a "School Discovery Guide" — a real map for new students showing the best free resources and interesting spots
Design a neighborhood map showing free recreation options (parks, trails, public art, libraries)

ell.label: English Language Learners
strategies: Teach map words with the board outline: door, window, desk, board, map.
Let students mark spots with the picture symbols and draw their finds instead of writing.
Give the frame "I found ___. It is ___." for each Discovery Log entry.

learningDifferences.label: Students with Learning Differences
strategies: Give a pre-drawn outline of the room so students only add X's and symbols.
Mark the walking boundary clearly and show a visual timer during the expedition.
Let students tell a partner their finds instead of writing log entries.

advanced.label: Advanced Students
strategies: Add a key to the map and use a ruler to draw it closer to scale.
Plan the shortest route that visits all their spots and count the steps.
Draw a guide map for a new student showing the best free spots in the school.

description.en: Each student identifies one thing they're genuinely good at — not necessarily art, but anything — and creates a "skill card." In a structured Skills Fair, students spend time teaching their skill to a partner. The experience of being sought out for what you know generates the same "full inside" feeling Riley describes in the episode.

description.en: Students complete a detailed skill card on their half sheet of paper, in pencil: Skill Title, "I can teach you ___," "To do this well, you need to ___," "Here's the hardest part: ___." This prepares them to actually teach, not just demonstrate.
description.es: Students complete a detailed skill card on their half sheet of paper, in pencil: Skill Title, "I can teach you ___," "To do this well, you need to ___," "Here's the hardest part: ___." This prepares them to actually teach, not just demonstrate.

description.en: Students draw their skill on their card with a pencil. The teacher helps write the skill name. Each student tells a partner the hardest part of the skill.
description.es: Students draw their skill on their card with a pencil. The teacher helps write the skill name. Each student tells a partner the hardest part of the skill.

sayThis.en: "Draw your skill on your card. Then tell your partner: what is the hardest part?"
sayThis.es: "Draw your skill on your card. Then tell your partner: what is the hardest part?"

watchFor.en: "I don't have a skill." Nobody gets to say that. Tying laces, helping a little brother, finding things — all skills. Name one for them if you have to.
watchFor.es: "I don't have a skill." Nobody gets to say that. Tying laces, helping a little brother, finding things — all skills. Name one for them if you have to.

doneWhen.en: Every student has a drawing on the card and has told a partner the hardest part.
doneWhen.es: Every student has a drawing on the card and has told a partner the hardest part.

sayThis.en: "Cards on desks. One silent minute. Walk and read. No talking yet — you're shopping."
sayThis.es: "Cards on desks. One silent minute. Walk and read. No talking yet — you're shopping."

doneWhen.en: Every student is back at their own desk and the room has gone quiet.
doneWhen.es: Every student is back at their own desk and the room has gone quiet.

watchFor.en: Talking. Hold the silence; it makes the next step faster.
watchFor.es: Talking. Hold the silence; it makes the next step faster.

description.en: Cards are placed on desks. Students do a 1-minute silent gallery walk reading cards — no talking yet.
description.es: Cards are placed on desks. Students do a 1-minute silent gallery walk reading cards — no talking yet.

sayThis.en: "Three rounds, five minutes each. Go to the person you want to learn from. Teachers teach. Learners fill in the passport. When I call time, you move."
sayThis.es: "Three rounds, five minutes each. Go to the person you want to learn from. Teachers teach. Learners fill in the passport. When I call time, you move."

doneWhen.en: Every passport has three entries in it.
doneWhen.es: Every passport has three entries in it.

watchFor.en: Popular students swamped and quiet students alone. Cap it at three learners per teacher and steer people by name.
watchFor.es: Popular students swamped and quiet students alone. Cap it at three learners per teacher and steer people by name.

description.en: Three 5-minute rounds. Each round: students move to one "teacher" they want to learn from. Teacher teaches; learner fills in their Passport. When the round ends, learners rotate. Each student teaches 3 people total.
description.es: Three 5-minute rounds. Each round: students move to one "teacher" they want to learn from. Teacher teaches; learner fills in their Passport. When the round ends, learners rotate. Each student teaches 3 people total.

sayThis.en: "Frances brought Riley flowers at the art stand. Nobody made her do it. Write a thank-you note on your scrap of paper to one person who taught you something. Say what you can do now that you couldn't do an hour ago."
sayThis.es: "Frances brought Riley flowers at the art stand. Nobody made her do it. Write a thank-you note on your scrap of paper to one person who taught you something. Say what you can do now that you couldn't do an hour ago."

doneWhen.en: Every student has written and delivered one thank-you note.
doneWhen.es: Every student has written and delivered one thank-you note.

watchFor.en: "Thanks, it was fun." Send it back. It has to name the thing learned.
watchFor.es: "Thanks, it was fun." Send it back. It has to name the thing learned.

description.en: After the market, each student writes a thank-you note on a scrap of paper for one person who taught them something. Discuss: "Frances brought Riley flowers at the art stand. What is that equivalent to in the Skills Market?"
description.es: After the market, each student writes a thank-you note on a scrap of paper for one person who taught them something. Discuss: "Frances brought Riley flowers at the art stand. What is that equivalent to in the Skills Market?"

sayThis.en: "Put a price on your card. What would you charge to teach this to one person for one hour? Then swap with your partner and argue. Too high, too low, why."
sayThis.es: "Put a price on your card. What would you charge to teach this to one person for one hour? Then swap with your partner and argue. Too high, too low, why."

doneWhen.en: Every price is on the board and the class total is read out loud.
doneWhen.es: Every price is on the board and the class total is read out loud.

watchFor.en: Everyone writing the same number. Ask whether the hardest skill in the room and the easiest are really worth the same.
watchFor.es: Everyone writing the same number. Ask whether the hardest skill in the room and the easiest are really worth the same.

description.en: Each student writes a price on their skill card: what would you charge to teach this to one person for one hour? Pairs challenge each other's price — too high, too low, and why. Then a recorder totals every price on the board. Point at it: "That is one hour of this room's time." Ask what makes one skill worth more than another, and whether the hardest skill to learn is always the most valuable.
description.es: Each student writes a price on their skill card: what would you charge to teach this to one person for one hour? Pairs challenge each other's price — too high, too low, and why. Then a recorder totals every price on the board. Point at it: "That is one hour of this room's time." Ask what makes one skill worth more than another, and whether the hardest skill to learn is always the most valuable.

description.en: Each student picks a price in whole dollars, from $1 to $10, to teach their skill to one friend. The teacher writes each price on the board. Partners say if a price feels too high or too low. The teacher does the adding and reads the class total. Ask: is a harder skill worth more?
description.es: Each student picks a price in whole dollars, from $1 to $10, to teach their skill to one friend. The teacher writes each price on the board. Partners say if a price feels too high or too low. The teacher does the adding and reads the class total. Ask: is a harder skill worth more?

sayThis.en: "How many dollars would you charge to teach your skill to a friend? Pick a number from 1 to 10. Tell your partner. Too high or too low?"
sayThis.es: "How many dollars would you charge to teach your skill to a friend? Pick a number from 1 to 10. Tell your partner. Too high or too low?"

watchFor.en: Everyone saying the same number. Ask, "Is tying shoes worth the same as drawing a horse?"
watchFor.es: Everyone saying the same number. Ask, "Is tying shoes worth the same as drawing a horse?"

doneWhen.en: Every price is on the board and the teacher has read the class total out loud.
doneWhen.es: Every price is on the board and the teacher has read the class total out loud.

sayThis.en: "Every different skill in this room, one list. Count them. That's what this room owns, and none of it cost a thing."
sayThis.es: "Every different skill in this room, one list. Count them. That's what this room owns, and none of it cost a thing."

doneWhen.en: The list is on the board and the count is written at the bottom.
doneWhen.es: The list is on the board and the count is written at the bottom.

watchFor.en: Skills getting merged to save time. Keep them separate; the length of the list is the point.
watchFor.es: Skills getting merged to save time. Keep them separate; the length of the list is the point.

description.en: Together, create a class list: "Our classroom's skills:" — tally each unique skill. "We have ___ different skills in this room. Together, we're worth ___."
description.es: Together, create a class list: "Our classroom's skills:" — tally each unique skill. "We have ___ different skills in this room. Together, we're worth ___."

discussionQuestions: Did you value your skill more or less after teaching it? Why?
What happened when multiple people wanted the same teacher? (High demand.)
Riley could have sold her art instead of giving it. Would the lesson have been the same?
What's the difference between a skill you can sell, a skill you choose to give, and a skill nobody wants?
What skill does your family have that saves them money? (Cooking, fixing things, growing food.)
extensionIdeas: Create a "Class Skills Directory" that students add to over the school year — resource for when someone needs help
Explore: what are the most valuable skills in different careers? How do you develop a skill into something people pay for?
Compare: Riley's art stand is free. A commissioned art piece costs money. What changed? When is it okay to charge for something?

beforeClass.en: Decide how you'll move the room for three rotations and say it before round one starts. Have a fallback skill in your pocket for the student who says they have none. Set out index cards, pencils and a scrap of paper per student. Fold one passport per student from plain paper, or have students fold them before Skills Market Rounds.
beforeClass.es: Decide how you'll move the room for three rotations and say it before round one starts. Have a fallback skill in your pocket for the student who says they have none. Set out index cards, pencils and a scrap of paper per student. Fold one passport per student from plain paper, or have students fold them before Skills Market Rounds.

runningLongOrShort.en: Long: cut the market to two rounds instead of three. Short: add a fourth round where students must learn from someone they've never worked with.
runningLongOrShort.es: Long: cut the market to two rounds instead of three. Short: add a fourth round where students must learn from someone they've never worked with.

beforeClass.en: Decide how you'll move the room for three rotations and say it before round one starts. Have a fallback skill in your pocket for the student who says they have none. Tear plain paper sheets in half for skill cards, and set out pencils and a scrap of paper per student. Fold one passport per student from plain paper, or have students fold them before Skills Market Rounds.
beforeClass.es: Decide how you'll move the room for three rotations and say it before round one starts. Have a fallback skill in your pocket for the student who says they have none. Tear plain paper sheets in half for skill cards, and set out pencils and a scrap of paper per student. Fold one passport per student from plain paper, or have students fold them before Skills Market Rounds.

focus: Name one thing you are good at
Make a skill card (draw it)
Show your skill to a partner
Words: skill, good, teach, learn
Describe your skill in a sentence
Teach your skill step by step to a partner
Notice a skill you learned from someone
Vocabulary: skill, practice, teach, talent
Break your skill into clear steps to teach it
Teach three people and fill in your passport
Explain how skills have value to others
Vocabulary: expertise, feedback, value, demonstrate
Plan a mini-lesson and teach it effectively
Evaluate which skills are most useful and why
Reflect on how skills can be traded or hired
Vocabulary: proficiency, specialization, market value, mentor

ell.label: English Language Learners
strategies: Let students show their skill with their hands first and add words after.
Give the frames "My skill is ___." and "First you ___. Then you ___."
Pair students with a partner who speaks their language for the first teaching round.

learningDifferences.label: Students with Learning Differences
strategies: Offer a short list of skills to pick from (tying shoes, drawing a cat, clapping a rhythm) with a picture for each.
Let students draw the skill card and tell the teacher the words.
Let a student watch the first teaching round before they teach.

advanced.label: Advanced Students
strategies: Write the skill as three numbered steps a stranger could follow.
Teach a harder version of the skill to a second partner and note what they had to explain differently.
Explain what they would charge to teach the skill for an hour, and why.

description.en: Students run a classroom savings simulation over the course of one week (or compressed into a single session). They "save" virtual or play coins into a class savings jar each day, practice counting and recording, then make a group decision about what to do with the accumulated total — mirroring the friends' debate in the episode.
description.es: Students run a classroom savings simulation over the course of one week (or compressed into a single session). They "save" virtual or play coins into a class savings jar each day, practice counting and recording, then make a group decision about what to do with the accumulated total — mirroring the friends' debate in the episode.

20.label: 20 Minutes

fromScratch.costPerStudent: $0 — everything is free or from home
fromScratch.description: The teacher tears paper coins from plain paper. Each group of four sorts and counts one pile and writes its counts on scrap paper in pencil. The teacher checks totals on the board.
items: Plain paper — 5 sheets, teacher tears into paper coins, one mixed pile per group (5 groups of 4)
Scrap paper — 6 pieces, one per group for the counts plus one for the teacher's answer list, free
Pencils — 5, one per group for writing the counts
Board — teacher, for counting a total together

basicClassroom.costPerStudent: $0 — uses supplies the school already has
basicClassroom.description: The teacher cuts paper coins from plain paper with scissors. Each group of four sorts and counts one pile and writes its counts on scrap paper in pencil. The teacher checks totals on the board.
items: Plain paper — 5 sheets, teacher cuts into paper coins, one mixed pile per group (5 groups of 4)
Scissors — 1, teacher, for cutting the paper coins
Scrap paper — 6 pieces, one per group for the counts plus one for the teacher's answer list, free
Pencils — 5, one per group for writing the counts
Board — teacher, for counting a total together

description.en: "The friends found $4.73 in one week just by looking. Today you're going to count a jar of coins and figure out the total."
description.es: "The friends found $4.73 in one week just by looking. Today you're going to count a jar of coins and figure out the total."

sayThis.en: "The friends found four dollars and seventy-three cents in one week, just by looking. Your group gets a pile of coins. Let's find out how much it is."
sayThis.es: "The friends found four dollars and seventy-three cents in one week, just by looking. Your group gets a pile of coins. Let's find out how much it is."

watchFor.en: Kids who can't tell the coins apart. Hold up each coin once and say its name and value.
watchFor.es: Kids who can't tell the coins apart. Hold up each coin once and say its name and value.

doneWhen.en: The class has named all four coins with you.
doneWhen.es: The class has named all four coins with you.

description.en: Tell the class the friends found a big pile of coins in one week just by looking. Skip the exact amount. Hold up each coin and say its name. Names only, not values.
description.es: Tell the class the friends found a big pile of coins in one week just by looking. Skip the exact amount. Hold up each coin and say its name. Names only, not values.

sayThis.en: "The friends found a big pile of coins in one week, just by looking. Here is a penny. A nickel. A dime. A quarter. Say them with me."
sayThis.es: "The friends found a big pile of coins in one week, just by looking. Here is a penny. A nickel. A dime. A quarter. Say them with me."

watchFor.en: Kids mixing up nickels and quarters. Hold the two up side by side and say, "The big one is a quarter."
watchFor.es: Kids mixing up nickels and quarters. Hold the two up side by side and say, "The big one is a quarter."

description.en: Each group gets a pile of mixed coins. Sort into piles: pennies, nickels, dimes, quarters.
description.es: Each group gets a pile of mixed coins. Sort into piles: pennies, nickels, dimes, quarters.

sayThis.en: "Make four piles. Pennies. Nickels. Dimes. Quarters. Read the number on each coin."
sayThis.es: "Make four piles. Pennies. Nickels. Dimes. Quarters. Read the number on each coin."

watchFor.en: One child doing all the sorting. Give each person in the group one kind of coin to collect.
watchFor.es: One child doing all the sorting. Give each person in the group one kind of coin to collect.

doneWhen.en: Every group has four piles with no mixed coins.
doneWhen.es: Every group has four piles with no mixed coins.

description.en: Each group sorts its pile into three piles: pennies, dimes and quarters. Take the nickels out before you hand the pile over - nickels and quarters look too much alike at this age. Sort by color and size, not by reading numbers.
description.es: Each group sorts its pile into three piles: pennies, dimes and quarters. Take the nickels out before you hand the pile over - nickels and quarters look too much alike at this age. Sort by color and size, not by reading numbers.

sayThis.en: "Make three piles. Pennies are brown. Dimes are the little silver ones. Quarters are the big silver ones."
sayThis.es: "Make three piles. Pennies are brown. Dimes are the little silver ones. Quarters are the big silver ones."

doneWhen.en: Every group has three piles and no coins left over.
doneWhen.es: Every group has three piles and no coins left over.

description.en: Count each pile. Record how many of each on the group's scrap of paper, in pencil. "We have ___ pennies, ___ nickels, ___ dimes, ___ quarters."
description.es: Count each pile. Record how many of each on the group's scrap of paper, in pencil. "We have ___ pennies, ___ nickels, ___ dimes, ___ quarters."

sayThis.en: "Count each pile. Touch each coin as you count. Fill in: We have ___ pennies, ___ nickels, ___ dimes, ___ quarters."
sayThis.es: "Count each pile. Touch each coin as you count. Fill in: We have ___ pennies, ___ nickels, ___ dimes, ___ quarters."

watchFor.en: Kids counting money instead of coins. Say, "How many coins, not how much money. That comes next."
watchFor.es: Kids counting money instead of coins. Say, "How many coins, not how much money. That comes next."

doneWhen.en: Every group has four numbers written down.
doneWhen.es: Every group has four numbers written down.

description.en: Each group counts a pile out loud, touching every coin. The teacher writes the three numbers on the board. No writing for students.
description.es: Each group counts a pile out loud, touching every coin. The teacher writes the three numbers on the board. No writing for students.

sayThis.en: "Count your pennies. Touch each one as you count. Tell me the number and I will write it on the board. Now your dimes."
sayThis.es: "Count your pennies. Touch each one as you count. Tell me the number and I will write it on the board. Now your dimes."

doneWhen.en: The board shows three numbers for every group.
doneWhen.es: The board shows three numbers for every group.

description.en: Add up the total. Teacher checks with the class. Correct if needed.
description.es: Add up the total. Teacher checks with the class. Correct if needed.

sayThis.en: "Now how much money? Count the quarters by 25s, the dimes by 10s, the nickels by 5s, then add the pennies."
sayThis.es: "Now how much money? Count the quarters by 25s, the dimes by 10s, the nickels by 5s, then add the pennies."

watchFor.en: Groups stuck when time runs out. Do one group's total on the board, counting out loud together.
watchFor.es: Groups stuck when time runs out. Do one group's total on the board, counting out loud together.

doneWhen.en: Each group's total has been checked against your list.
doneWhen.es: Each group's total has been checked against your list.

description.en: Students count their pennies one by one. Then the teacher counts the rest of the pile out loud on the board: nickels by 5s, dimes by 10s, quarters by 25s. The class counts along.
description.es: Students count their pennies one by one. Then the teacher counts the rest of the pile out loud on the board: nickels by 5s, dimes by 10s, quarters by 25s. The class counts along.

sayThis.en: "Count your pennies. Touch each one. Now count with me. Nickels go 5, 10, 15."
sayThis.es: "Count your pennies. Touch each one. Now count with me. Nickels go 5, 10, 15."

watchFor.en: Kids who lose count. Have them slide each coin to a new spot as they count it.
watchFor.es: Kids who lose count. Have them slide each coin to a new spot as they count it.

doneWhen.en: Each group has counted its pennies and counted its total along with you.
doneWhen.es: Each group has counted its pennies and counted its total along with you.

discussionQuestions: Did the total surprise you? Were there more pennies or more dimes?
If you found 1 coin every day for a year, how much would you have?
What would you do with $4.73 — spend it, split it, save it, or buy something for the group?

beforeClass.en: Cut paper coins from plain paper with scissors and write 1¢, 5¢, 10¢ or 25¢ on each one. Make one mixed pile per group of four, and write on a scrap of paper how many of each coin you put in so you can check their counts. Put a pencil and a scrap of paper with each pile.
beforeClass.es: Cut paper coins from plain paper with scissors and write 1¢, 5¢, 10¢ or 25¢ on each one. Make one mixed pile per group of four, and write on a scrap of paper how many of each coin you put in so you can check their counts. Put a pencil and a scrap of paper with each pile.

runningLongOrShort.en: Long: in Count Each Pile, count only pennies and dimes, and do Calculate Total together on the board. Short: in Calculate Total, have groups trade piles and check each other's total.
runningLongOrShort.es: Long: in Count Each Pile, count only pennies and dimes, and do Calculate Total together on the board. Short: in Calculate Total, have groups trade piles and check each other's total.

beforeClass.es: Tear plain paper into small squares for coins and write 1¢, 5¢, 10¢ or 25¢ on each one. Make one mixed pile per group of four, and write on a scrap of paper how many of each coin you put in so you can check their counts. Put a pencil and a scrap of paper with each pile.

description.en: Each student draws a savings jar tracker on a sheet of plain paper with a pencil, or receives one already drawn. Explain: "Each day this week, you'll save a different amount. Today is Day 1 — save 25 cents." Students draw a quarter in Row 1 and write $0.25.
description.es: Each student draws a savings jar tracker on a sheet of plain paper with a pencil, or receives one already drawn. Explain: "Each day this week, you'll save a different amount. Today is Day 1 — save 25 cents." Students draw a quarter in Row 1 and write $0.25.

sayThis.en: "This is your savings jar tracker. Seven rows, one for each day. Day 1: you found a quarter. Draw it in Row 1 and write $0.25."
sayThis.es: "This is your savings jar tracker. Seven rows, one for each day. Day 1: you found a quarter. Draw it in Row 1 and write $0.25."

watchFor.en: Rows too small to draw coins in. Tell them to make each row about two fingers tall.
watchFor.es: Rows too small to draw coins in. Tell them to make each row about two fingers tall.

doneWhen.en: Every tracker has seven rows and a quarter with $0.25 in Row 1.
doneWhen.es: Every tracker has seven rows and a quarter with $0.25 in Row 1.

description.en: Each student gets a savings jar tracker drawn on plain paper, seven rows for Day 1 to Day 7. Day 1: you found a quarter. Students draw a quarter in Row 1 with a pencil and write 25¢.
description.es: Each student gets a savings jar tracker drawn on plain paper, seven rows for Day 1 to Day 7. Day 1: you found a quarter. Students draw a quarter in Row 1 with a pencil and write 25¢.

sayThis.en: "This is your savings jar. Seven rows, one for each day. Day 1: you found a quarter. Draw it in Row 1 and write 25 cents."
sayThis.es: "This is your savings jar. Seven rows, one for each day. Day 1: you found a quarter. Draw it in Row 1 and write 25 cents."

watchFor.en: Kids who are not sure which coin is a quarter. Draw one on the board and say its name.
watchFor.es: Kids who are not sure which coin is a quarter. Draw one on the board and say its name.

doneWhen.en: Every tracker has a quarter and 25¢ in Row 1.
doneWhen.es: Every tracker has a quarter and 25¢ in Row 1.

description.en: Run all 7 days in 8 minutes. Teacher calls out each day's "find": - Day 1: 25¢ (quarter near the vending machine) - Day 2: 10¢ (dime at the park bench) - Day 3: 3¢ (three pennies near the fountain) - Day 4: 5¢ (nickel outside the corner store) - Day 5: 50¢ (found in the wash at home) - Day 6: 35¢ (three dimes and a nickel) - Day 7: $3.45 (found a whole collection — big find!) Students record each day and draw the coins.
description.es: Run all 7 days in 8 minutes. Teacher calls out each day's "find": - Day 1: 25¢ (quarter near the vending machine) - Day 2: 10¢ (dime at the park bench) - Day 3: 3¢ (three pennies near the fountain) - Day 4: 5¢ (nickel outside the corner store) - Day 5: 50¢ (found in the wash at home) - Day 6: 35¢ (three dimes and a nickel) - Day 7: $3.45 (found a whole collection — big find!) Students record each day and draw the coins.

sayThis.en: "Day 2: a dime at the park bench. Draw it and write ten cents." Keep going, one day at a time.
sayThis.es: "Day 2: a dime at the park bench. Draw it and write ten cents." Keep going, one day at a time.

watchFor.en: Kids falling behind while drawing. Tell them to write the amount first and draw only if there's time.
watchFor.es: Kids falling behind while drawing. Tell them to write the amount first and draw only if there's time.

doneWhen.en: Every tracker has all seven days written in.
doneWhen.es: Every tracker has all seven days written in.

description.en: Run all 7 days in 8 minutes. Call out each day's find and draw the coins on the board: Day 2 a dime, Day 3 three pennies, Day 4 a nickel, Day 5 two quarters, Day 6 three dimes and a nickel. Day 7 is a big find, a whole pile of coins, so students draw a big pile. Students copy the coins into their tracker.
description.es: Run all 7 days in 8 minutes. Call out each day's find and draw the coins on the board: Day 2 a dime, Day 3 three pennies, Day 4 a nickel, Day 5 two quarters, Day 6 three dimes and a nickel. Day 7 is a big find, a whole pile of coins, so students draw a big pile. Students copy the coins into their tracker.

sayThis.en: "Day 2: a dime at the park bench. Draw one dime in Row 2." Keep going, one day at a time.
sayThis.es: "Day 2: a dime at the park bench. Draw one dime in Row 2." Keep going, one day at a time.

watchFor.en: Kids falling behind while drawing. Leave the coins on the board so they can catch up.
watchFor.es: Kids falling behind while drawing. Leave the coins on the board so they can catch up.

doneWhen.en: Every tracker has coins drawn in all seven rows.
doneWhen.es: Every tracker has coins drawn in all seven rows.

description.en: Students add up all 7 days. Compare with a partner. Correct answer: $4.73.
description.es: Students add up all 7 days. Compare with a partner. Correct answer: $4.73.

sayThis.en: "Add up all seven days. Then check with your partner. Do you match?"
sayThis.es: "Add up all seven days. Then check with your partner. Do you match?"

watchFor.en: The $3.45 lined up wrong with the small amounts. Have them add Days 1 to 6 first ($1.28), then add $3.45.
watchFor.es: The $3.45 lined up wrong with the small amounts. Have them add Days 1 to 6 first ($1.28), then add $3.45.

doneWhen.en: Every pair agrees on $4.73.
doneWhen.es: Every pair agrees on $4.73.

description.en: Students count how many coins they drew this week and compare with a partner. Then the teacher shows the $4.73 total on the board.
description.es: Students count how many coins they drew this week and compare with a partner. Then the teacher shows the $4.73 total on the board.

sayThis.en: "Count every coin you drew. Touch each one. Does your partner have the same number?"
sayThis.es: "Count every coin you drew. Touch each one. Does your partner have the same number?"

watchFor.en: Kids counting one coin twice. Have them make a small mark on each coin as they count it.
watchFor.es: Kids counting one coin twice. Have them make a small mark on each coin as they count it.

doneWhen.en: Every pair has counted their coins and seen the total on the board.
doneWhen.es: Every pair has counted their coins and seen the total on the board.

description.en: Read aloud the three options from the story: "Benny said SPLIT IT. Ellis said SAVE IT. Layla said BUY SOMETHING WE ALL SHARE." Class vote. Discuss why people chose differently.
description.es: Read aloud the three options from the story: "Benny said SPLIT IT. Ellis said SAVE IT. Layla said BUY SOMETHING WE ALL SHARE." Class vote. Discuss why people chose differently.

sayThis.en: "Benny said split it. Ellis said save it. Layla said buy something we all share. Which would you pick? Hands up for each one."
sayThis.es: "Benny said split it. Ellis said save it. Layla said buy something we all share. Which would you pick? Hands up for each one."

watchFor.en: Kids voting with their best friend. Before the vote, have each student tell a partner one reason for their pick.
watchFor.es: Kids voting with their best friend. Before the vote, have each student tell a partner one reason for their pick.

doneWhen.en: The vote count is on the board and two students have explained different choices.
doneWhen.es: The vote count is on the board and two students have explained different choices.

discussionQuestions: Did Day 7's big find change things? What if you'd spent the first $1.28 before Day 7?
Ellis wrote everything in his notebook. Why was that helpful?
Why did Mr. Mason's penny jar story change how the friends thought about their money?
If you save $4.73 per week, how much do you have in a month? ($18.92) Tier 1 (K-1): if you save $1 a week, how much do you have after 4 weeks?

beforeClass.en: Draw a tracker with seven rows, Day 1 to Day 7, on the board for kids to copy, or give each student one already drawn. Keep the list of daily finds in your hand so you can call them out fast.
beforeClass.es: Draw a tracker with seven rows, Day 1 to Day 7, on the board for kids to copy, or give each student one already drawn. Keep the list of daily finds in your hand so you can call them out fast.

runningLongOrShort.en: Long: in the Week Simulation, have students write the amounts and skip drawing the coins. Short: in The Group Decision, ask one student from each side to explain their vote.
runningLongOrShort.es: Long: in the Week Simulation, have students write the amounts and skip drawing the coins. Short: in The Group Decision, ask one student from each side to explain their vote.

sayThis.en: "Four columns. Date. Amount. Running total. Where you found it. Ellis kept records — that's the only reason he knew there was four dollars and seventy-three cents."
sayThis.es: "Four columns. Date. Amount. Running total. Where you found it. Ellis kept records — that's the only reason he knew there was four dollars and seventy-three cents."

doneWhen.en: Every ledger has four labeled columns.
doneWhen.es: Every ledger has four labeled columns.

watchFor.en: Students who skip the running total. Without it the next step doesn't work.
watchFor.es: Students who skip the running total. Without it the next step doesn't work.

description.en: Students set up a personal ledger on plain paper, in pencil: Date | Amount Found | Running Total | How Found. Teacher explains: "Ellis kept records. That's how he knew you're not going to believe this — we have $4.73!"
description.es: Students set up a personal ledger on plain paper, in pencil: Date | Amount Found | Running Total | How Found. Teacher explains: "Ellis kept records. That's how he knew you're not going to believe this — we have $4.73!"

description.en: Students set up a coin ledger on plain paper with two columns: Coins I Found | Where. Teacher explains: "Ellis wrote everything down. That's how he knew how much money they had!"
description.es: Students set up a coin ledger on plain paper with two columns: Coins I Found | Where. Teacher explains: "Ellis wrote everything down. That's how he knew how much money they had!"

sayThis.en: "Two columns. Coins I found. Where I found it. Ellis wrote everything down — that's how he knew how much money they had."
sayThis.es: "Two columns. Coins I found. Where I found it. Ellis wrote everything down — that's how he knew how much money they had."

watchFor.en: Columns too narrow to draw coins in. Show a ledger on the board with wide columns.
watchFor.es: Columns too narrow to draw coins in. Show a ledger on the board with wide columns.

doneWhen.en: Every ledger has two labeled columns.
doneWhen.es: Every ledger has two labeled columns.

sayThis.en: "Thirty coins are hidden in this room. When you find one, write it down before you go looking for the next one. If it isn't in your ledger, it doesn't count."
sayThis.es: "Thirty coins are hidden in this room. When you find one, write it down before you go looking for the next one. If it isn't in your ledger, it doesn't count."

doneWhen.en: All thirty coins are found and every one is written in somebody's ledger.
doneWhen.es: All thirty coins are found and every one is written in somebody's ledger.

watchFor.en: Pocketing coins and recording later. Say the rule again mid-round. Also the student who finds nothing — steer them toward an untouched corner.
watchFor.es: Pocketing coins and recording later. Say the rule again mid-round. Also the student who finds nothing — steer them toward an untouched corner.

description.en: Teacher has hidden 30 paper coins around the classroom in advance. Students hunt for them. Every coin found gets recorded in the ledger immediately: where found, denomination, running total updated.
description.es: Teacher has hidden 30 paper coins around the classroom in advance. Students hunt for them. Every coin found gets recorded in the ledger immediately: where found, denomination, running total updated.

description.en: Teacher has hidden 30 paper coins around the classroom in advance. Students hunt for them. Every coin found gets drawn in the ledger right away, with where it was found. The class counts the total together in the next step.
description.es: Teacher has hidden 30 paper coins around the classroom in advance. Students hunt for them. Every coin found gets drawn in the ledger right away, with where it was found. The class counts the total together in the next step.

sayThis.en: "Thirty paper coins are hidden in this room. When you find one, draw it in your ledger before you look for the next one. If it isn't in your ledger, it doesn't count."
sayThis.es: "Thirty paper coins are hidden in this room. When you find one, draw it in your ledger before you look for the next one. If it isn't in your ledger, it doesn't count."

watchFor.en: Pocketing coins and drawing them later. Say the rule again mid-round. Also the student who finds nothing — steer them toward an untouched corner.
watchFor.es: Pocketing coins and drawing them later. Say the rule again mid-round. Also the student who finds nothing — steer them toward an untouched corner.

doneWhen.en: All thirty coins are found and every one is drawn in somebody's ledger.
doneWhen.es: All thirty coins are found and every one is drawn in somebody's ledger.

sayThis.en: "Pool everything. Sort by type. Count each pile. One person writes the totals. Then we check it — because a total nobody checked is just a guess."
sayThis.es: "Pool everything. Sort by type. Count each pile. One person writes the totals. Then we check it — because a total nobody checked is just a guess."

doneWhen.en: One agreed grand total is written on the board.
doneWhen.es: One agreed grand total is written on the board.

watchFor.en: Two different totals. Good. Make them find the error rather than telling them.
watchFor.es: Two different totals. Good. Make them find the error rather than telling them.

description.en: Class pools all found coins. Pairs sort by denomination and count. One recorder writes the totals on the board. Class verifies the grand total.
description.es: Class pools all found coins. Pairs sort by denomination and count. One recorder writes the totals on the board. Class verifies the grand total.

description.en: Class pools all found coins. Pairs sort them into four piles: pennies, nickels, dimes, quarters. They count how many coins are in each pile. The teacher writes each count on the board and counts the money total out loud with the class.
description.es: Class pools all found coins. Pairs sort them into four piles: pennies, nickels, dimes, quarters. They count how many coins are in each pile. The teacher writes each count on the board and counts the money total out loud with the class.

sayThis.en: "Put all the coins together. Make four piles. Count how many coins are in each pile. I'll write your numbers on the board, and we'll count the money together."
sayThis.es: "Put all the coins together. Make four piles. Count how many coins are in each pile. I'll write your numbers on the board, and we'll count the money together."

watchFor.en: Two different counts for the same pile. Good. Count that pile again together, touching each coin.
watchFor.es: Two different counts for the same pile. Good. Count that pile again together, touching each coin.

doneWhen.en: Every pile count is on the board and the class has counted the total with you.
doneWhen.es: Every pile count is on the board and the class has counted the total with you.

sayThis.en: "Three proposals. Split it equally. Save it four more weeks. Spend it on something everyone gets. Thirty seconds each. Then we vote."
sayThis.es: "Three proposals. Split it equally. Save it four more weeks. Spend it on something everyone gets. Thirty seconds each. Then we vote."

doneWhen.en: All three proposals have been heard and every ballot is in.
doneWhen.es: All three proposals have been heard and every ballot is in.

watchFor.en: Proposals with no detail. Split it how? Save it for what? Make them finish the sentence.
watchFor.es: Proposals with no detail. Split it how? Save it for what? Make them finish the sentence.

description.en: Teacher facilitates a formal "financial meeting" — three students make proposals (assign roles in advance or take volunteers): - "I move that we split the money equally." (Propose how.) - "I move that we save it for 4 more weeks and then decide." (Propose what goal.) - "I move that we spend it on something the whole class can enjoy." (Name what.) Class discusses pros and cons. Vote by written ballot on scrap paper (secret vote adds engagement).
description.es: Teacher facilitates a formal "financial meeting" — three students make proposals (assign roles in advance or take volunteers): - "I move that we split the money equally." (Propose how.) - "I move that we save it for 4 more weeks and then decide." (Propose what goal.) - "I move that we spend it on something the whole class can enjoy." (Name what.) Class discusses pros and cons. Vote by written ballot on scrap paper (secret vote adds engagement).

description.en: The teacher runs a class meeting with three ideas from the story: share the money, save it for later, or buy one thing the whole class can enjoy. Three students each say one idea and one reason. Students vote by drawing their choice on a scrap of paper.
description.es: The teacher runs a class meeting with three ideas from the story: share the money, save it for later, or buy one thing the whole class can enjoy. Three students each say one idea and one reason. Students vote by drawing their choice on a scrap of paper.

sayThis.en: "Three ideas. Share it. Save it. Buy one thing for the whole class. Listen to each one. Then draw your vote on your scrap of paper."
sayThis.es: "Three ideas. Share it. Save it. Buy one thing for the whole class. Listen to each one. Then draw your vote on your scrap of paper."

watchFor.en: Kids voting for what a friend picks. Ask each one to tell you one reason.
watchFor.es: Kids voting for what a friend picks. Ask each one to tell you one reason.

doneWhen.en: All three ideas have been heard and every vote is in.
doneWhen.es: All three ideas have been heard and every vote is in.

sayThis.en: "The winning plan gets a budget. Here's the exact total. Spend it down on paper — item, cost, what's left. You can't go over, and you can't leave more than a dollar sitting there."
sayThis.es: "The winning plan gets a budget. Here's the exact total. Spend it down on paper — item, cost, what's left. You can't go over, and you can't leave more than a dollar sitting there."

doneWhen.en: Two teams have read a complete budget out loud.
doneWhen.es: Two teams have read a complete budget out loud.

watchFor.en: Rounded numbers that don't add up. Make them show the running balance line by line.
watchFor.es: Rounded numbers that don't add up. Make them show the running balance line by line.

description.en: The winning proposal now gets a budget. Teams take the exact total the class counted and plan how to spend it down to the last cent on a scrap-paper budget sheet — item, cost, running balance. They may not go over and they may not leave more than a dollar unspent. Two teams read their budgets out. Ask which plan the class would actually vote for now that the money has real things attached to it.
description.es: The winning proposal now gets a budget. Teams take the exact total the class counted and plan how to spend it down to the last cent on a scrap-paper budget sheet — item, cost, running balance. They may not go over and they may not leave more than a dollar unspent. Two teams read their budgets out. Ask which plan the class would actually vote for now that the money has real things attached to it.

description.en: The winning idea gets a plan. Teams draw two or three things to buy on a scrap of paper, each with a whole-dollar price from $1 to $4. The teacher shows on the board how much money is left as each team picks. Two teams share their plans.
description.es: The winning idea gets a plan. Teams draw two or three things to buy on a scrap of paper, each with a whole-dollar price from $1 to $4. The teacher shows on the board how much money is left as each team picks. Two teams share their plans.

sayThis.en: "Draw two or three things to buy. Give each one a price: 1, 2, 3 or 4 dollars. I'll show on the board how much money is left."
sayThis.es: "Draw two or three things to buy. Give each one a price: 1, 2, 3 or 4 dollars. I'll show on the board how much money is left."

watchFor.en: Teams picking more than the money covers. Count what is left on the board together before they add one more thing.
watchFor.es: Teams picking more than the money covers. Count what is left on the board together before they add one more thing.

doneWhen.en: Two teams have shared a plan out loud.
doneWhen.es: Two teams have shared a plan out loud.

sayThis.en: "I'm writing the decision in the class ledger on the board. Now — did the vote surprise you? What changed people's minds once real things had prices on them?"
sayThis.es: "I'm writing the decision in the class ledger on the board. Now — did the vote surprise you? What changed people's minds once real things had prices on them?"

doneWhen.en: The decision is written in the class ledger on the board and two students have said what changed their thinking.
doneWhen.es: The decision is written in the class ledger on the board and two students have said what changed their thinking.

watchFor.en: Sore losers. Name it: the vote was close, and the other plan wasn't stupid.
watchFor.es: Sore losers. Name it: the vote was close, and the other plan wasn't stupid.

description.en: Record the winning decision in the class savings ledger on the board, under the grand total. Ask: "Did the vote surprise you? What changed people's minds?"
description.es: Record the winning decision in the class savings ledger on the board, under the grand total. Ask: "Did the vote surprise you? What changed people's minds?"

discussionQuestions: Ellis said 'we need to record this.' Why does writing down what you have matter?
What would have happened if the friends spent their first $1 before they found the rest?
Mr. Mason saved for a whole year. What does that take? What gets in the way?
You voted to ___. Does everyone feel good about the decision? What did you give up?
How is a savings jar different from a savings account? What's the same?
extensionIdeas: Run the class savings simulation for a real week — each day a student "deposits" a token (a real penny or a paper one) and the class tracks the running total
Research: what is a savings account? What is interest? How does a bank use your money while it's saving?
Calculate: if you save $4.73 per week for 52 weeks, what do you have? What could you buy?

beforeClass.en: Cut thirty paper coins from plain paper with scissors and write 1¢, 5¢, 10¢ or 25¢ on each. Hide them before students arrive and write down where, or you'll lose some for good. Set out plain paper and pencils for ledgers and scrap paper for ballots. Save a corner of the board for the class savings ledger. Decide whether the vote is secret ballot or hands — secret works better.
beforeClass.es: Cut thirty paper coins from plain paper with scissors and write 1¢, 5¢, 10¢ or 25¢ on each. Hide them before students arrive and write down where, or you'll lose some for good. Set out plain paper and pencils for ledgers and scrap paper for ballots. Save a corner of the board for the class savings ledger. Decide whether the vote is secret ballot or hands — secret works better.

runningLongOrShort.en: Long: cut the coin hunt to six minutes; the counting and the meeting matter more. Short: run a second hunt with fewer coins and a time limit.
runningLongOrShort.es: Long: cut the coin hunt to six minutes; the counting and the meeting matter more. Short: run a second hunt with fewer coins and a time limit.

Set out plain paper and pencils for ledgers and scrap paper for ballots. Save a corner of the board for the class savings ledger. Decide whether the vote is secret ballot or hands — secret works better.

focus: Add a coin to the jar each day
Count the coins with the class
Hunt for paper coins and draw each one you find
Words: save, coin, count, more
Record the daily total on a chart
Add up all seven days and check with a partner
Vote on splitting, saving, or spending the money
Vocabulary: savings, daily, total, goal
Keep a ledger with a running total as you find coins
Sort and count the class coins to one grand total
Explain why one of the three money choices is best

Plan a budget that spends the exact class total
Weigh the three proposals and vote by ballot
Defend a savings strategy with your data
Vocabulary: proposal, ballot, budget, balance

ell.label: English Language Learners
strategies: Post a coin chart with a picture, the name and the value of each coin.
Count out loud together, pointing to each coin as you say the number.
Give the frames "I found ___ cents." and "I want to ___ because ___."

learningDifferences.label: Students with Learning Differences
strategies: Use large paper coins with the value written big on each one.
Give a tracker or ledger with the rows and columns already drawn.
Keep a coin value card on the desk the whole time.

advanced.label: Advanced Students
strategies: Work out what $4.73 a week adds up to after a month and after a year.
Write a coin story problem for a partner to solve.
Find two different sets of coins that make the same total.

description.en: Teams receive identical sets of limited classroom materials and a challenge: build the tallest freestanding structure in a set time. Crucially, teams must draw a blueprint BEFORE building. The planning phase is non-negotiable. After building, they assess: what from the plan worked? What did they find around the room (or in the rules) that helped?
description.es: Teams receive identical sets of limited classroom materials and a challenge: build the tallest freestanding structure in a set time. Crucially, teams must draw a blueprint BEFORE building. The planning phase is non-negotiable. After building, they assess: what from the plan worked? What did they find around the room (or in the rules) that helped?
