fromScratch.costPerStudent: $0 — everything is free or from home
fromScratch.description: Each student draws a plan on one sheet of plain paper in pencil, then builds a tower from two more sheets and one strip of masking tape. The teacher measures in hand-widths.
items: Plain paper — 60 sheets, 3 per student: 1 for the plan, 2 for the tower (Tier 1: 40 sheets, 1 plan each plus 2 per pair)
Masking tape — 20 strips, torn ahead, 1 per student (Tier 1: 10 strips, 1 per pair)
Pencils — 20, one per student for the plan

basicClassroom.costPerStudent: $0 — uses supplies the school already has
basicClassroom.description: Each student draws a plan on one sheet of plain paper in pencil, then builds a tower from two more sheets and one strip of masking tape. The teacher measures with a ruler.
items: Plain paper — 60 sheets, 3 per student: 1 for the plan, 2 for the tower (Tier 1: 40 sheets, 1 plan each plus 2 per pair)
Masking tape — 20 strips, pre-cut, 1 per student (Tier 1: 10 strips, 1 per pair)
Pencils — 20, one per student for the plan

description.en: Students draw a plan for their tower on one sheet of paper BEFORE touching the other materials. "What shape? How tall? How does it stand up?" Teacher models drawing a quick layered-tower plan.
description.es: Students draw a plan for their tower on one sheet of paper BEFORE touching the other materials. "What shape? How tall? How does it stand up?" Teacher models drawing a quick layered-tower plan.

sayThis.en: "Draw your tower first. Don't touch the other paper yet. What shape is it? How tall? How will it stand up?"
sayThis.es: "Draw your tower first. Don't touch the other paper yet. What shape is it? How tall? How will it stand up?"

watchFor.en: Students folding the building paper while they draw. Move the two blank sheets to the corner of the desk until the plan is done.
watchFor.es: Students folding the building paper while they draw. Move the two blank sheets to the corner of the desk until the plan is done.

doneWhen.en: Every student has a drawing on one sheet and two blank sheets still flat.
doneWhen.es: Every student has a drawing on one sheet and two blank sheets still flat.

description.en: Students draw their tower on one sheet before touching the other paper. One question only: how tall is it? Skip the shape and how it stands up.
description.es: Students draw their tower on one sheet before touching the other paper. One question only: how tall is it? Skip the shape and how it stands up.

sayThis.en: "Draw your tower first. Hands off the other paper. How tall is your tower going to be?"
sayThis.es: "Draw your tower first. Hands off the other paper. How tall is your tower going to be?"

description.en: Using only the remaining 2 sheets of paper and 1 strip of tape, build the tallest freestanding structure possible. No scissors. Structure must stand on its own for 10 seconds.
description.es: Using only the remaining 2 sheets of paper and 1 strip of tape, build the tallest freestanding structure possible. No scissors. Structure must stand on its own for 10 seconds.

sayThis.en: "Now build. Two sheets and one piece of tape. No scissors. It has to stand up by itself while I count to ten."
sayThis.es: "Now build. Two sheets and one piece of tape. No scissors. It has to stand up by itself while I count to ten."

watchFor.en: Flat sheets that flop over. Show once how rolling or folding a sheet makes it stiff.
watchFor.es: Flat sheets that flop over. Show once how rolling or folding a sheet makes it stiff.

doneWhen.en: Every student has a tower standing, or has tried and is ready to measure.
doneWhen.es: Every student has a tower standing, or has tried and is ready to measure.

description.en: Students build in pairs, not alone. Two sheets and one strip of tape for each pair. No scissors. The tower has to stand by itself while the teacher counts to ten.
description.es: Students build in pairs, not alone. Two sheets and one strip of tape for each pair. No scissors. The tower has to stand by itself while the teacher counts to ten.

sayThis.en: "Build with your partner. Two sheets and one piece of tape. No scissors. It has to stand up by itself while I count to ten."
sayThis.es: "Build with your partner. Two sheets and one piece of tape. No scissors. It has to stand up by itself while I count to ten."

watchFor.en: One partner building while the other watches. Give each child one sheet so both have to help.
watchFor.es: One partner building while the other watches. Give each child one sheet so both have to help.

doneWhen.en: Every pair has a tower standing on the desk, or a fallen one they are holding up to show you.
doneWhen.es: Every pair has a tower standing on the desk, or a fallen one they are holding up to show you.

description.en: Teacher measures each structure with a ruler or hand-widths. Tallest wins. Show blueprints: "Did your plan match what you built?"
description.es: Teacher measures each structure with a ruler or hand-widths. Tallest wins. Show blueprints: "Did your plan match what you built?"

sayThis.en: "Hands off. I'll measure. Now hold up your plan. Does your tower look like your drawing?"
sayThis.es: "Hands off. I'll measure. Now hold up your plan. Does your tower look like your drawing?"

watchFor.en: Students whose tower fell feeling they lost. Ask what they would change on their plan.
watchFor.es: Students whose tower fell feeling they lost. Ask what they would change on their plan.

doneWhen.en: Every tower is measured and the tallest one is named.
doneWhen.es: Every tower is measured and the tallest one is named.

description.en: Teacher measures each structure in hand-widths. Tallest wins. Show blueprints: "Did your plan match what you built?"
description.es: Teacher measures each structure in hand-widths. Tallest wins. Show blueprints: "Did your plan match what you built?"

description.en: Teacher measures each tower in hand-widths, counting out loud, not with a ruler. Then each pair holds its drawing up next to its tower and looks. Skip the writing and the ranking talk.
description.es: Teacher measures each tower in hand-widths, counting out loud, not with a ruler. Then each pair holds its drawing up next to its tower and looks. Skip the writing and the ranking talk.

sayThis.en: "Hands off. I will measure with my hand. One, two, three. Now hold your drawing up next to your tower. Do they look the same?"
sayThis.es: "Hands off. I will measure with my hand. One, two, three. Now hold your drawing up next to your tower. Do they look the same?"

watchFor.en: Children upset that their tower fell over. Say, "Builders try again," and let them stand it back up.
watchFor.es: Children upset that their tower fell over. Say, "Builders try again," and let them stand it back up.

discussionQuestions: Did your blueprint help you build faster or slower?
Mr. Mason said 'before you build, you need a plan.' Were the friends glad he said that?
What would you do differently if you had one more piece of paper?

beforeClass.en: Give each student 3 sheets of plain paper, 1 pre-cut strip of masking tape and a pencil. Keep a ruler handy. Clear a flat spot where towers can stand on their own.
beforeClass.es: Give each student 3 sheets of plain paper, 1 pre-cut strip of masking tape and a pencil. Keep a ruler handy. Clear a flat spot where towers can stand on their own.

runningLongOrShort.en: Long: skip showing blueprints in Measure & Share and just measure. Short: after measuring, let anyone whose tower fell rebuild it with the same paper and measure again.
runningLongOrShort.es: Long: skip showing blueprints in Measure & Share and just measure. Short: after measuring, let anyone whose tower fell rebuild it with the same paper and measure again.

beforeClass.en: Give each student 3 sheets of plain paper, 1 strip of masking tape torn ahead and a pencil. Plan to measure in hand-widths. Clear a flat spot where towers can stand on their own.
beforeClass.es: Give each student 3 sheets of plain paper, 1 strip of masking tape torn ahead and a pencil. Plan to measure in hand-widths. Clear a flat spot where towers can stand on their own.

sayThis.es: "Listen to each one. Two prices. Circle the one that is smaller. Don't call it out."

watchFor.en: Students circling the one they like to eat. Hold up fingers for each price and ask which is less.
watchFor.es: Students circling the one they like to eat. Hold up fingers for each price and ask which is less.

doneWhen.en: Every student has circled an answer in all three parts.
doneWhen.es: Every student has circled an answer in all three parts.

description.en: Go through answers. Discuss: "Was homemade always cheaper? Why might someone still buy from the store?"
description.es: Go through answers. Discuss: "Was homemade always cheaper? Why might someone still buy from the store?"

sayThis.en: "Hands up if you circled homemade. Now store. Was homemade cheaper every time? Why might someone still buy it at the store?"
sayThis.es: "Hands up if you circled homemade. Now store. Was homemade cheaper every time? Why might someone still buy it at the store?"

watchFor.en: Answers only about price. Ask what making it at home takes — time, dishes, knowing how.
watchFor.es: Answers only about price. Ask what making it at home takes — time, dishes, knowing how.

doneWhen.en: At least two reasons to buy from the store have been said out loud.
doneWhen.es: At least two reasons to buy from the store have been said out loud.

description.en: Hands up for who circled homemade, then say the answer out loud. Ask one question: why would somebody buy cookies at the store? Take two answers and stop.
description.es: Hands up for who circled homemade, then say the answer out loud. Ask one question: why would somebody buy cookies at the store? Take two answers and stop.

sayThis.en: "Hands up if you circled homemade. Two dollars is less than four, so homemade costs less. Why would somebody still buy cookies at the store?"
sayThis.es: "Hands up if you circled homemade. Two dollars is less than four, so homemade costs less. Why would somebody still buy cookies at the store?"

watchFor.en: Nobody has an idea. Say, "Making cookies takes a long time," then ask for one more reason.
watchFor.es: Nobody has an idea. Say, "Making cookies takes a long time," then ask for one more reason.

doneWhen.en: Hands have gone up and two children have said a reason out loud.
doneWhen.es: Hands have gone up and two children have said a reason out loud.

discussionQuestions: Frances's vegetables came from her garden — that made the bread cost less. What if you grew your own food?
"Even if homemade is cheaper, what does it cost that we didn't count?" (Time, effort)
Benny said this bread was better than store-bought AND cheaper. Do you think that's always true?

beforeClass.en: Have the three scenarios ready to read, with the prices written on the board. Each student folds a sheet of plain paper into three parts and writes "homemade" and "store" in each part with a pencil.
beforeClass.es: Have the three scenarios ready to read, with the prices written on the board. Each student folds a sheet of plain paper into three parts and writes "homemade" and "store" in each part with a pencil.

runningLongOrShort.en: Long: read two scenarios instead of three and go straight to Reveal & Discussion. Short: in Reveal & Discussion, have students make up one more homemade-or-store question for the class.
runningLongOrShort.es: Long: read two scenarios instead of three and go straight to Reveal & Discussion. Short: in Reveal & Discussion, have students make up one more homemade-or-store question for the class.

basicClassroom.description: Each student works the recipe math on a sheet of plain paper in pencil. The teacher writes the recipe prices on the board. Nothing is bought, cooked or eaten.
items: Plain paper — 20 sheets, one per student for the worksheet
Pencils — 20, one per student for the math

description.en: Display the trail mix recipe. "Today you're Frances — figure out if homemade is worth it. First, estimate: do you think homemade trail mix costs MORE or LESS than $1.50 per serving?"
description.es: Display the trail mix recipe. "Today you're Frances — figure out if homemade is worth it. First, estimate: do you think homemade trail mix costs MORE or LESS than $1.50 per serving?"

sayThis.en: "Today you're Frances. Here's a trail mix recipe. At the store, one serving costs a dollar fifty. Guess: does homemade cost more or less? Write your guess."
sayThis.es: "Today you're Frances. Here's a trail mix recipe. At the store, one serving costs a dollar fifty. Guess: does homemade cost more or less? Write your guess."

watchFor.en: Students trying to add it all up now. Tell them it's only a guess; the math comes next.
watchFor.es: Students trying to add it all up now. Tell them it's only a guess; the math comes next.

doneWhen.en: Every student has written "more" or "less" on their sheet.
doneWhen.es: Every student has written "more" or "less" on their sheet.

description.en: Students fill in worksheet: write each ingredient, its cost, add them up for total batch cost.
description.es: Students fill in worksheet: write each ingredient, its cost, add them up for total batch cost.

sayThis.en: "Write each ingredient and its cost, one on each line. Then add them all up. That's what the whole batch costs."
sayThis.es: "Write each ingredient and its cost, one on each line. Then add them all up. That's what the whole batch costs."

watchFor.en: Adding 40 cents and 30 cents and getting 70 dollars. Have them line up the decimal points before adding.
watchFor.es: Adding 40 cents and 30 cents and getting 70 dollars. Have them line up the decimal points before adding.

doneWhen.en: Every sheet shows a batch total of $1.10.
doneWhen.es: Every sheet shows a batch total of $1.10.

description.en: Students copy the four ingredients from the board with a pencil. They count the ingredients, then circle the one that costs the most.
description.es: Students copy the four ingredients from the board with a pencil. They count the ingredients, then circle the one that costs the most.

sayThis.en: "Copy the four ingredients. How many are there? Now circle the one that costs the most."
sayThis.es: "Copy the four ingredients. How many are there? Now circle the one that costs the most."

watchFor.en: Kids picking the longest name as the priciest. Point at the prices and compare the numbers.
watchFor.es: Kids picking the longest name as the priciest. Point at the prices and compare the numbers.

doneWhen.en: Every sheet has four ingredients and the most expensive one circled.
doneWhen.es: Every sheet has four ingredients and the most expensive one circled.

description.en: "Our batch makes 4 servings. How much does each serving cost?" ($1.10 ÷ 4 = $0.275 ≈ $0.28 per serving.)
description.es: "Our batch makes 4 servings. How much does each serving cost?" ($1.10 ÷ 4 = $0.275 ≈ $0.28 per serving.)

sayThis.en: "The batch makes four servings. Split $1.10 into four equal parts. How much is one part?"
sayThis.es: "The batch makes four servings. Split $1.10 into four equal parts. How much is one part?"

watchFor.en: Students stuck at $0.275. Show them to round to the nearest cent: about 28 cents.
watchFor.es: Students stuck at $0.275. Show them to round to the nearest cent: about 28 cents.

doneWhen.en: Every sheet shows about $0.28 per serving.
doneWhen.es: Every sheet shows about $0.28 per serving.

description.en: Tell the class that one serving costs about 28 cents. Students write 28¢ on their sheet. Ask: is that more or less than a dollar?
description.es: Tell the class that one serving costs about 28 cents. Students write 28¢ on their sheet. Ask: is that more or less than a dollar?

sayThis.en: "One serving costs about 28 cents. Write 28 cents. Is that more or less than one dollar?"
sayThis.es: "One serving costs about 28 cents. Write 28 cents. Is that more or less than one dollar?"

watchFor.en: Kids who think 28 is more than 1. Say, "100 cents make one dollar, and 28 is less than 100."
watchFor.es: Kids who think 28 is more than 1. Say, "100 cents make one dollar, and 28 is less than 100."

doneWhen.en: Every sheet shows 28¢ and the word "more" or "less".
doneWhen.es: Every sheet shows 28¢ and the word "more" or "less".

description.en: Write: Homemade = $0.28/serving. Store-bought = $1.50/serving. "How much do you save per serving?" ($1.22) "If your family makes this once a week, how much do you save in a year?"
description.es: Write: Homemade = $0.28/serving. Store-bought = $1.50/serving. "How much do you save per serving?" ($1.22) "If your family makes this once a week, how much do you save in a year?"

sayThis.en: "Homemade is 28 cents. The store is a dollar fifty. How much do you save on one serving? Now — if your family makes it every week, how much is that in a year?"
sayThis.es: "Homemade is 28 cents. The store is a dollar fifty. How much do you save on one serving? Now — if your family makes it every week, how much is that in a year?"

watchFor.en: Students who don't know how many weeks are in a year. Write 52 on the board.
watchFor.es: Students who don't know how many weeks are in a year. Write 52 on the board.

doneWhen.en: Every sheet shows $1.22 saved per serving.
doneWhen.es: Every sheet shows $1.22 saved per serving.

description.en: Write on the board: Homemade = 28¢. Store = $1.50. Ask which costs less. Skip the yearly savings.
description.es: Write on the board: Homemade = 28¢. Store = $1.50. Ask which costs less. Skip the yearly savings.

sayThis.en: "Homemade is 28 cents. The store is a dollar fifty. Which one costs less?"
sayThis.es: "Homemade is 28 cents. The store is a dollar fifty. Which one costs less?"

watchFor.en: Kids picking the store because it has a dollar sign. Say, "A dollar fifty is 150 cents. Which is less, 28 or 150?"
watchFor.es: Kids picking the store because it has a dollar sign. Say, "A dollar fifty is 150 cents. Which is less, 28 or 150?"

doneWhen.en: Every student has circled the one that costs less.
doneWhen.es: Every student has circled the one that costs less.

description.en: "What does homemade cost that we didn't add up?" (Time, dishes, shopping for ingredients.)
description.es: "What does homemade cost that we didn't add up?" (Time, dishes, shopping for ingredients.)

sayThis.en: "Homemade saved money. What did it cost that we didn't add up?"
sayThis.es: "Homemade saved money. What did it cost that we didn't add up?"

watchFor.en: Silence. Ask who does the shopping and who washes the bowl.
watchFor.es: Silence. Ask who does the shopping and who washes the bowl.

doneWhen.en: Time and one other hidden cost have been named.
doneWhen.es: Time and one other hidden cost have been named.

discussionQuestions: Was your estimate right? Were you surprised by how much cheaper homemade is?
Riley asked Frances 'how much does this cost?' Why is that a smart question?
Is homemade always better? Can you think of when store-bought might actually be a better choice?
Frances's vegetables were free from the garden. What's something your family grows or gets for free that could lower a food cost?

beforeClass.en: Write the trail mix price list on the board: cereal $0.40, raisins $0.30, pretzels $0.25, chocolate chips $0.15. That is $1.10 for 4 servings. Store-bought is $1.50 a serving. Nothing is bought or eaten; the recipe is prices on paper. Give each student a sheet of plain paper and a pencil for the worksheet.
beforeClass.es: Write the trail mix price list on the board: cereal $0.40, raisins $0.30, pretzels $0.25, chocolate chips $0.15. That is $1.10 for 4 servings. Store-bought is $1.50 a serving. Nothing is bought or eaten; the recipe is prices on paper. Give each student a sheet of plain paper and a pencil for the worksheet.

runningLongOrShort.en: Long: in Compare, skip the yearly savings question. Short: in Tradeoff Discussion, ask what would happen to the cost per serving if the batch made 8 servings instead of 4.
runningLongOrShort.es: Long: in Compare, skip the yearly savings question. Short: in Tradeoff Discussion, ask what would happen to the cost per serving if the batch made 8 servings instead of 4.

fromScratch.costPerStudent: $0 — everything is free or from home

items: Plain paper — 20 sheets, one per student for the copied price list and recipe sheet

basicClassroom.costPerStudent: $0 — uses supplies the school already has
basicClassroom.description: Each student gets the price list, printed or copied onto plain paper, and designs a recipe on paper in pencil. The teacher writes the list and the target on the board. Nothing is bought, cooked or eaten.
items: Plain paper — 20 sheets, one per student for the price list and recipe sheet
Pencils — 20, one per student for the recipe and math
Board — teacher, for the price list and the target cost

sayThis.en: "These are close to real grocery prices. You're going to design a recipe on paper — something a kid could actually make — and work out whether it's a good deal. Nothing gets cooked today. Circle three things on the list you'd use."
sayThis.es: "These are close to real grocery prices. You're going to design a recipe on paper — something a kid could actually make — and work out whether it's a good deal. Nothing gets cooked today. Circle three things on the list you'd use."

doneWhen.en: Every student has the price list with three items circled.
doneWhen.es: Every student has the price list with three items circled.

watchFor.en: Students expecting to eat. Say it once, clearly, at the start.
watchFor.es: Students expecting to eat. Say it once, clearly, at the start.

description.en: Review price list together. "These are close to real grocery prices. You're going to design a simple recipe — something K-4 could actually make at home — and figure out whether it's a good deal."
description.es: Review price list together. "These are close to real grocery prices. You're going to design a simple recipe — something K-4 could actually make at home — and figure out whether it's a good deal."

sayThis.en: "Three to six ingredients, all off the list. It has to be real — something you'd actually eat. Write the amounts, not just the names."
sayThis.es: "Three to six ingredients, all off the list. It has to be real — something you'd actually eat. Write the amounts, not just the names."

doneWhen.en: Every recipe has between three and six ingredients with amounts.
doneWhen.es: Every recipe has between three and six ingredients with amounts.

watchFor.en: Recipes with one ingredient, or twenty. Hold the range.
watchFor.es: Recipes with one ingredient, or twenty. Hold the range.

description.en: Each student designs a simple recipe (3-6 ingredients from the list). Must be something real (a snack, simple breakfast, lunch item). List all ingredients and amounts.
description.es: Each student designs a simple recipe (3-6 ingredients from the list). Must be something real (a snack, simple breakfast, lunch item). List all ingredients and amounts.

sayThis.en: "Cost for each line, then add it up. Now the harder bit — how many servings does that actually make? Guess honestly."
sayThis.es: "Cost for each line, then add it up. Now the harder bit — how many servings does that actually make? Guess honestly."

doneWhen.en: Every sheet has a batch total and a serving count.
doneWhen.es: Every sheet has a batch total and a serving count.

watchFor.en: Pricing a whole package when the recipe uses a spoonful. Ask how much of it they actually used.
watchFor.es: Pricing a whole package when the recipe uses a spoonful. Ask how much of it they actually used.

description.en: Fill in cost for each ingredient, add for batch total. Estimate how many servings the recipe makes.
description.es: Fill in cost for each ingredient, add for batch total. Estimate how many servings the recipe makes.

description.en: Students write the price next to each ingredient. They count the ingredients and guess how many people the recipe feeds. The class adds up one recipe together, with the teacher at the board.
description.es: Students write the price next to each ingredient. They count the ingredients and guess how many people the recipe feeds. The class adds up one recipe together, with the teacher at the board.

sayThis.en: "Write the price next to each ingredient. Count them. How many people could your recipe feed? Now let's add up one recipe together."
sayThis.es: "Write the price next to each ingredient. Count them. How many people could your recipe feed? Now let's add up one recipe together."

watchFor.en: Kids trying to add many prices alone. Pick one student's recipe and add it on the board with the class.
watchFor.es: Kids trying to add many prices alone. Pick one student's recipe and add it on the board with the class.

doneWhen.en: Every sheet has a price on each line and a number of servings.
doneWhen.es: Every sheet has a price on each line and a number of servings.

sayThis.en: "Total divided by servings. Write it big. That's the number that matters."
sayThis.es: "Total divided by servings. Write it big. That's the number that matters."

doneWhen.en: Every student has a cost per serving written clearly.
doneWhen.es: Every student has a cost per serving written clearly.

watchFor.en: Division errors that make snacks cost eleven dollars. Get a partner to check anything that looks strange.
watchFor.es: Division errors that make snacks cost eleven dollars. Get a partner to check anything that looks strange.

description.en: Divide total cost by number of servings. Write it clearly.
description.es: Divide total cost by number of servings. Write it clearly.

description.en: Walk the room and help each student find what one serving costs. Use easy numbers: a $2 recipe that feeds 2 people costs $1 for each person. Students write the cost for one serving big on their sheet.
description.es: Walk the room and help each student find what one serving costs. Use easy numbers: a $2 recipe that feeds 2 people costs $1 for each person. Students write the cost for one serving big on their sheet.

sayThis.en: "Your recipe costs this much, and it feeds this many people. Let's find what one serving costs. Write it big."
sayThis.es: "Your recipe costs this much, and it feeds this many people. Let's find what one serving costs. Write it big."

watchFor.en: Kids writing the whole recipe cost as one serving. Ask, "Does one person eat the whole thing?"
watchFor.es: Kids writing the whole recipe cost as one serving. Ask, "Does one person eat the whole thing?"

doneWhen.en: Every student has a cost for one serving written big.
doneWhen.es: Every student has a cost for one serving written big.

sayThis.en: "What does the store version cost? Work out what you save per serving. Then times it by fifty-two."
sayThis.es: "What does the store version cost? Work out what you save per serving. Then times it by fifty-two."

doneWhen.en: Every sheet has a saving per serving and a yearly figure.
doneWhen.es: Every sheet has a saving per serving and a yearly figure.

watchFor.en: Wild store prices. Anchor them with two store prices from the list.
watchFor.es: Wild store prices. Anchor them with two store prices from the list.

description.en: What would the store equivalent cost? (Use the store prices on the price list, or students estimate.) Calculate the savings per serving. Calculate the annual savings if made weekly.
description.es: What would the store equivalent cost? (Use the store prices on the price list, or students estimate.) Calculate the savings per serving. Calculate the annual savings if made weekly.

description.en: Tell students what the store version costs, using a store price on the list. Students circle which costs less, homemade or store. Skip the yearly figure.
description.es: Tell students what the store version costs, using a store price on the list. Students circle which costs less, homemade or store. Skip the yearly figure.

sayThis.en: "The store version costs this much. Your homemade serving costs this much. Circle the one that costs less."
sayThis.es: "The store version costs this much. Your homemade serving costs this much. Circle the one that costs less."

watchFor.en: Kids circling homemade every time. Read the two numbers out loud and ask which is smaller.
watchFor.es: Kids circling homemade every time. Read the two numbers out loud and ask which is smaller.

doneWhen.en: Every sheet has homemade or store circled.
doneWhen.es: Every sheet has homemade or store circled.

sayThis.en: "New rule. Your recipe has to come in under the target now. Swap an ingredient, cut an amount, or stretch the servings. Redo the math. Your partner checks it."
sayThis.es: "New rule. Your recipe has to come in under the target now. Swap an ingredient, cut an amount, or stretch the servings. Redo the math. Your partner checks it."

doneWhen.en: Every student is under the target and a partner has initialed the new math.
doneWhen.es: Every student is under the target and a partner has initialed the new math.

watchFor.en: Stretching servings to twenty to hit the number. Ask whether that serving is still a real portion.
watchFor.es: Stretching servings to twenty to hit the number. Ask whether that serving is still a real portion.

description.en: Teacher names a target: your recipe now has to come in under a set cost per serving. Students redesign on paper — swap an ingredient, cut an amount, or stretch the servings — and recalculate. Nothing is cooked or brought in; this is all arithmetic on the price list. Partners check each other's new math. Ask what the recipe lost when it got cheaper, and whether it was worth the saving.
description.es: Teacher names a target: your recipe now has to come in under a set cost per serving. Students redesign on paper — swap an ingredient, cut an amount, or stretch the servings — and recalculate. Nothing is cooked or brought in; this is all arithmetic on the price list. Partners check each other's new math. Ask what the recipe lost when it got cheaper, and whether it was worth the saving.

description.en: Students find the most expensive ingredient in their recipe and swap it for a cheaper one on the price list. They say which recipe costs less now. Partners check the swap.
description.es: Students find the most expensive ingredient in their recipe and swap it for a cheaper one on the price list. They say which recipe costs less now. Partners check the swap.

sayThis.en: "Find your most expensive ingredient. Swap it for a cheaper one on the list. Does your recipe cost less now?"
sayThis.es: "Find your most expensive ingredient. Swap it for a cheaper one on the list. Does your recipe cost less now?"

watchFor.en: Swapping for something that costs more. Put the two prices side by side and ask which is smaller.
watchFor.es: Swapping for something that costs more. Put the two prices side by side and ask which is smaller.

doneWhen.en: Every student has swapped one ingredient and said which recipe costs less.
doneWhen.es: Every student has swapped one ingredient and said which recipe costs less.

sayThis.en: "One sentence. Mine costs this per serving, the store costs that, I save this, and in a year that's this. Then tell us what your recipe lost when it got cheaper."
sayThis.es: "One sentence. Mine costs this per serving, the store costs that, I save this, and in a year that's this. Then tell us what your recipe lost when it got cheaper."

doneWhen.en: Every student has presented and their trade-off is written on their sheet.
doneWhen.es: Every student has presented and their trade-off is written on their sheet.

watchFor.en: Presentations that skip the last part. That's the interesting half.
watchFor.es: Presentations that skip the last part. That's the interesting half.

description.en: Each student (or pair) presents their recipe in one sentence: "My [recipe] costs $[X] per serving. The store version costs $[Y]. I save $[Z] per serving. In a year, that's $[A]."
description.es: Each student (or pair) presents their recipe in one sentence: "My [recipe] costs $[X] per serving. The store version costs $[Y]. I save $[Z] per serving. In a year, that's $[A]."

description.en: Each student presents in one sentence: "My [recipe] costs [X] for one serving. The store costs [Y]. Homemade costs less (or more)." Then they say what they swapped to make it cheaper.
description.es: Each student presents in one sentence: "My [recipe] costs [X] for one serving. The store costs [Y]. Homemade costs less (or more)." Then they say what they swapped to make it cheaper.

sayThis.en: "One sentence. My recipe costs this. The store costs that. Which one costs less? Then tell us what you swapped."
sayThis.es: "One sentence. My recipe costs this. The store costs that. Which one costs less? Then tell us what you swapped."

watchFor.en: Kids who forget the store price. Point to it on the price list.
watchFor.es: Kids who forget the store price. Point to it on the price list.

doneWhen.en: Every student has presented and said which costs less.
doneWhen.es: Every student has presented and said which costs less.

discussionQuestions: Did any recipe surprise you — either cheaper or more expensive than you expected?
Frances used vegetables from her garden (free). If you grew one ingredient, how does that change your math?
Benny said the bread was better than store-bought. Is 'better' part of the math? (Satisfaction has value too.)
What's the tradeoff for the recipe you made cheaper in the cut-the-cost round? Is it always worth it?
What's one thing your family makes at home that saves money? Do you know how much it saves?
extensionIdeas: Grocery store field trip or virtual grocery tour: find the cheapest version of 5 items on the price list
Create a "Class Cookbook" of the cheapest recipes designed in this activity
Research: what percentage of American food spending is on restaurants vs. groceries? What's the math behind eating at home?

Compare homemade vs. store cost and find the gap
Explain why homemade can cost less
Vocabulary: per serving, savings, value, estimate
Compute cost per serving and total savings
Analyze when homemade is worth the time
Argue a buy-or-make decision with your numbers
Vocabulary: unit cost, opportunity cost, trade-off, margin

ell.label: English Language Learners
strategies: Draw a small picture next to each item on the price list or recipe, like a raisin next to raisins.
Give a sentence frame for the last step: "Homemade costs $___. The store costs $___. I save $___."
Pair with a partner who reads the prices out loud.

learningDifferences.label: Students with Learning Differences
strategies: Give a sheet with the ingredient and cost columns already drawn so students only fill in numbers.
Let a partner check each division before moving on, so one slip doesn't carry through the whole sheet.
In the 45-minute version, hold the recipe to three ingredients.

advanced.label: Advanced Students
strategies: Double the batch and check whether the cost per serving changes.
Add the cost of their own time and decide whether homemade still wins.
Find two prices for one ingredient and redo the math with the cheaper one.

description.en: Each student receives a "broken" item (a deliberately torn, crumpled, or damaged paper object) and a small set of repair tools (tape, glue stick, scissors, scrap paper). They diagnose the problem, decide on a repair approach, fix it, and then calculate: what would it cost to replace this vs. repair it? The activity builds both hands-on competence and a repair-vs-replace decision-making habit.

In your repair report, what was the biggest savings — the item where fixing cost least vs. replacement cost most?
What skills did you use today? What if you could use those skills every time something breaks at home?
Mr. Mason said his grandfather's chair was still standing after decades of repairs. What's the 'chair' equivalent in your home — something old that's been fixed many times?
Is there an environmental argument for fixing vs. throwing away? What happens to things that get thrown away?
extensionIdeas: Start a class "Fix-It Log" — students record one thing they notice each week that could be fixed instead of replaced
Research the "Right to Repair" movement — why do some companies make things hard to fix?
Bring in a real small broken item (with parent permission) and brainstorm the repair approach as a class

ell.label: English Language Learners
strategies: Hold up a broken item and act out each word: torn, wrinkled, cut, bent.
Let students draw the problem on the back of the item instead of writing it.
Give a frame for the chart or report: "I fixed the ___ with ___."

learningDifferences.label: Students with Learning Differences
strategies: Fix two items well instead of four, and chart only those two.
Pre-cut tape strips and paper patches so the repair is not all scissors work.
Let a partner hold the item flat while the student tapes it.

advanced.label: Advanced Students
strategies: Fix one item two different ways and decide which repair is stronger.
Find the total saved across all four items and explain which repair mattered most.
Write a three-step repair guide for the hardest item that a classmate could follow.

description.en: Each team picks the one resource on the map they think is most underused and gets ninety seconds on the timer to sell it to the class — what it is, who it is for, what it saves you. The class scores each pitch by show of hands on one question only: would you actually go? Tally the scores on the board. Ask what made the winning pitch work, and why good things stay unused when nobody talks about them.

watchFor.en: Five days of the same thing. Push for variety across the categories.

description.en: As a class, design a hypothetical "Week of Free Activities" using only resources on the map. What would you do Monday through Friday that costs $0? Present one family's week.
description.es: As a class, design a hypothetical "Week of Free Activities" using only resources on the map. What would you do Monday through Friday that costs $0? Present one family's week.

discussionQuestions: The library uses tax money. You and your family already paid for it — are you getting your money's worth?
Ellis said 'how can everything be free?' Is it actually free, or is the cost hidden? Who pays and how?
What's the most valuable free resource in our neighborhood that most people don't use?
Could you live an entire month using only free community resources for entertainment and learning? What would you miss?
Mr. Mason says 'the best things in life are free.' Is that true? What's the limit of that idea?
extensionIdeas: Visit the local library and get library cards for anyone who doesn't have one
Assign: "Resource Hunt" — find one free or borrowable resource at home you've never used and report back
Research: what's in the "Library of Things" at your nearest library? (Many lend tools, instruments, games, even seeds!)

Mark them on a community map
Decide one need you can meet without money

Categorize resources and map them with a key
Build a borrow-vs-buy comparison

Propose how to share resources more widely

ell.label: English Language Learners
strategies: Draw a small picture next to each category or sorting word, like a book for Learn and a ball for Play.
Let students draw the resource on their card and label it with one word.
Give a sentence frame: "___ is free. It helps ___."

learningDifferences.label: Students with Learning Differences
strategies: Write the questions on the card ahead — who can use it, what you get, what it costs — so students fill in answers only.
Let a student say their resource to a partner who writes it down.
Give one clear job at the map, like drawing the symbols, instead of writing notes.

advanced.label: Advanced Students
strategies: Estimate what one resource saves a family in a year and show the math.
Find something on the Must Buy side that could be borrowed and explain how.
Write a short guide entry for the most underused resource on the map.

description.en: Students start with equal small "investments" (tokens or paper shapes). Through structured giving rounds, they observe what happens to the group's total when people share freely. The simulation generates the experience Frances describes — giving doesn't deplete you; it generates reciprocal giving and collective abundance.
description.es: Students start with equal small "investments" (tokens or paper shapes). Through structured giving rounds, they observe what happens to the group's total when people share freely. The simulation generates the experience Frances describes — giving doesn't deplete you; it generates reciprocal giving and collective abundance.

description.es: "The friends grew more vegetables than they could use. They gave them away. In return, neighbors gave them jam, cookies, and flowers. Today we're going to see what happens when everyone shares." Distribute 3 tokens per student.

sayThis.en: "The friends grew lots of vegetables. They gave them away, and their neighbors gave them jam, cookies and flowers. Here are three tokens. Let's see what happens when we share."
sayThis.es: "The friends grew lots of vegetables. They gave them away, and their neighbors gave them jam, cookies and flowers. Here are three tokens. Let's see what happens when we share."

watchFor.en: Students playing with tokens right away. Tokens stay in the envelope until the round starts.
watchFor.es: Students playing with tokens right away. Tokens stay in the envelope until the round starts.

doneWhen.es: Every student has three tokens.

watchFor.en: Students playing with tokens right away. Tokens stay in the paper pocket until the round starts.
watchFor.es: Students playing with tokens right away. Tokens stay in the paper pocket until the round starts.

description.es: "Give ONE token to someone you think needs it or would appreciate it. You choose who. You may give to anyone in the room." Observe: every student gives one and (likely) receives one or more.

sayThis.en: "Give one token to someone. You pick who. Then sit back down."
sayThis.es: "Give one token to someone. You pick who. Then sit back down."

watchFor.en: Nobody giving to the quiet students. Don't fix it now — bring it up in Discussion.
watchFor.es: Nobody giving to the quiet students. Don't fix it now — bring it up in Discussion.

doneWhen.en: Every student has given one token and is back in their seat.
doneWhen.es: Every student has given one token and is back in their seat.

description.en: Each student gives one token to the person sitting next to them. Nobody picks who - choosing turns into a popularity contest at this age.
description.es: Each student gives one token to the person sitting next to them. Nobody picks who - choosing turns into a popularity contest at this age.

sayThis.en: "Pick up one token. Give it to the person next to you. Then hands in your lap."
sayThis.es: "Pick up one token. Give it to the person next to you. Then hands in your lap."

watchFor.en: A child who will not let go of a token. Say, "You still have two," and count the two with them.
watchFor.es: A child who will not let go of a token. Say, "You still have two," and count the two with them.

doneWhen.en: Every student has given one token away and has hands in their lap.
doneWhen.es: Every student has given one token away and has hands in their lap.

description.en: "Count your tokens. Did you end up with more, less, or the same as you started?" Class show of hands: more / same / fewer. Tally.
description.es: "Count your tokens. Did you end up with more, less, or the same as you started?" Class show of hands: more / same / fewer. Tally.

sayThis.en: "Count your tokens. Hands up if you have more than three. The same. Fewer."
sayThis.es: "Count your tokens. Hands up if you have more than three. The same. Fewer."

watchFor.en: Miscounting. Have them lay the tokens in a row and touch each one.
watchFor.es: Miscounting. Have them lay the tokens in a row and touch each one.

doneWhen.en: The more, same and fewer tally is on the board.
doneWhen.es: The more, same and fewer tally is on the board.

description.en: Students lay their tokens in a row and count by touching each one. Two hands-up groups, not three: hands up for three tokens, then hands up for not three.
description.es: Students lay their tokens in a row and count by touching each one. Two hands-up groups, not three: hands up for three tokens, then hands up for not three.

sayThis.en: "Lay your tokens in a row. Touch each one and count. Hands up if you have three."
sayThis.es: "Lay your tokens in a row. Touch each one and count. Hands up if you have three."

watchFor.en: Kids sliding tokens around while they count. Have them slide each counted token back into the envelope.
watchFor.es: Kids sliding tokens around while they count. Have them slide each counted token back into the envelope.

doneWhen.en: Every student has their tokens in a row and both sets of hands have been counted.
doneWhen.es: Every student has their tokens in a row and both sets of hands have been counted.

description.en: "What happened? Did giving away one token leave you with less? Why or why not?"
description.es: "What happened? Did giving away one token leave you with less? Why or why not?"

sayThis.en: "You gave one away. Did you end up with less? Why, or why not?"
sayThis.es: "You gave one away. Did you end up with less? Why, or why not?"

watchFor.en: Students with fewer feeling left out. Ask how it felt to give, not only to get.
watchFor.es: Students with fewer feeling left out. Ask how it felt to give, not only to get.

doneWhen.en: At least two students have said what happened to their tokens and why.
doneWhen.es: At least two students have said what happened to their tokens and why.

description.en: One question only: did it feel good to give a token away? Skip the why.
description.es: One question only: did it feel good to give a token away? Skip the why.

sayThis.en: "You gave one token away and somebody gave you one. Did it feel good to give?"
sayThis.es: "You gave one token away and somebody gave you one. Did it feel good to give?"

doneWhen.en: Two children have said out loud how giving felt.
doneWhen.es: Two children have said out loud how giving felt.

discussionQuestions: Frances said there's always enough when we share. Did today show that?
Did anyone give more than one token? Did they end up with less?
What if nobody gave any tokens — would that be better?

beforeClass.en: With scissors, cut construction paper into small squares, 3 per student, and put each set in an envelope. Every square counts as one token.
beforeClass.es: With scissors, cut construction paper into small squares, 3 per student, and put each set in an envelope. Every square counts as one token.

runningLongOrShort.en: Long: in Count, skip the tally and just ask for hands. Short: run a second giving round before Discussion and count again.
runningLongOrShort.es: Long: in Count, skip the tally and just ask for hands. Short: run a second giving round before Discussion and count again.

description.en: Distribute 5 tokens. Students write "5" in the START row of their journal.
description.es: Distribute 5 tokens. Students write "5" in the START row of their journal.

sayThis.en: "Here are five tokens. Count them. Write 5 in the Start row of your journal."
sayThis.es: "Here are five tokens. Count them. Write 5 in the Start row of your journal."

watchFor.en: Journals with no rows. Point to the rows on the board and have them copy.
watchFor.es: Journals with no rows. Point to the rows on the board and have them copy.

doneWhen.en: Every journal says 5 in the Start row.
doneWhen.es: Every journal says 5 in the Start row.

description.en: "Give however many tokens you want to whoever you want. You don't have to give any. You don't have to give equally." After round: count tokens, record in journal row.
description.es: "Give however many tokens you want to whoever you want. You don't have to give any. You don't have to give equally." After round: count tokens, record in journal row.

sayThis.en: "Give as many as you want to anyone you want. You can give none. When I say stop, count and write your number in Round 1."
sayThis.es: "Give as many as you want to anyone you want. You can give none. When I say stop, count and write your number in Round 1."

watchFor.en: Students taking tokens instead of waiting to be given them. Only giving counts.
watchFor.es: Students taking tokens instead of waiting to be given them. Only giving counts.

doneWhen.en: Every journal has a Round 1 number.
doneWhen.es: Every journal has a Round 1 number.

description.en: "The friends grew more than they could use — they gave the excess. This round: give away any tokens you have above 3. Keep 3 for yourself, share the rest." After round: count and record.
description.es: "The friends grew more than they could use — they gave the excess. This round: give away any tokens you have above 3. Keep 3 for yourself, share the rest." After round: count and record.

sayThis.en: "The friends had more than they could use, so they shared the extra. Keep three. Give away the rest. Then count and write."
sayThis.es: "The friends had more than they could use, so they shared the extra. Keep three. Give away the rest. Then count and write."

watchFor.en: Students with three or fewer thinking they have to give. They keep what they have.
watchFor.es: Students with three or fewer thinking they have to give. They keep what they have.

doneWhen.en: Every journal has a Round 2 number.
doneWhen.es: Every journal has a Round 2 number.

description.en: Teacher tallies: how many tokens does the class have total? Did the total go up, down, or stay the same? (It stays the same — conservation of tokens. Point this out. The distribution changed, not the total.)
description.es: Teacher tallies: how many tokens does the class have total? Did the total go up, down, or stay the same? (It stays the same — conservation of tokens. Point this out. The distribution changed, not the total.)

sayThis.en: "Let's add up every token in the room. Is it more, less, or the same as when we started?"
sayThis.es: "Let's add up every token in the room. Is it more, less, or the same as when we started?"

watchFor.en: Students expecting the total to grow. Write the starting total next to the new one.
watchFor.es: Students expecting the total to grow. Write the starting total next to the new one.

doneWhen.en: Both totals are on the board and the class can see they match.
doneWhen.es: Both totals are on the board and the class can see they match.

description.en: "What changed between Round 1 and Round 2? What does it mean to share only the 'excess'? The friends had 3 full baskets — more than enough. That's why sharing felt easy."
description.es: "What changed between Round 1 and Round 2? What does it mean to share only the 'excess'? The friends had 3 full baskets — more than enough. That's why sharing felt easy."

sayThis.en: "What was different in Round 2? The friends had three full baskets — more than enough. Why did that make sharing easy?"
sayThis.es: "What was different in Round 2? The friends had three full baskets — more than enough. Why did that make sharing easy?"

watchFor.en: Students saying sharing made more tokens. Point back to the two totals on the board.
watchFor.es: Students saying sharing made more tokens. Point back to the two totals on the board.

doneWhen.en: At least two students have said what changed between the rounds.
doneWhen.es: At least two students have said what changed between the rounds.

discussionQuestions: Why is it easier to share when you have MORE than enough?
Frances said 'sharing creates abundance.' What does that mean if the total number of tokens didn't change?
What's the difference between giving because you have extra vs. giving when you're barely getting by?
The seeds the friends planted in Frances's garden (Chapter 2) grew into enough to share. What was the 'investment' that made that possible?

beforeClass.es: With scissors, cut construction paper into squares, 5 per student, in envelopes. Draw the journal on the board for students to copy on plain paper with a pencil: three rows labeled Start, Round 1 and Round 2.

runningLongOrShort.es: Long: in Discussion, ask only the first question. Short: after Count Class Total, run a quick round where everyone gives one token, then count again.

sayThis.en: "Back to chapter two. Riley planted seeds and got a whole garden. What did she put in? What came back? Today we do the same thing with tokens."
sayThis.es: "Back to chapter two. Riley planted seeds and got a whole garden. What did she put in? What came back? Today we do the same thing with tokens."

doneWhen.en: Every card names one thing invested and one thing returned.
doneWhen.es: Every card names one thing invested and one thing returned.

watchFor.en: Answers only about flowers. Push toward time and patience as the investment.
watchFor.es: Answers only about flowers. Push toward time and patience as the investment.

description.en: Students complete their Investment Card. "Think back to Chapter 2. Riley planted flower seeds. The return was a whole garden. What did she invest? What did she get back?" sayThis.es: "Here are your tokens." Nothing else. Don't explain the amounts.

doneWhen.es: Every student has their envelope and at least one person has said "that's not fair".

watchFor.en: The moment someone notices. Let it happen. Don't answer the question yet.
watchFor.es: The moment someone notices. Let it happen. Don't answer the question yet.

description.es: Distribute tokens unevenly: some students get 15 (the "abundant harvest" students), some get 8, some get 5, some get 3 (the "scarce" students). Do NOT announce this is unequal — let them discover.

doneWhen.es: Every student has their paper pocket and at least one person has said "that's not fair".

sayThis.es: "Give to whoever you want, as much as you want. No rules at all. Write down every give in your journal."

doneWhen.es: Every journal has at least one entry, including "gave nothing".

watchFor.es: Who gives and who gets ignored. Note two names — you'll use them in the last step.

description.es: Open giving round. "Give however you want to whoever you want. No rules." Record in journal. Observe who gives, who receives, whether inequity narrows or widens.

sayThis.en: "New rule. Five tokens is what a person needs. Anything over five is extra, and the extra gets shared first."
sayThis.es: "New rule. Five tokens is what a person needs. Anything over five is extra, and the extra gets shared first."

doneWhen.en: Every student has written their new total in their journal.
doneWhen.es: Every student has written their new total in their journal.

watchFor.en: Hoarders hiding tokens. Don't police it — record it. It's data.
watchFor.es: Hoarders hiding tokens. Don't police it — record it. It's data.

description.es: "This round: everyone identifies their 'need' (a baseline of 5 tokens). Anyone with more than 5 shares the excess first." Record. Does inequity narrow?

sayThis.es: "Last rule. If somebody gives to you, you have to give to somebody. Doesn't have to be back to them. Watch what happens to the room."

doneWhen.es: At least one chain of three is drawn on the board.

watchFor.es: Chains forming. Point one out loud as it happens.

description.es: "This round: if someone gives to you, you must give something back — not necessarily to them, but to someone." Record. Observe the chain-reaction effect.

sayThis.en: "Three columns. After each round, the highest number in the room and the lowest. Subtract. That's the gap. Copy the three numbers down and draw the line."
sayThis.es: "Three columns. After each round, the highest number in the room and the lowest. Subtract. That's the gap. Copy the three numbers down and draw the line."

doneWhen.es: Every student has drawn the line and the winning rule is circled on the board.

watchFor.en: Students reading a falling line as everyone getting poorer. Ask what happened to the class total.
watchFor.es: Students reading a falling line as everyone getting poorer. Ask what happened to the class total.

description.en: Three columns on the board: after Round 1, after Round 2, after Round 3. For each, record the highest token count in the room and the lowest, and subtract to get the gap. Students copy the three numbers and draw the line on scrap paper. The shape of that line is the whole lesson. Ask which rule closed the gap fastest, whether closing it made the room better off in total, and what happened to the people who started with the most.
description.es: Three columns on the board: after Round 1, after Round 2, after Round 3. For each, record the highest token count in the room and the lowest, and subtract to get the gap. Students copy the three numbers and draw the line on scrap paper. The shape of that line is the whole lesson. Ask which rule closed the gap fastest, whether closing it made the room better off in total, and what happened to the people who started with the most.

sayThis.en: "Here is the most anyone had, and the fewest. I worked out the gap. Did the gap get bigger or smaller after each round? Draw the line."
sayThis.es: "Here is the most anyone had, and the fewest. I worked out the gap. Did the gap get bigger or smaller after each round? Draw the line."

watchFor.es: Students thinking a smaller gap means everyone lost tokens. Ask if the class still has the same number of tokens.

doneWhen.en: Every student has drawn the line and the class has said which round made the gap smallest.
doneWhen.es: Every student has drawn the line and the class has said which round made the gap smallest.

sayThis.en: "Which round felt best? Not which was fairest — which felt best. Were they the same round? And what happened to the people who started with the most?"

description.es: Compare all three rounds. "Which round felt best? Which reduced the gap between the most and least token-holders? Why?"

discussionQuestions: In Round 1, did the gap between the richest and poorest students get bigger or smaller? What about Round 3?
The friends grew Frances's seeds into food. The seeds cost nothing and came from nature. But the investment of TIME changed everything. What does that tell us?
Layla and her friends gave away vegetables. Neighbors gave back jam and cookies and flowers. Did they end up poorer?
Benny asked 'to who?' when they decided to share. How do you decide who to give to when you have extra?
The class as a whole had the same number of tokens the whole time. So what did 'abundance' actually mean?
extensionIdeas: Connect to real-world abundance: research community gardens, food banks, mutual aid networks — organizations built on the idea that sharing excess creates community resilience
Write Frances's speech from the episode: "You learned about investment and patience" — expand it into a 3-paragraph essay from the perspective of one of the friends
Compare: what would happen in a market economy where tokens could only be traded for equal value, not given? Run Round 4 with that rule and compare the result

runningLongOrShort.en: Long: cut round three and graph two rounds instead of three. Short: add a fourth round where giving is anonymous.

focus: Start with a few tokens
Give one token in each round
Watch what happens to the group pile
Words: give, share, more, group
Track your tokens through the giving rounds
Notice that the group total stays the same
Tell how it felt to give and receive
Vocabulary: give, share, abundance, group
Record your token total after each round
Explain why sharing changed who has tokens, not the total
Compare giving freely vs. holding back
Vocabulary: generosity, abundance, contribute, community
Graph the gap between the most and fewest tokens
Give back after receiving and trace the chain
Argue when giving benefits the whole group
Vocabulary: reciprocity, abundance, collective value, surplus

ell.label: English Language Learners
strategies: Act out giving with one token before each round: hold it out, hand it over, say "for you".
Give sentence frames: "I gave ___. I got ___."
Let students use tally marks in the journal instead of words.

learningDifferences.label: Students with Learning Differences
strategies: Let students line tokens up in a row to count them.
Draw the journal rows ahead of time so students only write numbers.
Pair with a partner who counts tokens with them after each round.

advanced.label: Advanced Students
strategies: Predict the gap or the count before each round, then check the prediction.
Invent a new giving rule and explain what it would do to the gap.
Explain why the class total stays the same while each person's count changes.

ell.label: English Language Learners

Post sentence frames on the board: "My treasure is ___." "My skill is ___."
Pair with a fluent partner for the share or gallery walk.

strategies: Pre-fold and staple the book for students who find folding hard.

Work out the savings goal at two weekly amounts and compare the weeks.

description.en: Explain swap meet rules: bring one item you're willing to trade, both people must agree, you can say no, trades must be fair. Review what makes trading fair.
description.es: Explain swap meet rules: bring one item you're willing to trade, both people must agree, you can say no, trades must be fair. Review what makes trading fair.

sayThis.en: "Today we trade. You hold one thing. You can swap it for a friend's thing. You both have to say yes. You can always say no thank you."
sayThis.es: "Today we trade. You hold one thing. You can swap it for a friend's thing. You both have to say yes. You can always say no thank you."

watchFor.en: Kids who think saying no is mean. Ask one child to say "no thank you" to you, and thank them for it.
watchFor.es: Kids who think saying no is mean. Ask one child to say "no thank you" to you, and thank them for it.

doneWhen.en: Every child is holding an item and can say one rule back to you.
doneWhen.es: Every child is holding an item and can say one rule back to you.

description.en: Give every child one item to hold before you talk. Teach two rules only: you both have to say yes, and you can always say no thank you. Skip the talk about what makes a trade fair.
description.es: Give every child one item to hold before you talk. Teach two rules only: you both have to say yes, and you can always say no thank you. Skip the talk about what makes a trade fair.

doneWhen.en: Every child is holding one item and the whole class has said "no thank you" out loud together.
doneWhen.es: Every child is holding one item and the whole class has said "no thank you" out loud together.

description.en: Students circulate with their items and negotiate trades. Encourage respectful communication: 'Would you trade your ___ for my ___?' Track who trades and who doesn't on class chart.
description.es: Students circulate with their items and negotiate trades. Encourage respectful communication: 'Would you trade your ___ for my ___?' Track who trades and who doesn't on class chart.

sayThis.en: "Walk and look. Ask, 'Will you trade your ___ for my ___?' If they say no, say okay and ask someone else."
sayThis.es: "Walk and look. Ask, 'Will you trade your ___ for my ___?' If they say no, say okay and ask someone else."

watchFor.en: A child standing still with an item nobody has asked about. Walk over with them and ask a classmate yourself.
watchFor.es: A child standing still with an item nobody has asked about. Walk over with them and ask a classmate yourself.

doneWhen.en: Every child has asked at least one person, and each trade has a mark on the chart.
doneWhen.es: Every child has asked at least one person, and each trade has a mark on the chart.

description.en: Children walk with their one item and ask one friend to trade. Model the question with one child first, in front of everyone. You make the marks on the chart. The children do no writing.
description.es: Children walk with their one item and ask one friend to trade. Model the question with one child first, in front of everyone. You make the marks on the chart. The children do no writing.

sayThis.en: "Walk and look. Ask, 'Will you trade your blank for my blank?' If they say no, say okay and ask someone else."
sayThis.es: "Walk and look. Ask, 'Will you trade your blank for my blank?' If they say no, say okay and ask someone else."

description.en: Pause trading. Quick discussion: What trades happened? What made you decide to trade or not trade? Any surprises? Students can make additional trades if they want.
description.es: Pause trading. Quick discussion: What trades happened? What made you decide to trade or not trade? Any surprises? Students can make additional trades if they want.

sayThis.en: "Freeze. Hold up what you have now. Who has something new? Why did you say yes? Why did you say no?"
sayThis.es: "Freeze. Hold up what you have now. Who has something new? Why did you say yes? Why did you say no?"

watchFor.en: Kids who want their old item back. Tell them they can ask to trade back, and the other person can say yes or no.
watchFor.es: Kids who want their old item back. Tell them they can ask to trade back, and the other person can say yes or no.

doneWhen.en: Three children have told the class why they traded or why they didn't.
doneWhen.es: Three children have told the class why they traded or why they didn't.

description.en: Stop the trading. Everyone holds up what they have right now. Ask one question only: did you say yes or did you say no? Children who still want to trade get one more turn.
description.es: Stop the trading. Everyone holds up what they have right now. Ask one question only: did you say yes or did you say no? Children who still want to trade get one more turn.

sayThis.en: "Freeze. Hold up what you have now. Who has something new? Tell me one word about why you said yes."
sayThis.es: "Freeze. Hold up what you have now. Who has something new? Tell me one word about why you said yes."

doneWhen.en: Two children have told the class why they traded.
doneWhen.es: Two children have told the class why they traded.

description.en: Look at class trading data: How many students traded? How many trades total? Who didn't trade and why? Chart the results together.
description.es: Look at class trading data: How many students traded? How many trades total? Who didn't trade and why? Chart the results together.

sayThis.en: "Hands up if you traded. Let's count. Hands up if you kept your thing. Let's count that too."
sayThis.es: "Hands up if you traded. Let's count. Hands up if you kept your thing. Let's count that too."

watchFor.en: Kids who kept their item feeling like they lost. Say out loud that keeping your thing is a fine choice.
watchFor.es: Kids who kept their item feeling like they lost. Say out loud that keeping your thing is a fine choice.

doneWhen.en: The chart shows how many traded, how many kept, and the total number of trades.
doneWhen.es: The chart shows how many traded, how many kept, and the total number of trades.

description.en: Count hands with the class twice: how many traded, how many kept. Write those two numbers on the board. Skip the total number of trades and skip asking why.
description.es: Count hands with the class twice: how many traded, how many kept. Write those two numbers on the board. Skip the total number of trades and skip asking why.

doneWhen.en: Two numbers are on the board: how many traded and how many kept.
doneWhen.es: Two numbers are on the board: how many traded and how many kept.

description.en: Discuss: Is your new item better than your old one? What makes a trade feel fair? How is trading different from buying and selling?
description.es: Discuss: Is your new item better than your old one? What makes a trade feel fair? How is trading different from buying and selling?

sayThis.en: "Look at what you have. Do you like it more than what you brought? Thumbs up or thumbs down."
sayThis.es: "Look at what you have. Do you like it more than what you brought? Thumbs up or thumbs down."

watchFor.en: Only the loud kids answering. Use thumbs so everyone answers at once, then ask one quiet child why.
watchFor.es: Only the loud kids answering. Use thumbs so everyone answers at once, then ask one quiet child why.

doneWhen.en: Every child has shown a thumb, and two have said why.
doneWhen.es: Every child has shown a thumb, and two have said why.

description.en: Thumbs up or thumbs down only: do you like what you have now? Skip the question about fair trades and skip the one about buying and selling.
description.es: Thumbs up or thumbs down only: do you like what you have now? Skip the question about fair trades and skip the one about buying and selling.

discussionQuestions: Did you trade? Why or why not?
Is your new item better than your old one? Why?
What made you want to trade?

runningLongOrShort.es: Long: cut the Mid-Activity Check-In to one question and skip the extra trades. Short: give the Trading Round two more minutes, then do the Check-In.

description.en: For each item, write a value card with a pencil: "This is a ___. It's special because ___." Draw a picture of the item with crayons.
description.es: For each item, write a value card with a pencil: "This is a ___. It's special because ___." Draw a picture of the item with crayons.

sayThis.en: "Put your thing in front of you. On your card, draw it. Then finish this: 'It's special because...' Give one reason a friend would want it."
sayThis.es: "Put your thing in front of you. On your card, draw it. Then finish this: 'It's special because...' Give one reason a friend would want it."

watchFor.en: Kids who spend all five minutes on the drawing. At three minutes, tell everyone to move on to the reason.
watchFor.es: Kids who spend all five minutes on the drawing. At three minutes, tell everyone to move on to the reason.

doneWhen.en: Every student has a card with a drawing and a reason.
doneWhen.es: Every student has a card with a drawing and a reason.

description.en: Each child draws their item on the card with crayons. Then they say out loud why it is special, and the teacher writes one word on the card with a pencil.
description.es: Each child draws their item on the card with crayons. Then they say out loud why it is special, and the teacher writes one word on the card with a pencil.

sayThis.en: "Put your thing in front of you. Draw it on your card. Now tell me: why is it special? I will write one word for you."
sayThis.es: "Put your thing in front of you. Draw it on your card. Now tell me: why is it special? I will write one word for you."

watchFor.en: Kids who wait for you before they draw. Tell them to draw first, then go desk to desk writing one word on each card.
watchFor.es: Kids who wait for you before they draw. Tell them to draw first, then go desk to desk writing one word on each card.

doneWhen.en: Every child has a card with a drawing and one word on it.
doneWhen.es: Every child has a card with a drawing and one word on it.

description.en: Each student arranges their items at their desk with value cards displayed
description.es: Each student arranges their items at their desk with value cards displayed

sayThis.en: "Put your thing on your desk. Stand your card next to it so people can see it."
sayThis.es: "Put your thing on your desk. Stand your card next to it so people can see it."

watchFor.en: Cards lying flat where nobody can read them. Show them how to fold the card so it stands up.
watchFor.es: Cards lying flat where nobody can read them. Show them how to fold the card so it stands up.

doneWhen.en: Every desk has an item with its card beside it.
doneWhen.es: Every desk has an item with its card beside it.

description.en: Students walk around viewing all items. Mental note of what they want.
description.es: Students walk around viewing all items. Mental note of what they want.

sayThis.en: "Walk and look. Hands behind your back. No trading yet. Find one thing you would like."
sayThis.es: "Walk and look. Hands behind your back. No trading yet. Find one thing you would like."

watchFor.en: Kids picking up other people's things. Say "hands behind your back" again at the first grab.
watchFor.es: Kids picking up other people's things. Say "hands behind your back" again at the first grab.

doneWhen.en: Every student can point to one item they want.
doneWhen.es: Every student can point to one item they want.

description.en: Students approach each other to propose trades. "I'll trade you my ___ for your ___." Both must agree.
description.es: Students approach each other to propose trades. "I'll trade you my ___ for your ___." Both must agree.

sayThis.en: "Now you can trade. Take your thing to the person whose thing you liked. Say, 'I'll trade you my ___ for your ___.' You both must say yes. No thank you is okay."
sayThis.es: "Now you can trade. Take your thing to the person whose thing you liked. Say, 'I'll trade you my ___ for your ___.' You both must say yes. No thank you is okay."

watchFor.en: A crowd around the one item everyone wants. Tell the owner they get to choose, and send the rest to their second pick.
watchFor.es: A crowd around the one item everyone wants. Tell the owner they get to choose, and send the rest to their second pick.

doneWhen.en: Every student has made at least one offer and all trades are finished.
doneWhen.es: Every student has made at least one offer and all trades are finished.

description.en: Sit in circle. Share: "I traded my ___ for ___ because ___."
description.es: Sit in circle. Share: "I traded my ___ for ___ because ___."

sayThis.en: "Finish my sentence: 'I traded my ___ for ___ because ___.' If you kept yours, say 'I kept my ___ because ___.'"
sayThis.es: "Finish my sentence: 'I traded my ___ for ___ because ___.' If you kept yours, say 'I kept my ___ because ___.'"

watchFor.en: Two minutes is not enough for everyone. Pick four kids to share, and have the rest tell a partner.
watchFor.es: Two minutes is not enough for everyone. Pick four kids to share, and have the rest tell a partner.

doneWhen.en: Four students have shared out loud, and everyone else has told a partner.
doneWhen.es: Four students have shared out loud, and everyone else has told a partner.

discussionQuestions: Did everyone value the same items? Why or why not?
What made a trade feel fair?
Was there an item lots of people wanted? What happened?
How did you decide what to trade for?
How is a swap meet different from a store?
extensionIdeas: Create a class "Trade Log" where students record: "I traded ___ to ___ for ___."

runningLongOrShort.en: Long: cut the Gallery Walk to two minutes and go straight to the Open Trading Period. Short: in the Reflection Circle, let every child share, not just a few.
runningLongOrShort.es: Long: cut the Gallery Walk to two minutes and go straight to the Open Trading Period. Short: in the Reflection Circle, let every child share, not just a few.
