sayThis.en: "You're opening a bakery, and nothing you make can be eaten. You build paper pastries. People buy them for parties and to put on top of presents. Pick your product. Then guess two numbers: what will one cost to build, and what will you charge?"
sayThis.es: "You're opening a bakery, and nothing you make can be eaten. You build paper pastries. People buy them for parties and to put on top of presents. Pick your product. Then guess two numbers: what will one cost to build, and what will you charge?"

doneWhen.es: Every team has a product, four named roles, and a guessed cost and price written down.

watchFor.es: Teams picking the fanciest build without reading the parts prices. Make them read the sheet first.

description.en: Teams choose a build from 2-3 options (a simple cupcake, a layered cake slice, a decorated paper cookie) - Receive the parts cost sheet - Predict: "How much will this cost to make? How much should we charge?" - Assign roles: Head Baker, Parts Manager, Cost Tracker, Packaging Designer

discussionQuestions: What surprised you about the costs?
Was any part more expensive than you expected?
How much profit should a business make—a little or a lot? Why?
What happens if you price too low? Too high?
Why do real bakeries charge different prices for different items?
Besides ingredients, what OTHER costs does a real bakery have? (Rent, electricity, wages, equipment)
How does knowing exact costs help you run a business?
Could your family run a bakery business with what you learned today?

Calculate break-even point (how many items must you sell to cover costs?)

Calculate cost per item with teacher support (simple division)
Set appropriate selling prices that include profit
Compare homemade costs to store-bought prices
Understand that profit is necessary for businesses
Track wasted parts and what the mistakes cost
Complex cost calculations including packaging, labor, and waste
Independent calculation of profit margins
Calculate total revenue if every pastry sells
Compare making vs. buying economics across multiple products
Create a bakery name, logo and price tags
Write business justifications and pricing strategies
Decide what to do with the profit (reinvest, pay, expand)

ell.label: English Language Learners
strategies: Draw a small picture beside each part and its price on the board: base, frosting, wrapper, topper.
Post the frame "It costs ___. We charge ___." and have students say it before they write a price.
Build one pastry in front of the class before giving spoken instructions.

learningDifferences.label: Students with Learning Differences
strategies: Give a cost sheet with the parts already listed and a box for tally marks beside each.
Offer the parts tracker job, which uses tally marks instead of writing.
Allow a calculator for the adding and dividing in the cost step.

advanced.label: Advanced Students
strategies: Add packaging and labor to the cost, then compare cost per item with the party-shop price.
Work out how many pastries must sell to cover all the costs.
Price a second build and compare which one makes more profit per item.

description.es: Each student receives: * 1 perishable card (fish, bread, milk, fruit) * 2 non-perishable cards (toys, books, tools, clothes). Explain three trading rounds. Show price chart on board

sayThis.es: "You each have three cards. One goes bad fast. Two last. We have three rounds. Look at the chart: fresh things drop in price every round. The others stay the same."

watchFor.en: Cards changing hands before the round starts. Cards stay face down until the timer starts.
watchFor.es: Cards changing hands before the round starts. Cards stay face down until the timer starts.

doneWhen.en: Every student has three cards and can point to their fresh one.
doneWhen.es: Every student has three cards and can point to their fresh one.

description.es: Timer set for 3 minutes. Prices: Perishables $10, Non-perishables $5. Students can sell to "market buyer" (teacher/volunteer). Buyers walk around making offers. Record what each student sells

sayThis.en: "Round one. Fresh things are $10. Everything else is $5. Sell to the buyer if you want to. Write down what you sell."
sayThis.es: "Round one. Fresh things are $10. Everything else is $5. Sell to the buyer if you want to. Write down what you sell."

watchFor.es: Everyone crowding the buyer. Sellers stay at their desks and the buyer walks to them.

doneWhen.es: The timer is done and every sale is written down.

description.en: Timer set for 2 minutes. Prices: Perishables DROP to $5, Non-perishables stay $5. Students who held perishables see value decrease. More selling happens. Visual: Update price chart dramatically
description.es: Timer set for 2 minutes. Prices: Perishables DROP to $5, Non-perishables stay $5. Students who held perishables see value decrease. More selling happens. Visual: Update price chart dramatically

sayThis.en: "Price change! Fresh things are only $5 now. If you still have fish, it just lost half its price."
sayThis.es: "Price change! Fresh things are only $5 now. If you still have fish, it just lost half its price."

watchFor.en: Kids arguing it should still be $10. Point to the chart and say fresh things go bad.
watchFor.es: Kids arguing it should still be $10. Point to the chart and say fresh things go bad.

doneWhen.es: The chart shows the new price and Round 2 sales are written down.

sayThis.es: "Last round. Fresh things are $1. One minute. This is your last chance to sell."

watchFor.es: Kids holding fresh cards to be stubborn. Let them. The count at the end will show what it cost.

doneWhen.es: The timer is done and every student knows what they are still holding.

items: Scrap paper — 40 sheets, torn into about 100 inventory cards (10 stalls), about 220 paper-money bills for the starting cash, 20 tracking sheets, buyer badges and 3 covers for the price periods

sayThis.en: "Fifty dollars each. Your stall has fresh things and things that keep. Write down everything you're holding before we open, because you will not remember later."
sayThis.es: "Fifty dollars each. Your stall has fresh things and things that keep. Write down everything you're holding before we open, because you will not remember later."

doneWhen.es: Every stall has its inventory written on the sheet and $50 counted out on the desk.

watchFor.en: Stalls trying to open before the sheet is filled in. Hold the bell.
watchFor.es: Stalls trying to open before the sheet is filled in. Hold the bell.

description.en: Students set up stalls with inventory. Receive starting cash $50. Review price tracking sheet. Assign initial "buyers" (rotating role). Practice using tracking sheet with a pencil.
description.es: Students set up stalls with inventory. Receive starting cash $50. Review price tracking sheet. Assign initial "buyers" (rotating role). Practice using tracking sheet with a pencil.

description.en: Students set up stalls with their inventory cards. Each child gets $20 in scrap-paper money. Look at the tracking sheet together: tick each card you hold with a pencil. Pick the first buyers; the buyer job moves around.
description.es: Students set up stalls with their inventory cards. Each child gets $20 in scrap-paper money. Look at the tracking sheet together: tick each card you hold with a pencil. Pick the first buyers; the buyer job moves around.

sayThis.en: "Twenty dollars each. Your stall has fresh things and things that keep. Tick every card you hold on your sheet before we open."
sayThis.es: "Twenty dollars each. Your stall has fresh things and things that keep. Tick every card you hold on your sheet before we open."

watchFor.en: Stalls trying to open before the sheet is ticked. Hold the bell.
watchFor.es: Stalls trying to open before the sheet is ticked. Hold the bell.

doneWhen.en: Every stall has its cards ticked on the sheet and $20 counted out on the desk.
doneWhen.es: Every stall has its cards ticked on the sheet and $20 counted out on the desk.

sayThis.en: "Market's open. Fish, fruit, milk and bread are eight dollars. Everything else is five. Sell what you can and mark every sale as it happens, not at the end."
sayThis.es: "Market's open. Fish, fruit, milk and bread are eight dollars. Everything else is five. Sell what you can and mark every sale as it happens, not at the end."

doneWhen.en: Every seller has at least one line written in the Period 1 row.
doneWhen.es: Every seller has at least one line written in the Period 1 row.

watchFor.en: Sellers holding out for a better price on the fresh goods. Say nothing yet. That's the trap and it should spring on its own.
watchFor.es: Sellers holding out for a better price on the fresh goods. Say nothing yet. That's the trap and it should spring on its own.

Buyers visit stalls, negotiate, purchase. Sellers mark sales on tracking sheet. Rotate buyer badges after 3 minutes
description.es: Timer: 5 minutes of active trading. Starting prices: * Perishables: $8 each (fish, fruit, milk, bread) * Non-perishables: $5 each (toys, books, tools, clothes, crafts, jewelry). description.es: The timer runs for 5 minutes. Fresh things (fish, fruit, milk, bread) cost $8. Things that keep (toys, books, tools, clothes) cost $5. Buyers visit stalls and buy. Sellers make one tally mark on the tracking sheet for each sale. Swap buyers after 3 minutes.

sayThis.es: "Market's open. Fresh things are eight dollars. Everything else is five. Each time you sell, make a tally mark on your sheet."

watchFor.en: Sellers holding out for a better price on the fresh goods. Say nothing yet. Let them find out on their own.
watchFor.es: Sellers holding out for a better price on the fresh goods. Say nothing yet. Let them find out on their own.

doneWhen.en: Every seller has at least one tally mark in the Period 1 row.
doneWhen.es: Every seller has at least one tally mark in the Period 1 row.

sayThis.es: "Price change. Fresh things are four dollars now. Everything else is still five. If you're holding fish, your fish just lost half its value while you stood there."

doneWhen.en: Every tracking sheet has a Period 2 row filled in, even if the line says nothing sold.
doneWhen.es: Every tracking sheet has a Period 2 row filled in, even if the line says nothing sold.

watchFor.en: Students who don't see why. Say it plainly: fresh things go off, things that keep don't.
watchFor.es: Students who don't see why. Say it plainly: fresh things go off, things that keep don't.

description.es: Timer: 4 minutes of active trading. Price changes announced dramatically: * Perishables: DROP to $4 each * Non-perishables: STAY $5 each. Discussion pause: "Notice anything about your fish value?". Continue trading. Sellers see depreciation impact. Rotate buyers again

sayThis.es: "Last change. Fresh is two dollars. Three minutes. If you're still holding fresh goods, this is the last money you will ever get for them."

doneWhen.en: The market is closed and every Period 3 row is filled.
doneWhen.es: The market is closed and every Period 3 row is filled.

watchFor.en: Panic selling turning into shouting. Set the rule: one seller talking at a time at each stall.
watchFor.es: Panic selling turning into shouting. Set the rule: one seller talking at a time at each stall.

description.es: Timer: 3 minutes of active trading. Final price changes: * Perishables: DROP to $2 each * Non-perishables: STAY $5 each. Urgent selling begins. Some students stuck with near-worthless perishables. Close market

doneWhen.es: Every bar graph shows a starting value and a final revenue.

focus: Simple sorting: "goes bad" vs. "lasts long" with picture support

Three price rounds with clear visual price charts
Simple money (dollar bills only, no coins)
Sentence frames: "I will sell my ___ now because ___"
Understanding that waiting = lower price for perishables

Full three-round market with price tracking sheets
Calculate simple revenue (items sold × price)

Complex tracking with profit/loss calculations

ell.label: English Language Learners

learningDifferences.label: Students with Learning Differences
strategies: Give just one fresh card and one keeping card.

advanced.label: Advanced Students
strategies: Work out how much a fresh card lost from the first period to the last, in dollars and as a fraction of its first price.

Complete contribution worksheet: * Name * Cash contributed: $_____ * Non-cash contributed: _____ * Total value: $_____. Pool all resources in center table. Calculate if goal met ($200 total).
description.es: Students receive varied resources: * 4 students: $30 cash each * 1 student: $30 cash + seed packets (worth $10) * 1 student: $30 cash + tools to share (worth $10). Complete contribution worksheet: * Name * Cash contributed: $_____ * Non-cash contributed: _____ * Total value: $_____. Pool all resources in center table. Calculate if goal met ($200 total).

description.en: Each child has a $1 card. In each group, one child also has a seeds card and one child has a tools card, worth $2 each. Each child says what they give: money, seeds or tools. Everyone puts their cards in the middle. Count together: $6 in money cards, $2 for seeds and $2 for tools make $10.
description.es: Each child has a $1 card. In each group, one child also has a seeds card and one child has a tools card, worth $2 each. Each child says what they give: money, seeds or tools. Everyone puts their cards in the middle. Count together: $6 in money cards, $2 for seeds and $2 for tools make $10.

sayThis.en: "Tell us what you give. Money, seeds or tools? Put your card in the middle. Now let's count it all together."
sayThis.es: "Tell us what you give. Money, seeds or tools? Put your card in the middle. Now let's count it all together."

watchFor.en: Kids thinking the seeds and tools cards do not count. Point to the board: the garden needs seeds and tools too.
watchFor.es: Kids thinking the seeds and tools cards do not count. Point to the board: the garden needs seeds and tools too.

doneWhen.en: The group has counted its cards out loud and reached $10.
doneWhen.es: The group has counted its cards out loud and reached $10.

sayThis.en: "Each square is two feet. Everyone gets a plot. You also need a path, somewhere for the tools and a tap. And you have to choose: same size plots for everyone, or bigger plots for whoever put in more. Your group decides, and you have to be able to defend it."
sayThis.es: "Each square is two feet. Everyone gets a plot. You also need a path, somewhere for the tools and a tap. And you have to choose: same size plots for everyone, or bigger plots for whoever put in more. Your group decides, and you have to be able to defend it."

doneWhen.en: Every grid shows labeled plots for all members, a path, a tool space and a water point.

watchFor.en: Groups drawing plots and forgetting the paths. Ask how anyone reaches the plot in the middle.

description.en: Groups (6-8 students) design garden layout: * Use grid paper (each square = 2 sq ft) * Divide into individual plots (4-6 sq ft per person) * Include shared spaces: tool shed area, compost bin, pathways, water access point. Assign plots fairly: * Option A: Equal sizes for all * Option B: Larger plots for larger investors * Group decides which is "fair". Choose plants for each plot and draw them in with a pencil. Label everything clearly.

description.en: Groups draw the garden on plain paper with a pencil. Draw one plot for each person, a path and a tap. Draw a plant in each plot and write each person's name on their plot. The group decides if every plot is the same size.
description.es: Groups draw the garden on plain paper with a pencil. Draw one plot for each person, a path and a tap. Draw a plant in each plot and write each person's name on their plot. The group decides if every plot is the same size.

sayThis.en: "Draw one garden. Everyone gets a plot. Draw a path so people can walk to their plot, and a tap. Then draw a plant in every plot and write your name on yours."
sayThis.es: "Draw one garden. Everyone gets a plot. Draw a path so people can walk to their plot, and a tap. Then draw a plant in every plot and write your name on yours."

watchFor.en: Plots nobody can reach. Ask how you walk to the plot in the middle.
watchFor.es: Plots nobody can reach. Ask how you walk to the plot in the middle.

doneWhen.es: Every drawing has a named plot for each child, a path and a tap.

sayThis.en: "Your plot grows this much. Work out what that's worth. Take off what you put in. Divide by what you put in. That's your return — put thirty in, get sixty back, you doubled it."
sayThis.es: "Your plot grows this much. Work out what that's worth. Take off what you put in. Divide by what you put in. That's your return — put thirty in, get sixty back, you doubled it."

doneWhen.en: Every student has written an investment, a harvest value and a return.
doneWhen.es: Every student has written an investment, a harvest value and a return.

watchFor.en: Division the wrong way round. Work the first example on the board with the whole room.
watchFor.es: Division the wrong way round. Work the first example on the board with the whole room.

description.en: Use provided data for expected harvest: * Tomatoes: 20 lbs per plot at $3 a lb * Lettuce: 10 heads per plot at $2 a head * Carrots: 15 bunches per plot at $2 a bunch. Students calculate: * Their investment: $______ * Their expected harvest value (at market price): $______ * ROI: (Harvest value − Investment) ÷ Investment. Example: Invested $30, harvest worth $60 → ROI = 100% (doubled money).
description.es: Use provided data for expected harvest: * Tomatoes: 20 lbs per plot at $3 a lb * Lettuce: 10 heads per plot at $2 a head * Carrots: 15 bunches per plot at $2 a bunch. Students calculate: * Their investment: $______ * Their expected harvest value (at market price): $______ * ROI: (Harvest value − Investment) ÷ Investment. Example: Invested $30, harvest worth $60 → ROI = 100% (doubled money).

description.en: Each child draws what their plot grows with a pencil: tomatoes, lettuce or carrots. Tell them each plot grows vegetables worth $4. Each child counts what they put in ($1, or $3 with a seeds or tools card) and what they get back ($4), and says which is more.
description.es: Each child draws what their plot grows with a pencil: tomatoes, lettuce or carrots. Tell them each plot grows vegetables worth $4. Each child counts what they put in ($1, or $3 with a seeds or tools card) and what they get back ($4), and says which is more.

sayThis.en: "Draw what your plot grows. Your plot grows $4 of vegetables. How much did you put in? Which is more? Do you get back more than you put in?"
sayThis.es: "Draw what your plot grows. Your plot grows $4 of vegetables. How much did you put in? Which is more? Do you get back more than you put in?"

watchFor.en: Kids who think they got back less. Count what they put in on your fingers, then count to $4.
watchFor.es: Kids who think they got back less. Count what they put in on your fingers, then count to $4.

doneWhen.en: Every child has drawn the harvest and said whether they got back more than they put in.
doneWhen.es: Every child has drawn the harvest and said whether they got back more than they put in.

sayThis.en: "One sentence, and everybody signs it. How are you splitting the vegetables? Equally, by what people put in, by who needs it most, or your own mix of those."
sayThis.es: "One sentence, and everybody signs it. How are you splitting the vegetables? Equally, by what people put in, by who needs it most, or your own mix of those."

doneWhen.en: Every group's agreement is written and signed by every member.
doneWhen.es: Every group's agreement is written and signed by every member.

watchFor.en: Groups choosing equal because it's quickest. Ask the biggest investor whether they agree, out loud.
watchFor.es: Groups choosing equal because it's quickest. Ask the biggest investor whether they agree, out loud.

description.en: Create written agreement: * "We agree that vegetables will be shared by: _____" * Options: equally, by contribution, by need, combination. All group members sign. Post agreements with garden designs
description.es: Create written agreement: * "We agree that vegetables will be shared by: _____" * Options: equally, by contribution, by need, combination. All group members sign. Post agreements with garden designs

sayThis.en: "Walk the room. Find one group that split the harvest differently from you."
sayThis.es: "Walk the room. Find one group that split the harvest differently from you."

doneWhen.en: Every group has named another group's sharing rule.
doneWhen.es: Every group has named another group's sharing rule.

watchFor.en: A lap with no reading. Give them the one thing to find before they stand up.
watchFor.es: A lap with no reading. Give them the one thing to find before they stand up.

description.en: View other groups' designs. Notice different solutions to fair distribution. Investment tracking sheet each group can copy onto plain paper: group name; for each member, cash, seeds, tools, time and total value; total group investment; goal met, or short by how much; plot assignments with each person's plot size in square feet and the reason for that size; the sharing agreement (equal shares, proportional to investment, based on need, or other) and every member's signature.
description.es: View other groups' designs. Notice different solutions to fair distribution. Investment tracking sheet each group can copy onto plain paper: group name; for each member, cash, seeds, tools, time and total value; total group investment; goal met, or short by how much; plot assignments with each person's plot size in square feet and the reason for that size; the sharing agreement (equal shares, proportional to investment, based on need, or other) and every member's signature.

discussionQuestions: Is it fair to give bigger plots to bigger investors, or should everyone get equal space?
What if someone contributed tools instead of money—should they get less vegetables?
How does a community garden help people who can't afford their own garden?
What's the return on investment if you invest $30 and get $60 worth of vegetables?
Could this idea work for other community projects? What else?
extensionIdeas: Plan next year's garden budget. Leave out one-time costs like the fence and see how much less each person must put in.
Draw a second layout for the same lot with fewer plots and a bigger shared space, then compare the two.
Find a shared space near school, such as a park or library, and list what different people give to keep it going.

strategies: Draw a small picture beside each cost on the board: plot, seeds, tools, soil.

strategies: Give a grid with the plots already marked.
Give each group member one job: drawer, counter, gluer or speaker.

description.en: Discuss handmade gifts: why make instead of buy? What makes handmade special? Review available materials for making holiday items.
description.es: Discuss handmade gifts: why make instead of buy? What makes handmade special? Review available materials for making holiday items.

sayThis.en: "You can buy a gift at a store. Or you can make one. Today you make one. What makes a made gift special?"
sayThis.es: "You can buy a gift at a store. Or you can make one. Today you make one. What makes a made gift special?"

watchFor.en: Kids saying bought gifts are better because they cost more. Ask how someone feels when you made it just for them.
watchFor.es: Kids saying bought gifts are better because they cost more. Ask how someone feels when you made it just for them.

doneWhen.en: Two kids have said why a handmade gift is special.
doneWhen.es: Two kids have said why a handmade gift is special.

description.en: One question only: what makes a gift you made special? Hold up a made card and a store card so they can see the two side by side.
description.es: One question only: what makes a gift you made special? Hold up a made card and a store card so they can see the two side by side.

description.en: Students choose what to make: card, ornament, bookmark, or simple craft. Plan design and gather materials.
description.es: Students choose what to make: card, ornament, bookmark, or simple craft. Plan design and gather materials.

sayThis.es: "Today we all make the same thing - a paper ornament. Your shape is already cut. Think of one person it is for."

doneWhen.es: Every child has a cut shape and crayons at their seat.

sayThis.es: "Add a message or a little picture. Make it special for the person who gets it."

sayThis.es: "Add one last thing to make it pretty. Tell me who it is for and I will write their name on it."

doneWhen.en: Every ornament has a name on it.
doneWhen.es: Every ornament has a name on it.

sayThis.es: "Hold up what you made. Who is it for? How is it different from a gift you buy?"

items: Plain paper — 40 sheets, shared at the stations for paper loops, bookmark shapes and cards

basicClassroom.description: Students make one item at a bead, felt, ribbon or paper station, write start and end times from the classroom clock on a tracking sheet with a pencil, then cost and price it.
items: Pony beads — about 400, shared at the bead station, from the art closet
Felt squares — 20, shared at the felt station
Ribbon or yarn — 1 roll, shared at the ribbon station, measured by the foot
Plain paper or cardstock — 20 sheets, shared at the paper station
Plain paper — 24 sheets, one tracking sheet per student and 4 price lists (teacher)
Scrap paper — 20 pieces, one price tag per student
Glue sticks — 4, one per station, shared
Scissors — 8 pairs, 2 per station, shared
Rulers — 2, at the ribbon station, for measuring ribbon by the foot
Pencils — 20, one per student for the tracking sheet and price tag
Board — teacher, for the list of reasons
Classroom clock — shared, students read start and end times

focus: *Simplifications:
Choose simplest craft (paper ornament, drawing card)
Copy the start and end times the teacher writes
No cost math for children: the teacher adds it on the board
Use concrete language: "took a long time" instead of "labor cost" Supports:
Pre-cut shapes for struggling cutters
Template to trace
Partner crafting for support
*Simplifications:
Simplified time tracking (start time, end time only)
Round numbers for cost (60¢ materials, $1.50 labor = $2.10 total)
Visual timer large and visible
Pre-filled worksheets with some data Supports:
Visual time tracking chart
Calculation helper on board (minutes × $0.10 = labor cost)
Partner for tricky steps (tying knots, counting beads)
*Simplifications:
Provide formula cards (Materials + Labor = Total Cost)
Simplified price list (fewer material options)
Calculator available
Template worksheet with examples Supports:
Detailed step-by-step tracking sheet
Visual examples of completed calculations
Station instructions with pictures
*Simplifications:
Formula reference cards available
Pre-made pricing strategy guide
Calculator for complex calculations
Reduce number of variables if overwhelming Supports:
Advanced cost tracking sheet with built-in formulas
Access to real store prices for comparison
Business planning worksheet

ell.label: English Language Learners
strategies: Hold up each material as you say its name and price: beads, felt, yarn, paper, glue.
Post the frame "I made ___. It took ___ minutes."
Show a finished sample of each craft before students start.

learningDifferences.label: Students with Learning Differences
strategies: Offer pre-cut felt shapes or a paper template to trace.
Let students write only start and end times; the teacher works out the minutes.
Pair students for tying knots and counting beads.

advanced.label: Advanced Students
strategies: Work out how long ten of the same item would take and what that time would cost.
Set a price that covers cost, then compare the profit on two different items.
Explain why a shop bracelet can cost $1, using time and how many a factory makes.

description.en: Read a short picture book or show images about Day of the Dead tradition. Discuss key concept: "People honor loved ones with priceless offerings—pictures of loved ones, favorite foods, treasured items". Introduce FL concept: Intrinsic Value * "Value that exists inside something, not based on money" * "Things that matter for what they ARE, not what they cost". Examples of priceless things: * People you love (can't buy family) * Memories (can't purchase experiences after they happen) * Cultural traditions (can't buy heritage) * Feelings (love, joy, connection). Students brainstorm: "What's priceless to you?" No book or images? Describe an ofrenda: pictures of loved ones, favorite foods, candles and paper marigolds.

sayThis.en: "Walk it in silence. Read every card. Then one note on one piece that isn't yours — say what you noticed, not whether you liked it."
sayThis.es: "Walk it in silence. Read every card. Then one note on one piece that isn't yours — say what you noticed, not whether you liked it."

doneWhen.en: Every piece has at least one note on it.
doneWhen.es: Every piece has at least one note on it.

watchFor.en: Notes going to friends only. Set the rule out loud: nobody's piece is left with nothing on it.
watchFor.es: Notes going to friends only. Set the rule out loud: nobody's piece is left with nothing on it.

description.en: Students walk through gallery silently, reading museum cards. Observe what classmates treasure. Notice diversity of priceless things. Appreciation activity: write a positive message in pencil on a sticky note and place it by the piece. No sticky notes? Use small squares of scrap paper set beside the piece.

discussionQuestions: What's priceless to you?
Why is this priceless? What does it represent?
Can you put a price on nature? Clean air? Friendship?
extensionIdeas: Give the artwork, or a thank-you note about it, to the person it honors.
Put the museum cards together into a class gallery guide to share with families.
Ask a family member what is priceless to them, and draw it beside your own piece.

beforeClass.en: Decide now how you'll handle a student whose priceless thing is somebody who died. Have a quiet word ready and a second theme they can take instead. Lay the materials out before the room comes in; this lesson should start calm.
beforeClass.es: Decide now how you'll handle a student whose priceless thing is somebody who died. Have a quiet word ready and a second theme they can take instead. Lay the materials out before the room comes in; this lesson should start calm.

runningLongOrShort.en: Long: cut the gallery setup to pushing two tables together. Short: add one line to the museum card — who else should see this, and why?
runningLongOrShort.es: Long: cut the gallery setup to pushing two tables together. Short: add one line to the museum card — who else should see this, and why?

focus: *Simplifications:
Simple drawing of one person or thing
Very short sentence (dictated or 2-3 words)
Focus on "special" rather than complex "intrinsic value"
Concrete language: "can't buy" instead of "priceless" Supports:
Teacher models: "I'm drawing my mom because she's special and I can't buy her at a store"
Sentence frame on board: "_____ is priceless to me"
Drawing support for struggling artists (start with circle for face, etc.)
*Simplifications:
Simplified museum card (title and one sentence)
Template with pictures to circle: "This is priceless because: ☐ I love them ☐ It's a memory ☐ It makes me happy"
Reduce writing demand, increase art time Supports:
Visual examples of finished artwork
Word bank for museum cards: love, memory, happy, special, family, friend, important
Sentence frames: "This artwork honors _____. It is priceless because _____."
Partner sharing before gallery walk Extensions:
*Simplifications:
Provide museum card template with sentence starters
Reduce number of reflection questions
Allow shorter artist statement Supports:
Examples of artist statements
Vocabulary word bank: intrinsic, value, priceless, treasure, honor, cherish, irreplaceable
Brainstorming worksheet before art creation
Small group discussion to develop ideas Extensions:
*Simplifications:
Provide formula/framework for artist statement
Allow use of visual instead of written artist statement
Reduce length requirements if overwhelming Supports:
Detailed museum card template with examples
Access to thesaurus for rich vocabulary
Small group philosophical discussion on value types
Teacher modeling of complex reflection Extensions:

ell.label: English Language Learners
strategies: Show the dollar and the photo side by side and say "can buy" and "can't buy" with a gesture for each.
Post the frame "___ is priceless because ___." with a word bank: love, memory, family, happy, special.
Let students write the title in their home language beside the English.

learningDifferences.label: Students with Learning Differences
strategies: Allow a spoken or dictated sentence instead of writing.
Give a museum card with only a title, a name and one line to finish.
Offer a quiet seat and a second theme for a student the topic upsets.

advanced.label: Advanced Students
strategies: Fill in the full museum card, including a market value answer with reasons.
Compare two things, one expensive but not priceless and one cheap but priceless, and explain the difference.
Write a short gallery guide saying what the class chose to honor.

description.en: Divide class into booth vendors and shoppers (will rotate) - Booth Types: * Handmade Crafts (items from CH10) * Art Gallery (items from CH11) * Paper Goods (paper treats drawn on index cards and cut out with scissors—discuss cost of goods) * Repair Shop (Diego-style—fix broken toys or sharpen pencils for fee). description.en: Assign roles: * Vendors (60% of class): run booths * Shoppers (30%): browse and buy * Market Managers (10%): help resolve issues, make change, support - Booth Setup by Category: * Handmade Crafts Booth (CH10 items): beaded jewelry, ornaments, cards * Art Gallery (CH11 items): memory art (some for sale, some priceless/display only) * Garden Produce Stand: shared garden items, drawn on index cards with crayons. No real food. * Paper Goods Booth (cost of goods): paper treats — cookies, cupcakes and pretzels drawn on index cards and cut out with scissors — each priced from what the card and the labor cost * Repair & Service Station (CH05): fix broken items, sharpen pencils, for fee (no broken items or sharpener? mend torn paper items with tape) * Trading Post (CH01): trade items without money. Vendors: * Price items (must justify: materials + labor, or fair trade value) * Arrange booth attractively * Create signs * Assign roles (cashier, sales, inventory).

description.en: Give each child a job: vendor, shopper or helper. Most children are vendors. Six booths: Handmade Crafts, Art Gallery, Garden Produce (drawn, no real food), Paper Goods (drawn paper treats), Repair Station (fix a broken or torn thing for a fee) and Trading Post (swap, no money). Vendors put a $1 or $5 price on each thing and give a short reason, like "it took a long time." Helpers help count coins.
description.es: Give each child a job: vendor, shopper or helper. Most children are vendors. Six booths: Handmade Crafts, Art Gallery, Garden Produce (drawn, no real food), Paper Goods (drawn paper treats), Repair Station (fix a broken or torn thing for a fee) and Trading Post (swap, no money). Vendors put a $1 or $5 price on each thing and give a short reason, like "it took a long time." Helpers help count coins.

sayThis.en: "Six booths: crafts, art, garden, paper goods, repairs and trading. Vendors, give each thing a price: $1 or $5. Tell me why, like 'it took a long time.' Shoppers, you get a turn at a booth too."
sayThis.es: "Six booths: crafts, art, garden, paper goods, repairs and trading. Vendors, give each thing a price: $1 or $5. Tell me why, like 'it took a long time.' Shoppers, you get a turn at a booth too."

watchFor.en: Prices with no reason. Ask one vendor per booth: why $1? Why $5?
watchFor.es: Prices with no reason. Ask one vendor per booth: why $1? Why $5?

doneWhen.en: Every booth has a sign, $1 or $5 prices and a named cashier.
doneWhen.es: Every booth has a sign, $1 or $5 prices and a named cashier.

sayThis.en: "Market's open. Shoppers — walk the whole market before you spend anything. Vendors, you can change your price whenever you like, but you'll have to say why at the close."
sayThis.es: "Market's open. Shoppers — walk the whole market before you spend anything. Vendors, you can change your price whenever you like, but you'll have to say why at the close."

doneWhen.en: Every booth has recorded at least one sale.
doneWhen.es: Every booth has recorded at least one sale.

watchFor.en: Shoppers spending everything at the first booth. Ring the bell at four minutes and move them along.
watchFor.es: Shoppers spending everything at the first booth. Ring the bell at four minutes and move them along.

description.en: Open market! Ring bell. Shoppers browse all booths. Make purchasing decisions. Vendors: * Sell items * Negotiate prices * Track inventory * Provide receipts. Market Managers circulate helping. Real market dynamics occur: * Some items sell out fast (demand!) * Perishables get discount as time passes (CH08) * Vendors adjust prices based on demand * Trades happen at Trading Post
description.es: Open market! Ring bell. Shoppers browse all booths. Make purchasing decisions. Vendors: * Sell items * Negotiate prices * Track inventory * Provide receipts. Market Managers circulate helping. Real market dynamics occur: * Some items sell out fast (demand!) * Perishables get discount as time passes (CH08) * Vendors adjust prices based on demand * Trades happen at Trading Post

description.en: Ring the bell to open. Shoppers look at every booth, then buy. Prices are $1 or $5. The shopper counts out coins, and the vendor counts them again. Vendors make a mark for each sale. Helpers walk around and help with counting. At the Trading Post, things are swapped, not bought.
description.es: Ring the bell to open. Shoppers look at every booth, then buy. Prices are $1 or $5. The shopper counts out coins, and the vendor counts them again. Vendors make a mark for each sale. Helpers walk around and help with counting. At the Trading Post, things are swapped, not bought.

sayThis.en: "Market's open! Shoppers, look at every booth before you buy. Count out your coins. Vendors, count them again and make a mark for each sale."
sayThis.es: "Market's open! Shoppers, look at every booth before you buy. Count out your coins. Vendors, count them again and make a mark for each sale."

watchFor.en: Shoppers spending everything at the first booth. Ring the bell at four minutes and move them along.
watchFor.es: Shoppers spending everything at the first booth. Ring the bell at four minutes and move them along.

doneWhen.en: Every booth has marked at least one sale.
doneWhen.es: Every booth has marked at least one sale.

sayThis.en: "Freeze. Crafts have sold out — that's demand. Garden is cutting prices, because those go off. The repair station has a queue. What does a queue tell you?"
sayThis.es: "Freeze. Crafts have sold out — that's demand. Garden is cutting prices, because those go off. The repair station has a queue. What does a queue tell you?"

doneWhen.en: Three market facts have been read out and the market is open again.
doneWhen.es: Three market facts have been read out and the market is open again.

watchFor.en: The pause turning into free time. Three announcements, then reopen.
watchFor.es: The pause turning into free time. Three announcements, then reopen.

description.en: Ring bell for brief pause. Quick announcements: * "Handmade Crafts Booth is sold out! High demand!" * "Garden Produce dropping prices—perishables!" * "Repair Station has a line—service in high demand!". Market insights create learning moments. Resume shopping
description.es: Ring bell for brief pause. Quick announcements: * "Handmade Crafts Booth is sold out! High demand!" * "Garden Produce dropping prices—perishables!" * "Repair Station has a line—service in high demand!". Market insights create learning moments. Resume shopping

sayThis.en: "Swap. Vendors are shoppers now. Before you go — one look at your stall. What sold? What didn't?"
sayThis.es: "Swap. Vendors are shoppers now. Before you go — one look at your stall. What sold? What didn't?"

doneWhen.en: Every booth has a new vendor and every former vendor is wearing a shopper badge.
doneWhen.es: Every booth has a new vendor and every former vendor is wearing a shopper badge.

watchFor.en: A slow swap eating into the second period. Count it down from ten.
watchFor.es: A slow swap eating into the second period. Count it down from ten.

description.en: Vendors and shoppers switch roles. Quick inventory: What sold? What didn't? Why?. Price adjustments for round 2
description.es: Vendors and shoppers switch roles. Quick inventory: What sold? What didn't? Why?. Price adjustments for round 2

sayThis.en: "Open. You watched the first round — use what you saw. If a price was wrong, change it."
sayThis.es: "Open. You watched the first round — use what you saw. If a price was wrong, change it."

doneWhen.en: Every booth has Period 2 sales recorded beside Period 1.
doneWhen.es: Every booth has Period 2 sales recorded beside Period 1.

watchFor.en: New vendors keeping the old prices out of politeness. Remind them the stall is theirs now.
watchFor.es: New vendors keeping the old prices out of politeness. Remind them the stall is theirs now.

description.en: Reopened market with role rotation. Apply learning from period 1. New vendors may price differently based on observations. Continued trading, buying, selling
description.es: Reopened market with role rotation. Apply learning from period 1. New vendors may price differently based on observations. Continued trading, buying, selling

sayThis.en: "Market's closed. Count your takings. Then tell me one thing you did today that you first learned in another chapter. The trading, the pricing, the repairs, the fresh-goods problem — all of it came from somewhere."
sayThis.es: "Market's closed. Count your takings. Then tell me one thing you did today that you first learned in another chapter. The trading, the pricing, the repairs, the fresh-goods problem — all of it came from somewhere."

doneWhen.en: Every booth's total is on the board and every award has been read out.
doneWhen.es: Every booth's total is on the board and every award has been read out.

watchFor.en: The answer stopping at "we sold stuff". Name one chapter yourself and let them take it from there.
watchFor.es: The answer stopping at "we sold stuff". Name one chapter yourself and let them take it from there.

description.en: Ring bell: "Market closing!". Vendors count revenue, complete tracking sheets. Shoppers review purchases - Whole-Class Discussion: * "What FL concepts did you use today?" * "What surprised you about running a market?" * "How did you decide what to buy/how to price?" * "What would you do differently next time?" - Award Ceremony (celebrating learning, not just profit): * "Best Negotiator" * "Fairest Trader" * "Most Creative Pricing" * "Kindest Vendor" * "Smartest Shopper" * Everyone gets participation certificate!
description.es: Ring bell: "Market closing!". Vendors count revenue, complete tracking sheets. Shoppers review purchases - Whole-Class Discussion: * "What FL concepts did you use today?" * "What surprised you about running a market?" * "How did you decide what to buy/how to price?" * "What would you do differently next time?" - Award Ceremony (celebrating learning, not just profit): * "Best Negotiator" * "Fairest Trader" * "Most Creative Pricing" * "Kindest Vendor" * "Smartest Shopper" * Everyone gets participation certificate!

description.en: Ring the bell: the market is closed. Vendors count their coins in piles of five. Shoppers show what they bought. Talk: What money lessons did you use today? What surprised you? Awards: Kindest Vendor, Fairest Trader, Smartest Shopper. Everyone gets a certificate!
description.es: Ring the bell: the market is closed. Vendors count their coins in piles of five. Shoppers show what they bought. Talk: What money lessons did you use today? What surprised you? Awards: Kindest Vendor, Fairest Trader, Smartest Shopper. Everyone gets a certificate!

sayThis.en: "Market's closed. Vendors, count your coins in fives. Then tell me one thing you did today that you learned in another story."
sayThis.es: "Market's closed. Vendors, count your coins in fives. Then tell me one thing you did today that you learned in another story."

watchFor.en: Counting taking too long. Help each booth make piles of five, and write each total on the board yourself.
watchFor.es: Counting taking too long. Help each booth make piles of five, and write each total on the board yourself.

doneWhen.en: Every booth's total is on the board and every award has been read out.
doneWhen.es: Every booth's total is on the board and every award has been read out.

discussionQuestions: What FL concepts did you use today?
What surprised you about running a market?
How did you decide what to buy/how to price?
What would you do differently next time?
extensionIdeas: Run a second market where half the booths trade only, with no money, and compare which way felt fairer.
Put every booth's total on the board and talk about why the top booth sold the most.
Invite another class to shop, and have vendors plan their stock and prices for more customers.

beforeClass.en: Check each booth has stock from its own chapter: crafts from Chapter 10, art from Chapter 11, garden produce drawn on index cards, paper goods cut and priced. No real food at any stall. Role badges written on scrap paper in a pile by the door. Give each shopper a $20 scrap-paper budget card and paper clips to use as coins.
beforeClass.es: Check each booth has stock from its own chapter: crafts from Chapter 10, art from Chapter 11, garden produce drawn on index cards, paper goods cut and priced. No real food at any stall. Role badges written on scrap paper in a pile by the door. Give each shopper a $20 scrap-paper budget card and paper clips to use as coins.

runningLongOrShort.en: Long: skip the rotation break and run one long market. Short: add a third period with one new rule — no money, trade only.
runningLongOrShort.es: Long: skip the rotation break and run one long market. Short: add a third period with one new rule — no money, trade only.

beforeClass.en: Check each booth has stock from its own chapter: crafts from Chapter 10, art from Chapter 11, garden produce drawn on scrap paper, paper goods torn out and priced. No real food at any stall. Role badges written on scrap paper in a pile by the door. Give each shopper a $20 scrap-paper budget card and scrap-paper coins.
beforeClass.es: Check each booth has stock from its own chapter: crafts from Chapter 10, art from Chapter 11, garden produce drawn on scrap paper, paper goods torn out and priced. No real food at any stall. Role badges written on scrap paper in a pile by the door. Give each shopper a $20 scrap-paper budget card and scrap-paper coins.

focus: *Simplifications:
Simplified market: everyone sells one item, buys one item
Round numbers only ($1, $5)
Teacher support for all transactions
Very simple tracking or none Supports:
Teacher or older buddy helps with transactions
Price tags pre-made or heavily supported
Visual cues: pictures for "buy" and "sell"
*Simplifications:
Simplified tracking sheet (just items and totals)
Pre-calculated prices available
Reduce number of booths/complexity
Pair students for support Supports:
Visual tracking sheets with pictures
Partner system: work in pairs as vendors
Step-by-step checklist for booth setup
*Simplifications:
Provide tracking sheet template
Allow calculator use
Reduce complexity: fewer booth types
Simplified award criteria Supports:
Detailed tracking worksheet with formulas
Examples of completed transactions
Small group booth teams with assigned roles
*Simplifications:
Provide formula reference cards
Reduce number of reflection questions
Allow digital tracking (spreadsheet) Supports:
Advanced tracking with built-in formulas
Access to calculators or spreadsheets
Small group vendor teams with clear leadership roles
Teacher modeling of sophisticated economic thinking

ell.label: English Language Learners
strategies: Put a picture sign on each booth and post the words buy, sell, price and change.
Post the frames "I'd like to buy your ___. How much?" and "It costs $___."
Let students point and hold up fingers for prices.

learningDifferences.label: Students with Learning Differences
strategies: Pair vendors so one sells and one keeps the sheet.
Use only $1 and $5 prices at that booth.
Give a tracking sheet with a box to tick for each sale.

advanced.label: Advanced Students
strategies: Keep a full sales record, then explain which booth earned the most and why.
Change one price in round two and compare sales before and after.
Serve as a Market Manager who settles price disputes and explains the fair answer.

items: Plain paper — 20 sheets, one per student for the dream product drawing
Pencils — 20, one per student, to write the product name

description.en: Go through checklist together. Raise hand if you can: draw, build things, cook/mix, garden, sew/craft, write stories, solve puzzles, organize things, come up with ideas, make people laugh. Students call out their top 2 skills.
description.es: Go through checklist together. Raise hand if you can: draw, build things, cook/mix, garden, sew/craft, write stories, solve puzzles, organize things, come up with ideas, make people laugh. Students call out their top 2 skills.

sayThis.en: "Hands up if you can draw. Hands up if you can build things. Keep going with me. Everyone can do something on this list."
sayThis.es: "Hands up if you can draw. Hands up if you can build things. Keep going with me. Everyone can do something on this list."

watchFor.en: A child who never raises a hand. Name something you saw them do today — "You stacked the chairs. That's organizing."
watchFor.es: A child who never raises a hand. Name something you saw them do today — "You stacked the chairs. That's organizing."

doneWhen.en: Every child has called out or pointed to two skills.
doneWhen.es: Every child has called out or pointed to two skills.

description.en: Go through a short list together: draw, build, cook, help, tell jokes. Five things, not ten. Children raise a hand for each one they can do, then each child names one skill. No writing.
description.es: Go through a short list together: draw, build, cook, help, tell jokes. Five things, not ten. Children raise a hand for each one they can do, then each child names one skill. No writing.

doneWhen.en: Every child has raised a hand at least once and said one skill out loud.
doneWhen.es: Every child has raised a hand at least once and said one skill out loud.

description.en: Draw ONE product you wish you could make. Name it. Show at least one picture.
description.es: Draw ONE product you wish you could make. Name it. Show at least one picture.

sayThis.en: "Draw one thing you wish you could make. Just one. Make it big. Then tell me its name."
sayThis.es: "Draw one thing you wish you could make. Just one. Make it big. Then tell me its name."

watchFor.en: Kids drawing lots of little things. Point and ask "Which one is best?" and have them make that one big.
watchFor.es: Kids drawing lots of little things. Point and ask "Which one is best?" and have them make that one big.

doneWhen.en: Every paper has one product on it and every child can say its name.
doneWhen.es: Every paper has one product on it and every child can say its name.

description.en: Draw ONE product you wish you could make with crayons. Make it big. Say its name out loud. No writing needed.
description.es: Draw ONE product you wish you could make with crayons. Make it big. Say its name out loud. No writing needed.

sayThis.en: "Draw one thing you wish you could make. Just one. Make it big. Then tell me its name. You don't have to write it."
sayThis.es: "Draw one thing you wish you could make. Just one. Make it big. Then tell me its name. You don't have to write it."

watchFor.en: Kids drawing lots of little things. Point and ask "Which one is best?" and have them draw that one big.
watchFor.es: Kids drawing lots of little things. Point and ask "Which one is best?" and have them draw that one big.

doneWhen.en: Every child has one big drawing and can say its name.
doneWhen.es: Every child has one big drawing and can say its name.

description.en: Turn to partner. Show your drawing. Say: "I want to make a ___."
description.es: Turn to partner. Show your drawing. Say: "I want to make a ___."

sayThis.en: "Turn to your partner. Hold up your picture. Say: I want to make a ... Then switch."
sayThis.es: "Turn to your partner. Hold up your picture. Say: I want to make a ... Then switch."

watchFor.en: One partner talking both turns. At one minute, say "Switch."
watchFor.es: One partner talking both turns. At one minute, say "Switch."

doneWhen.en: Every child has said "I want to make a ___" to a partner.
doneWhen.es: Every child has said "I want to make a ___" to a partner.

discussionQuestions: What can you already do?
What would you like to make someday?
Who would want to buy your product?

beforeClass.en: Write the ten skills on the board so you can point at each one. Put paper, pencils and crayons on every table.
beforeClass.es: Write the ten skills on the board so you can point at each one. Put paper, pencils and crayons on every table.

runningLongOrShort.en: Long: in Skills Check, skip the call-outs and go straight to Dream Product Draw. Short: in Quick Share, let two or three kids show their drawing to the whole class.
runningLongOrShort.es: Long: in Skills Check, skip the call-outs and go straight to Dream Product Draw. Short: in Quick Share, let two or three kids show their drawing to the whole class.

30.activityName: Skills Inventory & Dream Product Design Card

fromScratch.costPerStudent: $0 — everything is free or from home

description.en: Complete worksheet with guidance. For each category, check off things you can do. Count your skills in each category. Circle your top 2 categories — these are your "maker strengths."
description.es: Complete worksheet with guidance. For each category, check off things you can do. Count your skills in each category. Circle your top 2 categories — these are your "maker strengths."

sayThis.en: "Here are seven kinds of making. In each one, check off every thing you can do. Count your checks. Circle the two groups with the most. Those are your maker strengths."
sayThis.es: "Here are seven kinds of making. In each one, check off every thing you can do. Count your checks. Circle the two groups with the most. Those are your maker strengths."

watchFor.en: Kids leaving things unchecked because they think "can do" means "do really well." Say "If you've done it once, check it."
watchFor.es: Kids leaving things unchecked because they think "can do" means "do really well." Say "If you've done it once, check it."

doneWhen.en: Every sheet has checks, a count for each group and two circles.
doneWhen.es: Every sheet has checks, a count for each group and two circles.

description.en: Teacher shows/discusses 5-6 maker products: painted mugs, sewn pouches, built birdhouses, knitted hats, handmade cards, organized kits. Point out which skills each uses.
description.es: Teacher shows/discusses 5-6 maker products: painted mugs, sewn pouches, built birdhouses, knitted hats, handmade cards, organized kits. Point out which skills each uses.

sayThis.en: "Somebody made this painted mug. What skill did they use? Art. Now this birdhouse — what skill?"
sayThis.es: "Somebody made this painted mug. What skill did they use? Art. Now this birdhouse — what skill?"

watchFor.en: Talk drifting to who has one at home. Ask "What skill made it?" and move to the next one.
watchFor.es: Talk drifting to who has one at home. Ask "What skill made it?" and move to the next one.

doneWhen.en: Five or six products are shown, each with a skill named out loud.
doneWhen.es: Five or six products are shown, each with a skill named out loud.

description.en: On your design card, a sheet of plain paper, draw your dream product. Include: product name, what it does/who uses it, which of YOUR skills you'd use to make it, and simple price guess.
description.es: On your design card, a sheet of plain paper, draw your dream product. Include: product name, what it does/who uses it, which of YOUR skills you'd use to make it, and simple price guess.

sayThis.en: "Draw your dream product on your card. Add four things: its name, who uses it, which of your skills you'd use, and a price guess."
sayThis.es: "Draw your dream product on your card. Add four things: its name, who uses it, which of your skills you'd use, and a price guess."

watchFor.en: Prices like a million dollars. Ask "Would a grown-up you know pay that?" and let them change it.
watchFor.es: Prices like a million dollars. Ask "Would a grown-up you know pay that?" and let them change it.

doneWhen.en: Every card has a drawing, a name, a user, a skill and a price.
doneWhen.es: Every card has a drawing, a name, a user, a skill and a price.

description.en: Post designs around room. Students walk around viewing others' ideas. Return to seats and share one product you'd want to buy from a classmate.
description.es: Post designs around room. Students walk around viewing others' ideas. Return to seats and share one product you'd want to buy from a classmate.

sayThis.en: "Tape your card up. Walk and look with your hands behind your back. Back in your seat, tell us one thing you'd buy from a friend."
sayThis.es: "Tape your card up. Walk and look with your hands behind your back. Back in your seat, tell us one thing you'd buy from a friend."

watchFor.en: A crowd at one card. Keep them moving: "Look at three, then sit."
watchFor.es: A crowd at one card. Keep them moving: "Look at three, then sit."

doneWhen.en: Every card is on the wall and a few kids have named one they'd buy.
doneWhen.es: Every card is on the wall and a few kids have named one they'd buy.

discussionQuestions: What skills are you already good at?
What skills would you like to learn this season?
How can your skills become a product?
What makes a good product idea?
Who would be your customer?
