fromScratch.costPerStudent: $0 — everything is free or from home
fromScratch.description: Plain paper and pencils for the inventory, design and pitch, magazine photos or handmade objects from home, and a timer for the pitches.
items: Plain paper — 20 sheets, one per student for the skills inventory, ideas, design and pitch
Pencils — 20, one per student, for rating, sketching and writing
Magazine photos of maker products — 5 or 6 torn from old magazines, or 2 or 3 real handmade objects from home, free, for the product review
Board — teacher, for the ten skill areas and the pitch frame
Clock or phone timer — teacher, to time the 30-second pitches

basicClassroom.costPerStudent: $0 — uses supplies the school already has
basicClassroom.description: Plain paper and pencils for the inventory, design and pitch, magazine photos or handmade objects from home, and a timer for the pitches.
items: Plain paper — 20 sheets, one per student for the skills inventory, ideas, design and pitch
Pencils — 20, one per student, for rating, sketching and writing
Magazine photos of maker products — 5 or 6 torn from old magazines, or 2 or 3 real handmade objects from home, free, for the product review
Board — teacher, for the ten skill areas and the pitch frame
Clock or phone timer — teacher, to time the 30-second pitches

sayThis.en: "Ten kinds of making on the board. Score yourself one to five in every single one. One means you've never tried it. Five means people ask you to do it for them. Be honest — a low score is information, not a failure. Then circle your best three."
sayThis.es: "Ten kinds of making on the board. Score yourself one to five in every single one. One means you've never tried it. Five means people ask you to do it for them. Be honest — a low score is information, not a failure. Then circle your best three."

doneWhen.en: Every sheet has a number in all ten rows and three circled.
doneWhen.es: Every sheet has a number in all ten rows and three circled.

watchFor.en: Students scoring themselves one all the way down. Ask what they did last weekend and find the skill hiding inside it.
watchFor.es: Students scoring themselves one all the way down. Ask what they did last weekend and find the skill hiding inside it.

description.en: Complete detailed inventory across categories: Visual Arts, Construction/Building, Culinary Arts, Textile/Sewing, Writing/Storytelling, Music/Performance, Organization/Planning, Problem-Solving, Technology/Digital, Nature/Gardening - Rate yourself 1-5 in each (1=beginner, 5=expert) - Calculate your top 3 skill areas - Write one sentence: "I am a maker who is good at ___, ___, and ___."
description.es: Complete detailed inventory across categories: Visual Arts, Construction/Building, Culinary Arts, Textile/Sewing, Writing/Storytelling, Music/Performance, Organization/Planning, Problem-Solving, Technology/Digital, Nature/Gardening - Rate yourself 1-5 in each (1=beginner, 5=expert) - Calculate your top 3 skill areas - Write one sentence: "I am a maker who is good at ___, ___, and ___."

description.en: Read the ten skill areas on the board one at a time. Children raise a hand for every skill they have. Then each child tells a partner the one they do best.
description.es: Read the ten skill areas on the board one at a time. Children raise a hand for every skill they have. Then each child tells a partner the one they do best.

sayThis.en: "I'll read ten kinds of making. Raise your hand for every one you can do. Then turn to your partner and say: The thing I do best is ___."
sayThis.es: "I'll read ten kinds of making. Raise your hand for every one you can do. Then turn to your partner and say: The thing I do best is ___."

watchFor.en: A child who never raises a hand. Name something you saw them make or do today and find the skill inside it.
watchFor.es: A child who never raises a hand. Name something you saw them make or do today and find the skill inside it.

doneWhen.en: Every child has raised a hand at least once and told a partner their best skill.
doneWhen.es: Every child has raised a hand at least once and told a partner their best skill.

sayThis.en: "Five ideas. Not five good ones — five. Bad ideas are how you get to the good one. Then cross out four."
sayThis.es: "Five ideas. Not five good ones — five. Bad ideas are how you get to the good one. Then cross out four."

doneWhen.en: Every sheet shows five ideas with four crossed out.
doneWhen.es: Every sheet shows five ideas with four crossed out.

watchFor.en: Students stopping at one idea and defending it. Hold the line at five before anybody chooses.
watchFor.es: Students stopping at one idea and defending it. Hold the line at five before anybody chooses.

description.en: Review example products that use skills similar to yours - Brainstorm 5 possible products you could make using your skills - Choose the ONE you're most excited about
description.es: Review example products that use skills similar to yours - Brainstorm 5 possible products you could make using your skills - Choose the ONE you're most excited about

description.en: Look at the maker objects or magazine photos together. Each child draws two or three quick ideas for things they could make, then circles the one they like best.
description.es: Look at the maker objects or magazine photos together. Each child draws two or three quick ideas for things they could make, then circles the one they like best.

sayThis.en: "Draw two or three things you could make. Quick little drawings. Now circle your favorite."
sayThis.es: "Draw two or three things you could make. Quick little drawings. Now circle your favorite."

watchFor.en: Children stuck on one idea. Ask "What else could you make?" and let them draw one more.
watchFor.es: Children stuck on one idea. Ask "What else could you make?" and let them draw one more.

doneWhen.en: Every child has two or three small drawings with one circled.
doneWhen.es: Every child has two or three small drawings with one circled.

sayThis.en: "Draw it from two sides, not one. Give it a name. Then three answers: what it does, who needs it, what you'd charge. Last line — what would you have to learn to actually make this?"
sayThis.es: "Draw it from two sides, not one. Give it a name. Then three answers: what it does, who needs it, what you'd charge. Last line — what would you have to learn to actually make this?"

doneWhen.en: Every design has a name, two drawings, a named customer and a price.
doneWhen.es: Every design has a name, two drawings, a named customer and a price.

watchFor.en: Drawings with no materials named. Ask what it's made of and where that comes from.
watchFor.es: Drawings with no materials named. Ask what it's made of and where that comes from.

description.en: Sketch your product from multiple angles - Name it (be creative!) - Write description: What is it? What does it do? Who needs it? - Identify target customer (age, interests, why they'd buy it) - Estimate: Materials needed, time to make one, price you'd charge - Note: What skills do you already have? What would you need to learn?
description.es: Sketch your product from multiple angles - Name it (be creative!) - Write description: What is it? What does it do? Who needs it? - Identify target customer (age, interests, why they'd buy it) - Estimate: Materials needed, time to make one, price you'd charge - Note: What skills do you already have? What would you need to learn?

description.en: Draw your product big. Tell a partner its name and who it is for. No writing needed.
description.es: Draw your product big. Tell a partner its name and who it is for. No writing needed.

sayThis.en: "Draw the thing you picked. Make it big. Tell your partner its name and who would use it."
sayThis.es: "Draw the thing you picked. Make it big. Tell your partner its name and who would use it."

watchFor.en: Drawings with no name yet. Ask "What is it called?" and let them say it out loud.
watchFor.es: Drawings with no name yet. Ask "What is it called?" and let them say it out loud.

doneWhen.en: Every child has a drawing and has told a partner its name and who it is for.
doneWhen.es: Every child has a drawing and has told a partner its name and who it is for.

sayThis.en: "Thirty seconds. Who you are, what you're good at, what you made, who it's for. Then stop. Thirty seconds is shorter than you think, and I'm timing it."
sayThis.es: "Thirty seconds. Who you are, what you're good at, what you made, who it's for. Then stop. Thirty seconds is shorter than you think, and I'm timing it."

doneWhen.en: Every student has pitched to a partner and at least six have pitched to the room.
doneWhen.es: Every student has pitched to a partner and at least six have pitched to the room.

watchFor.en: Pitches that describe the drawing instead of the customer. Ask "who buys it?" once, mid-pitch.
watchFor.es: Pitches that describe the drawing instead of the customer. Ask "who buys it?" once, mid-pitch.

description.en: Using the pitch frame on the board, write a 30-second pitch: "Hi, I'm [name]. I'm a maker who can [skills]. I designed [product] for people who [need]. I'm excited to make this because [reason]." - Practice with partner - 6-8 volunteers present to class while you time each one on a clock or phone timer.
description.es: Using the pitch frame on the board, write a 30-second pitch: "Hi, I'm [name]. I'm a maker who can [skills]. I designed [product] for people who [need]. I'm excited to make this because [reason]." - Practice with partner - 6-8 volunteers present to class while you time each one on a clock or phone timer.

description.en: Say the pitch out loud with the frame on the board: "Hi, I'm ___. I made ___. It is for ___." No writing. Practice with a partner, then a few volunteers say it to the class while you time them on a clock or phone timer.
description.es: Say the pitch out loud with the frame on the board: "Hi, I'm ___. I made ___. It is for ___." No writing. Practice with a partner, then a few volunteers say it to the class while you time them on a clock or phone timer.

sayThis.en: "Say it with me: Hi, I'm blank. I made blank. It is for blank. Say it to your partner. Then who wants to say it to everyone?"
sayThis.es: "Say it with me: Hi, I'm blank. I made blank. It is for blank. Say it to your partner. Then who wants to say it to everyone?"

watchFor.en: Children who freeze. Say the first words with them and let them finish.
watchFor.es: Children who freeze. Say the first words with them and let them finish.

doneWhen.en: Every child has said the pitch to a partner and a few have said it to the class.
doneWhen.es: Every child has said the pitch to a partner and a few have said it to the class.

sayThis.en: "One compliment each, and it has to be about the product, not the person. Then finish the line on your sheet: after today, I'm excited to make blank."
sayThis.es: "One compliment each, and it has to be about the product, not the person. Then finish the line on your sheet: after today, I'm excited to make blank."

doneWhen.en: Every presenter has had one compliment and every sheet's last line is filled.
doneWhen.es: Every presenter has had one compliment and every sheet's last line is filled.

watchFor.en: "It was good" as the compliment. Ask what was good about it.
watchFor.es: "It was good" as the compliment. Ask what was good about it.

description.en: Classmates give one compliment per pitch - Self-reflection: "After today, I'm excited to make ___."
description.es: Classmates give one compliment per pitch - Self-reflection: "After today, I'm excited to make ___."

discussionQuestions: How did identifying your skills help you think of product ideas?
What's the difference between a skill and a product?
Why do different people have different maker skills?
If you don't have all the skills yet, can you still be a maker? (YES!)
How do you turn an idea into something you can actually make?
What makes a product worth buying?
extensionIdeas: Create digital "Maker Profile" posters to display
Research real makers in your community and their skills
Start a "Skill Swap" where students teach each other (art kid teaches drawing, building kid teaches construction)
Interview family members about their making skills
Create season-long "Learning Goals" based on skills you want to develop

beforeClass.en: Write the ten skill areas and the pitch frame on the board before anyone walks in; reading them off a sheet costs three minutes. Put plain paper and pencils on every table. Put two or three real maker objects from home where they can be seen — a painted mug, a sewn pouch, a handmade card. No real ones? Use magazine photos.
beforeClass.es: Write the ten skill areas and the pitch frame on the board before anyone walks in; reading them off a sheet costs three minutes. Put plain paper and pencils on every table. Put two or three real maker objects from home where they can be seen — a painted mug, a sewn pouch, a handmade card. No real ones? Use magazine photos.

runningLongOrShort.en: Long: take pitches from four volunteers instead of eight. Short: add a second pitch round where partners pitch each other's product.
runningLongOrShort.es: Long: take pitches from four volunteers instead of eight. Short: add a second pitch round where partners pitch each other's product.

focus: Simple verbal skills checklist with teacher guidance
Draw one picture of something they can make (no text required)
Say one skill out loud instead of writing it
Share with partner instead of whole class
Basic vocabulary: make, build, draw, create
Skills checklist with checkmarks and a count per group
Design card includes a name, who uses it and a price guess
Name one of your own skills the product would use
Gallery walk, then name one product you would buy
Vocabulary expansion: skill, product, maker, customer, design
Full skills inventory with written responses
Product design includes sketch, name, purpose, and customer
Practice explaining ideas to others
Brainstorm five product ideas, then keep one
Vocabulary: brainstorm, sketch, target customer, pitch, price
Comprehensive skills assessment with self-rating
Detailed product design with materials list and price estimate
Formal elevator pitch with business language
Consider learning curve: "What do I need to learn to make this real?"
Advanced vocabulary: inventory, rating, target customer, elevator pitch, estimate

ell.label: English Language Learners
strategies: Draw a small picture beside each skill word on the board so kids can match word to picture.
Give the pitch frame: "I can ___. I want to make ___. It is for ___."
Let the dream product be a drawing with a one-word label, and pair the student with a partner who shares their language for the share.

learningDifferences.label: Students with Learning Differences
strategies: Hand out the skills list as tick boxes so no one has to write skills out.
Scribe the product name, customer and price while the student draws.
Let a student share or pitch to you alone instead of the whole room.

advanced.label: Advanced Students
strategies: Design three products and pick the one that is easiest to really make, with a reason.
List the materials the dream product needs and guess what each costs.
Write what you would have to learn to make it, and how you would learn it.

20.label: 20 Minutes

fromScratch.costPerStudent: $0 — everything is free or from home
fromScratch.description: Free samples from home and the recycling bin, books for weight, a cup of water, scrap-paper price and budget cards, plain paper, pencils and tape for the builds.
items: Cardboard, fabric scraps, foil, plastic container lids, wood scraps, packaging foam and rubber bands — one of each per station (4 stations) plus a small pile per team (5 teams) for the builds, all from home or recycled, free
Clean glass jar — 1, teacher holds it, from the recycling bin, free; shown, not tested
Books — 3 or 4 textbooks from the class shelf, already in the room, the weight for the strength test
Water in a paper cup, with an old towel — 1 cup for the water station, cup and towel from home, free
Plain paper — 20 sheets, one per student for guesses, data sheet, chart and reflection
Pencils — 20, one per student, for guesses, results and the reflection
Masking tape — 1 roll, shared by the teams, to join the builds
Scrap paper — 13 pieces, teacher writes 8 price cards and 5 team budget cards (Tier 1: 8 pieces, price cards only, no team budget cards)

basicClassroom.costPerStudent: $0 — uses supplies the school already has
basicClassroom.description: Samples from the supply closet and recycling bin, books for weight, a cup of water, index-card price and budget cards, plain paper, pencils and tape for the builds.
items: Cardboard, fabric scraps, foil, plastic container lids, wood scraps or craft sticks, packaging foam and rubber bands — one of each per station (4 stations) plus a small pile per team (5 teams) for the builds
Clean glass jar — 1, teacher holds it, from the recycling bin, free; shown, not tested
Books — 3 or 4 textbooks from the class shelf, already in the room, the weight for the strength test
Water in a paper cup, with an old towel — 1 cup for the water station, cup and towel from home, free
Plain paper — 20 sheets, one per student for guesses, data sheet, chart and reflection
Pencils — 20, one per student, for guesses, results and the reflection
Masking tape — 1 roll, shared by the teams, to join the builds
Index cards — 13, teacher writes 8 price cards and 5 team budget cards (Tier 1: 8 cards, price cards only, no team budget cards)

description.en: Present 6-8 different materials (wood, cardboard, fabric, plastic, metal, foam, rubber, glass). Students predict which is strongest, most flexible, most expensive.
description.es: Present 6-8 different materials (wood, cardboard, fabric, plastic, metal, foam, rubber, glass). Students predict which is strongest, most flexible, most expensive.

sayThis.en: "Look at these materials. Which one is strongest? Which bends the most? Which costs the most? Point to your guess."
sayThis.es: "Look at these materials. Which one is strongest? Which bends the most? Which costs the most? Point to your guess."

watchFor.en: Kids grabbing the samples. Keep them on your tray until every guess is made.
watchFor.es: Kids grabbing the samples. Keep them on your tray until every guess is made.

doneWhen.en: Every child has pointed to a guess for all three questions.
doneWhen.es: Every child has pointed to a guess for all three questions.

description.en: Put out four materials only: wood, cloth, metal, foam. Children point to the one they think is strongest. One question, not three.
description.es: Put out four materials only: wood, cloth, metal, foam. Children point to the one they think is strongest. One question, not three.

sayThis.en: "Look at these four things. Which one is strongest? Point to your guess."
sayThis.es: "Look at these four things. Which one is strongest? Point to your guess."

doneWhen.en: Every child is pointing at one material.
doneWhen.es: Every child is pointing at one material.

description.en: Rotate through stations testing: strength (weight bearing), flexibility (bending), water resistance (drops), texture (touch sorting). Record results on data sheets.
description.es: Rotate through stations testing: strength (weight bearing), flexibility (bending), water resistance (drops), texture (touch sorting). Record results on data sheets.

sayThis.en: "Four stations. Press it, bend it, drip on it, touch it. Mark what happened, then move when I clap."
sayThis.es: "Four stations. Press it, bend it, drip on it, touch it. Mark what happened, then move when I clap."

watchFor.en: Groups breaking the samples. Say before they start: "Test gently. The next group needs it too."
watchFor.es: Groups breaking the samples. Say before they start: "Test gently. The next group needs it too."

doneWhen.en: Every data sheet has a mark for all four stations.
doneWhen.es: Every data sheet has a mark for all four stations.

description.en: Rotate through the four stations: press it, bend it, drip on it, touch it. At each station, draw a smile if the material held up and a frown if it did not. No writing.
description.es: Rotate through the four stations: press it, bend it, drip on it, touch it. At each station, draw a smile if the material held up and a frown if it did not. No writing.

sayThis.en: "Four stations. Press it, bend it, drip on it, touch it. Draw a smile or a frown for each one. Move when I clap."
sayThis.es: "Four stations. Press it, bend it, drip on it, touch it. Draw a smile or a frown for each one. Move when I clap."

watchFor.en: Groups breaking the samples. Say before they start: "Test gently. The next group needs it too."
watchFor.es: Groups breaking the samples. Say before they start: "Test gently. The next group needs it too."

doneWhen.en: Every data sheet has a smile or a frown for all four stations.
doneWhen.es: Every data sheet has a smile or a frown for all four stations.

description.en: Using simple price cards, students discover what each material costs. Create a chart comparing properties vs. cost. Which material gives the best value for different purposes?
description.es: Using simple price cards, students discover what each material costs. Create a chart comparing properties vs. cost. Which material gives the best value for different purposes?

sayThis.en: "Turn over the price cards. Put each price next to its material. Which one is strong and cheap?"
sayThis.es: "Turn over the price cards. Put each price next to its material. Which one is strong and cheap?"

watchFor.en: Kids thinking the most costly one is best. Point at a cheap one that did well at the stations.
watchFor.es: Kids thinking the most costly one is best. Point at a cheap one that did well at the stations.

doneWhen.en: Every material on the chart has a price next to it.
doneWhen.es: Every material on the chart has a price next to it.

description.en: Turn over the price cards. Put each price card next to its material. Point to the one that costs the least, then to one that is cheap and did well at the stations.
description.es: Turn over the price cards. Put each price card next to its material. Point to the one that costs the least, then to one that is cheap and did well at the stations.

sayThis.en: "Turn over the price cards. Put each price next to its material. Which one costs the least? Which one is cheap and strong?"
sayThis.es: "Turn over the price cards. Put each price next to its material. Which one costs the least? Which one is cheap and strong?"

watchFor.en: Kids thinking the one that costs the most is best. Point at a cheap one that did well at the stations.
watchFor.es: Kids thinking the one that costs the most is best. Point at a cheap one that did well at the stations.

doneWhen.en: Every price card sits next to its material and every child has pointed to the cheapest one.
doneWhen.es: Every price card sits next to its material and every child has pointed to the cheapest one.

description.en: Teams choose materials to build a simple structure (bridge, container, or shelter) within a budget. Must justify material choices based on test results and cost.
description.es: Teams choose materials to build a simple structure (bridge, container, or shelter) within a budget. Must justify material choices based on test results and cost.

sayThis.en: "Build a bridge, a box or a shelter. Stay inside your budget card. Be ready to say why you picked one thing."
sayThis.es: "Build a bridge, a box or a shelter. Stay inside your budget card. Be ready to say why you picked one thing."

watchFor.en: Teams spending the whole budget on the first material. Ask "What's left for the rest?"
watchFor.es: Teams spending the whole budget on the first material. Ask "What's left for the rest?"

doneWhen.en: Every team has a build and has not spent past its budget card.
doneWhen.es: Every team has a build and has not spent past its budget card.

description.en: Each team picks three materials and builds a bridge, a box or a shelter, joining it with tape. Each team gets ready to say one reason for one choice.
description.es: Each team picks three materials and builds a bridge, a box or a shelter, joining it with tape. Each team gets ready to say one reason for one choice.

sayThis.en: "Pick three materials. Build a bridge, a box or a shelter. Be ready to tell us why you picked one of them."
sayThis.es: "Pick three materials. Build a bridge, a box or a shelter. Be ready to tell us why you picked one of them."

watchFor.en: Teams grabbing every material. Say "Three things only."
watchFor.es: Teams grabbing every material. Say "Three things only."

doneWhen.en: Every team has a build made of three materials and one reason to share.
doneWhen.es: Every team has a build made of three materials and one reason to share.

description.en: Each team presents their design, explaining why they chose specific materials. Class votes on best value design. Discuss trade-offs between quality and cost.
description.es: Each team presents their design, explaining why they chose specific materials. Class votes on best value design. Discuss trade-offs between quality and cost.

sayThis.en: "Show your build. Tell us one thing you picked and why. Then we vote: which one did the job for the least money?"
sayThis.es: "Show your build. Tell us one thing you picked and why. Then we vote: which one did the job for the least money?"

watchFor.en: Votes going to the prettiest build. Say the rule again before hands go up.
watchFor.es: Votes going to the prettiest build. Say the rule again before hands go up.

doneWhen.en: Every team has shown its build and the vote is counted.
doneWhen.es: Every team has shown its build and the vote is counted.

description.en: Each team shows its build. The class votes with hands for the one that did the job.
description.es: Each team shows its build. The class votes with hands for the one that did the job.

sayThis.en: "Show your build. Tell us one thing you used. Hands up for the one that did the job best."
sayThis.es: "Show your build. Tell us one thing you used. Hands up for the one that did the job best."

watchFor.en: Votes going to the prettiest build. Ask "Which one did the job?" before hands go up.
watchFor.es: Votes going to the prettiest build. Ask "Which one did the job?" before hands go up.

doneWhen.en: Every team has shown its build and the class has voted.
doneWhen.es: Every team has shown its build and the class has voted.

description.en: Write or draw: What material surprised you most? Why do manufacturers choose different materials for different products?
description.es: Write or draw: What material surprised you most? Why do manufacturers choose different materials for different products?

sayThis.en: "Draw or write the material that surprised you. Why did it surprise you?"
sayThis.es: "Draw or write the material that surprised you. Why did it surprise you?"

watchFor.en: Blank papers. A drawing counts as a full answer.
watchFor.es: Blank papers. A drawing counts as a full answer.

doneWhen.en: Every paper has a drawing or words on it.
doneWhen.es: Every paper has a drawing or words on it.

description.en: Draw the material that surprised you. Tell a partner what it did.
description.es: Draw the material that surprised you. Tell a partner what it did.

sayThis.en: "Draw the material that surprised you. Then tell your partner what it did."
sayThis.es: "Draw the material that surprised you. Then tell your partner what it did."

watchFor.en: Blank papers. Ask "Which one did something you did not expect?" and let them draw it.
watchFor.es: Blank papers. Ask "Which one did something you did not expect?" and let them draw it.

doneWhen.en: Every child has a drawing and has told a partner about it.
doneWhen.es: Every child has a drawing and has told a partner about it.

discussionQuestions: Which material feels the hardest?
Which is the lightest?
What could you make with wood?

Write a price card for each material and a budget card for each team on index cards. Put plain paper and pencils on every table and a roll of masking tape out for the builds.
beforeClass.es: Set up four stations: a stack of books, samples to bend, a paper cup of water with a towel, and a touch pile. Hold up a clean glass jar yourself; it is shown, not tested. Write a price card for each material and a budget card for each team on index cards. Put plain paper and pencils on every table and a roll of masking tape out for the builds.

runningLongOrShort.en: Long: in Presentations & Analysis, have two teams present and skip the vote. Short: in Reflection, have kids share their answer with a partner too.
runningLongOrShort.es: Long: in Presentations & Analysis, have two teams present and skip the vote. Short: in Reflection, have kids share their answer with a partner too.

beforeClass.en: Set up four stations: a stack of books, samples to bend, a paper cup of water with a towel, and a touch pile. Hold up a clean glass jar yourself; it is shown, not tested. beforeClass.es: Set up four stations: a stack of books, samples to bend, a paper cup of water with a towel, and a touch pile. Hold up a clean glass jar yourself; it is shown, not tested. description.en: Teacher shows careful folding technique. Emphasize: "Watch closely. Precision matters."
description.es: Teacher shows careful folding technique. Emphasize: "Watch closely. Precision matters."

sayThis.en: "Watch my hands. I line up the corners. I press the fold flat. I go slow. Careful folds come out right."
sayThis.es: "Watch my hands. I line up the corners. I press the fold flat. I go slow. Careful folds come out right."

watchFor.en: Kids folding along before you finish. Papers stay flat on the desk until you say go.
watchFor.es: Kids folding along before you finish. Papers stay flat on the desk until you say go.

doneWhen.en: You have shown every fold once.
doneWhen.es: You have shown every fold once.

description.en: The teacher folds one paper slowly, three folds only. Line up the corners, press flat. Use the word careful, not precision.
description.es: The teacher folds one paper slowly, three folds only. Line up the corners, press flat. Use the word careful, not precision.

description.en: Students follow instructions to fold paper into specific shape (paper airplane, origami cup, or simple box). Teacher circulates, doesn't intervene.
description.es: Students follow instructions to fold paper into specific shape (paper airplane, origami cup, or simple box). Teacher circulates, doesn't intervene.

sayThis.en: "Now you fold. Corners together, press flat, one step at a time. I'm watching, but I won't help."
sayThis.es: "Now you fold. Corners together, press flat, one step at a time. I'm watching, but I won't help."

watchFor.en: Kids asking you to fix theirs. Say "Do your best. We'll look at them together."
watchFor.es: Kids asking you to fix theirs. Say "Do your best. We'll look at them together."

doneWhen.en: Every child has a finished fold, right or wrong.
doneWhen.es: Every child has a finished fold, right or wrong.

description.en: Children make the same three folds on their own paper. A simple hat or a fan, not a box. The teacher walks around and does not fold for them.
description.es: Children make the same three folds on their own paper. A simple hat or a fan, not a box. The teacher walks around and does not fold for them.

sayThis.en: "Now your turn. Corners together. Press it flat. Go slow. I will watch, but your hands do the folding."
sayThis.es: "Now your turn. Corners together. Press it flat. Go slow. I will watch, but your hands do the folding."

description.en: Hold up results. Compare to teacher's model. How many match exactly? Discuss what happened when steps were rushed or folds were off.
description.es: Hold up results. Compare to teacher's model. How many match exactly? Discuss what happened when steps were rushed or folds were off.

sayThis.en: "Hold yours up next to mine. Does it match? Where is it different?"
sayThis.es: "Hold yours up next to mine. Does it match? Where is it different?"

watchFor.en: Kids laughing at crooked ones. Say "Crooked shows us where the fold went wrong. That helps."
watchFor.es: Kids laughing at crooked ones. Say "Crooked shows us where the fold went wrong. That helps."

doneWhen.en: Every fold is held up and a few kids have said where theirs went off.
doneWhen.es: Every fold is held up and a few kids have said where theirs went off.

description.en: Children hold their fold up next to the teacher's. Ask one thing only: does it match, yes or no. Skip the talk about rushing.
description.es: Children hold their fold up next to the teacher's. Ask one thing only: does it match, yes or no. Skip the talk about rushing.

sayThis.en: "Hold yours up next to mine. Does it match? Yes or no."
sayThis.es: "Hold yours up next to mine. Does it match? Yes or no."

doneWhen.en: Every child has held a fold up and said yes or no.
doneWhen.es: Every child has held a fold up and said yes or no.

description.en: "What happens if you don't measure/fold carefully?" Connect to: carpenters can't unfold wood once it's cut.
description.es: "What happens if you don't measure/fold carefully?" Connect to: carpenters can't unfold wood once it's cut.

sayThis.en: "You can open paper and fold it again. If a carpenter cuts wood wrong, can they fix it? No. So what should they do first?"
sayThis.es: "You can open paper and fold it again. If a carpenter cuts wood wrong, can they fix it? No. So what should they do first?"

watchFor.en: Kids saying "just fix it after." Say "Fixes show. The buyer can see them."
watchFor.es: Kids saying "just fix it after." Say "Fixes show. The buyer can see them."

doneWhen.en: Kids can say "go slow" or "check first."
doneWhen.es: Kids can say "go slow" or "check first."

description.en: Show that paper opens back up and can be folded again. Then say wood cannot. Ask one question: should the carpenter go fast or slow? Skip the part about buyers.
description.es: Show that paper opens back up and can be folded again. Then say wood cannot. Ask one question: should the carpenter go fast or slow? Skip the part about buyers.

sayThis.en: "Paper opens back up. You can fold it again. Wood cannot. If you cut it wrong, it stays wrong. So should the carpenter go fast or slow?"
sayThis.es: "Paper opens back up. You can fold it again. Wood cannot. If you cut it wrong, it stays wrong. So should the carpenter go fast or slow?"

watchFor.en: Children shouting fast because fast sounds fun. Hold up a crooked fold and ask if going fast made it better.
watchFor.es: Children shouting fast because fast sounds fun. Hold up a crooked fold and ask if going fast made it better.

doneWhen.en: The class has said slow out loud together.
doneWhen.es: The class has said slow out loud together.

discussionQuestions: Did your paper look like the example?
What happened if you folded in the wrong place?
Can you unfold and start over with paper? Can you with wood?

beforeClass.en: Fold one model ahead of time — a paper cup is the quickest — and keep it to hold up. Put one sheet of paper on every desk.
beforeClass.es: Fold one model ahead of time — a paper cup is the quickest — and keep it to hold up. Put one sheet of paper on every desk.

runningLongOrShort.en: Long: in Comparison, hold up five papers instead of everyone's. Short: in Reflection, also ask what each child would do differently on a second try.
runningLongOrShort.es: Long: in Comparison, hold up five papers instead of everyone's. Short: in Reflection, also ask what each child would do differently on a second try.

30.label: 30 Minutes

fromScratch.costPerStudent: $0 — everything is free or from home
fromScratch.description: Plain paper for the measuring strips, the rectangles and the Tier 1 templates, pencils, and a recycled box for the waste. Kids measure with the strip and fold and tear instead of cutting.
items: Plain paper — 30 sheets: 5 for 20 measuring strips, 1 per student for the rectangle, 5 for Tier 1 templates (Tier 1: 25 sheets, no measuring strips)
Pencils — 20, one per student, to mark lines on the strips and the rectangle
Box — 1 from the recycling bin, free, to collect scraps
Board — teacher, for the target size and the count of accurate rectangles

basicClassroom.costPerStudent: $0 — uses supplies the school already has
basicClassroom.description: Cardboard from flattened boxes, rulers, pencils, safety scissors, a recycled box for the waste and the board for the target size.
items: Cardboard — 25 sheets from flattened shipping boxes, free: 1 per student for the rectangle, 5 for Tier 1 templates
Rulers — 20, one per student, to measure and check
Safety scissors — 20, one per student, to cut the rectangle
Pencils — 20, one per student, to mark the cutting lines
Box — 1 from the recycling bin, free, to collect scraps
Board — teacher, for the target size and the count of accurate rectangles

description.en: Show template with measurements. Students must create exact rectangle by measuring and cutting. Review ruler use. Emphasize: "Measure twice, cut once."
description.es: Show template with measurements. Students must create exact rectangle by measuring and cutting. Review ruler use. Emphasize: "Measure twice, cut once."

sayThis.en: "Your rectangle is 4 inches by 6 inches. Put the zero on your ruler at the edge. Measure twice, cut once. Nobody cuts until I check."
sayThis.es: "Your rectangle is 4 inches by 6 inches. Put the zero on your ruler at the edge. Measure twice, cut once. Nobody cuts until I check."

watchFor.en: Kids starting at the 1 instead of the 0. Hold up your ruler and point to the zero.
watchFor.es: Kids starting at the 1 instead of the 0. Hold up your ruler and point to the zero.

doneWhen.en: Every student can point to the zero on their ruler.
doneWhen.es: Every student can point to the zero on their ruler.

description.en: Show the target rectangle with its size in units. Students must make an exact rectangle by measuring with the measuring strip, folding and tearing. Review how to use the strip. Emphasize: "Measure twice, cut once."
description.es: Show the target rectangle with its size in units. Students must make an exact rectangle by measuring with the measuring strip, folding and tearing. Review how to use the strip. Emphasize: "Measure twice, cut once."

sayThis.en: "Your rectangle is 3 units by 5 units. Each space between two lines on your strip is one unit. Put the end of the strip right at the edge of the paper. Measure twice, cut once. Nobody tears until I check."
sayThis.es: "Your rectangle is 3 units by 5 units. Each space between two lines on your strip is one unit. Put the end of the strip right at the edge of the paper. Measure twice, cut once. Nobody tears until I check."

watchFor.en: Kids starting from the first pencil line instead of the end of the strip. Hold up your strip and point to the end.
watchFor.es: Kids starting from the first pencil line instead of the end of the strip. Hold up your strip and point to the end.

doneWhen.en: Every student can point to the end of their strip and count out 3 units.
doneWhen.es: Every student can point to the end of their strip and count out 3 units.

description.en: Students measure carefully and mark cutting lines on cardboard. Teacher checks measurements before anyone cuts.
description.es: Students measure carefully and mark cutting lines on cardboard. Teacher checks measurements before anyone cuts.

sayThis.en: "Measure 4 inches. Make a dot. Measure again. Now 6 inches. Join the dots with the ruler. Hands up when you're ready for me to check."
sayThis.es: "Measure 4 inches. Make a dot. Measure again. Now 6 inches. Join the dots with the ruler. Hands up when you're ready for me to check."

watchFor.en: Lines drawn without the ruler. Have them lay the ruler down and draw along it.
watchFor.es: Lines drawn without the ruler. Have them lay the ruler down and draw along it.

doneWhen.en: Every sheet has four lines you have checked.
doneWhen.es: Every sheet has four lines you have checked.

description.en: Students measure carefully with the measuring strip and mark the lines on their paper with a pencil. Teacher checks the marks before anyone tears.
description.es: Students measure carefully with the measuring strip and mark the lines on their paper with a pencil. Teacher checks the marks before anyone tears.

sayThis.en: "Count 3 units from the end. Make a dot. Measure again. Now 5 units. Join the dots along the edge of the strip. Hands up when you're ready for me to check."
sayThis.es: "Count 3 units from the end. Make a dot. Measure again. Now 5 units. Join the dots along the edge of the strip. Hands up when you're ready for me to check."

watchFor.en: Lines drawn freehand. Have them lay the strip down and draw along its edge.
watchFor.es: Lines drawn freehand. Have them lay the strip down and draw along its edge.

description.en: Lay the template on your sheet and trace around it with a pencil. No measuring.
description.es: Lay the template on your sheet and trace around it with a pencil. No measuring.

sayThis.en: "Put the template flat on your sheet. Hold it still with one hand. Trace all the way around with your pencil."
sayThis.es: "Put the template flat on your sheet. Hold it still with one hand. Trace all the way around with your pencil."

watchFor.en: Templates sliding while kids trace. Have a partner hold it down.
watchFor.es: Templates sliding while kids trace. Have a partner hold it down.

doneWhen.en: Every sheet has a traced rectangle with four closed corners.
doneWhen.es: Every sheet has a traced rectangle with four closed corners.

description.en: Students cut along marked lines.
description.es: Students cut along marked lines.

sayThis.en: "Cut right on the line, slowly. Turn the cardboard, not the scissors. Scraps go in the box."
sayThis.es: "Cut right on the line, slowly. Turn the cardboard, not the scissors. Scraps go in the box."

watchFor.en: Scissors drifting off the line at corners. Stop, turn the cardboard, start again on the line.
watchFor.es: Scissors drifting off the line at corners. Stop, turn the cardboard, start again on the line.

doneWhen.en: Every student has a cut rectangle and their scraps are in the box.
doneWhen.es: Every student has a cut rectangle and their scraps are in the box.

description.en: Students fold hard along each marked line, then tear slowly along the crease.
description.es: Students fold hard along each marked line, then tear slowly along the crease.

sayThis.en: "Fold right on the line and press the crease flat. Fold it back the other way and press again. Then tear slowly along the crease. Scraps go in the box."
sayThis.es: "Fold right on the line and press the crease flat. Fold it back the other way and press again. Then tear slowly along the crease. Scraps go in the box."

watchFor.en: Tears drifting off the crease. Stop, press the fold again, and tear in small pulls.
watchFor.es: Tears drifting off the crease. Stop, press the fold again, and tear in small pulls.

doneWhen.en: Every student has a torn rectangle and their scraps are in the box.
doneWhen.es: Every student has a torn rectangle and their scraps are in the box.

description.en: Measure finished rectangles. Award "Precision Points" for pieces within 1/4 inch of target. Display results: how many were accurate?
description.es: Measure finished rectangles. Award "Precision Points" for pieces within 1/4 inch of target. Display results: how many were accurate?

sayThis.en: "Swap with a partner. Measure their rectangle. Within a quarter inch of 4 by 6 gets a Precision Point."
sayThis.es: "Swap with a partner. Measure their rectangle. Within a quarter inch of 4 by 6 gets a Precision Point."

watchFor.en: Partners arguing over a tiny gap. You make the call and move on.
watchFor.es: Partners arguing over a tiny gap. You make the call and move on.

doneWhen.en: Every rectangle is measured and the count of accurate ones is on the board.
doneWhen.es: Every rectangle is measured and the count of accurate ones is on the board.

description.en: Measure finished rectangles with the measuring strip. Award "Precision Points" when every edge lands on its line; torn edges are rough, so an edge touching the line counts. Display results: how many were accurate?
description.es: Measure finished rectangles with the measuring strip. Award "Precision Points" when every edge lands on its line; torn edges are rough, so an edge touching the line counts. Display results: how many were accurate?

sayThis.en: "Swap with a partner. Lay the strip along each side. If the edges land on the 3 line and the 5 line, that's a Precision Point."
sayThis.es: "Swap with a partner. Lay the strip along each side. If the edges land on the 3 line and the 5 line, that's a Precision Point."

description.en: Lay the template on top of your rectangle and check if the edges match. A rectangle whose edges line up gets a Precision Point.
description.es: Lay the template on top of your rectangle and check if the edges match. A rectangle whose edges line up gets a Precision Point.

sayThis.en: "Put the template on top of your rectangle. Do the edges line up? If they do, that's a Precision Point."
sayThis.es: "Put the template on top of your rectangle. Do the edges line up? If they do, that's a Precision Point."

watchFor.en: Kids pushing the template to make it fit. Line up one corner first, then look.
watchFor.es: Kids pushing the template to make it fit. Line up one corner first, then look.

doneWhen.en: Every rectangle has been checked with the template and the count of matching ones is on the board.
doneWhen.es: Every rectangle has been checked with the template and the count of matching ones is on the board.

description.en: Show pile of scrap cardboard. "This is waste. If cardboard costs $1 per sheet and we wasted 30% making mistakes, we spent $0.30 extra. In a business, that adds up." Calculate class waste.
description.es: Show pile of scrap cardboard. "This is waste. If cardboard costs $1 per sheet and we wasted 30% making mistakes, we spent $0.30 extra. In a business, that adds up." Calculate class waste.

sayThis.en: "Look at the scrap box. We paid for every piece in it. If one sheet costs one dollar, how much did we throw away?"
sayThis.es: "Look at the scrap box. We paid for every piece in it. If one sheet costs one dollar, how much did we throw away?"

watchFor.en: Kids thinking scrap is free. Hold up a scrap and ask what the whole sheet cost.
watchFor.es: Kids thinking scrap is free. Hold up a scrap and ask what the whole sheet cost.

doneWhen.en: The class has counted the waste and said out loud what it cost.
doneWhen.es: The class has counted the waste and said out loud what it cost.

description.en: Show the pile of torn paper. "This is waste. If paper costs $1 per sheet and we wasted 30% making mistakes, we spent $0.30 extra. In a business, that adds up." Calculate class waste.
description.es: Show the pile of torn paper. "This is waste. If paper costs $1 per sheet and we wasted 30% making mistakes, we spent $0.30 extra. In a business, that adds up." Calculate class waste.

description.en: Show the box of scraps. Count the scrap pieces together. Every piece came from a sheet we paid for.
description.es: Show the box of scraps. Count the scrap pieces together. Every piece came from a sheet we paid for.

sayThis.en: "Let's count the scraps together. We paid for every piece. If one sheet costs one dollar, did we throw money away?"
sayThis.es: "Let's count the scraps together. We paid for every piece. If one sheet costs one dollar, did we throw money away?"

watchFor.en: Kids thinking scrap is free. Hold up a scrap and ask what the whole sheet cost.
watchFor.es: Kids thinking scrap is free. Hold up a scrap and ask what the whole sheet cost.

doneWhen.en: The class has counted the scraps and said out loud that waste costs money.
doneWhen.es: The class has counted the scraps and said out loud that waste costs money.

discussionQuestions: How many got the exact measurements?
What mistakes did you make?
How much cardboard did we waste?
If you were selling these, would mistakes cost you money?
extensionIdeas: Build simple box from measured cardboard pieces—precision matters for fit.

beforeClass.en: Write the target size on the board — for example, 4 inches by 6 inches — and draw the rectangle. Put a ruler, pencil, safety scissors and one cardboard sheet at each seat, with a box from the recycling bin at the front for scraps.
beforeClass.es: Write the target size on the board — for example, 4 inches by 6 inches — and draw the rectangle. Put a ruler, pencil, safety scissors and one cardboard sheet at each seat, with a box from the recycling bin at the front for scraps.

runningLongOrShort.en: Long: in Quality Check, measure five pieces as a class instead of every piece. Short: in Waste Discussion, have kids measure and cut a second rectangle from their scrap.
runningLongOrShort.es: Long: in Quality Check, measure five pieces as a class instead of every piece. Short: in Waste Discussion, have kids measure and cut a second rectangle from their scrap.

beforeClass.en: Write the target size on the board — 4 inches by 6 inches — and draw the rectangle. Cut one 4-by-6-inch cardboard template per table for tracing. Put a ruler, pencil, safety scissors and one cardboard sheet at each seat, with a box from the recycling bin at the front for scraps.
beforeClass.es: Write the target size on the board — 4 inches by 6 inches — and draw the rectangle. Cut one 4-by-6-inch cardboard template per table for tracing. Put a ruler, pencil, safety scissors and one cardboard sheet at each seat, with a box from the recycling bin at the front for scraps.

beforeClass.en: Make 20 measuring strips: fold 5 sheets of plain paper in half lengthwise twice, tear along the folds into 4 long strips each, then fold each strip in half three times, open it and draw a pencil line on every crease. Every strip now has 8 equal units, and every strip matches because every sheet is the same size. Write the target size on the board — 3 units by 5 units — and draw the rectangle. Put a measuring strip, a pencil and one sheet of plain paper at each seat, with a box from the recycling bin at the front for scraps.
beforeClass.es: Make 20 measuring strips: fold 5 sheets of plain paper in half lengthwise twice, tear along the folds into 4 long strips each, then fold each strip in half three times, open it and draw a pencil line on every crease. Every strip now has 8 equal units, and every strip matches because every sheet is the same size. Write the target size on the board — 3 units by 5 units — and draw the rectangle. Put a measuring strip, a pencil and one sheet of plain paper at each seat, with a box from the recycling bin at the front for scraps.

runningLongOrShort.en: Long: in Quality Check, measure five pieces as a class instead of every piece. Short: in Waste Discussion, have kids measure and tear a second rectangle from their scrap.
runningLongOrShort.es: Long: in Quality Check, measure five pieces as a class instead of every piece. Short: in Waste Discussion, have kids measure and tear a second rectangle from their scrap.

beforeClass.en: Make 20 measuring strips: fold 5 sheets of plain paper in half lengthwise twice, tear along the folds into 4 long strips each, then fold each strip in half three times, open it and draw a pencil line on every crease. Every strip now has 8 equal units, and every strip matches because every sheet is the same size. Write the target size on the board — 3 units by 5 units — and draw the rectangle. Tear one 3-by-5-unit paper template per table for tracing. Put a measuring strip, a pencil and one sheet of plain paper at each seat, with a box from the recycling bin at the front for scraps.
beforeClass.es: Make 20 measuring strips: fold 5 sheets of plain paper in half lengthwise twice, tear along the folds into 4 long strips each, then fold each strip in half three times, open it and draw a pencil line on every crease. Every strip now has 8 equal units, and every strip matches because every sheet is the same size. Write the target size on the board — 3 units by 5 units — and draw the rectangle. Tear one 3-by-5-unit paper template per table for tracing. Put a measuring strip, a pencil and one sheet of plain paper at each seat, with a box from the recycling bin at the front for scraps.

fromScratch.costPerStudent: $0 — everything is free or from home
fromScratch.description: Plain paper for the measuring strips, the sheets teams buy and the Tier 1 templates, scrap paper for cards and plans, pencils and tape. Teams measure with the strip and fold and tear instead of cutting.
items: Plain paper — 35 sheets: 5 for 20 measuring strips, 25 to sell at $2 each (up to 5 per team, 5 teams), 5 for Tier 1 templates
Scrap paper — 15 pieces, 3 per team for the budget card, the cutting plan and the waste tally
Pencils — 10, two per team, to mark lines and write the card and tally

Board — teacher, for the build spec and the class results

basicClassroom.costPerStudent: $0 — uses supplies the school already has
basicClassroom.description: Cardboard from flattened boxes, rulers, scissors, pencils, tape, scrap paper for cards and plans, and the board for the spec.
items: Cardboard — 30 sheets from flattened shipping boxes, free: 25 to sell at $2 each (up to 5 per team, 5 teams), 5 for Tier 1 templates
Rulers — 10, two per team, to measure and inspect
Scissors — 10, two per team, plus the teacher's to cut the sheets
Pencils — 10, two per team, to mark lines and write the card and tally
Masking tape — 2 rolls, shared by the 5 teams, to join the box
Scrap paper — 15 pieces, 3 per team for the budget card, the cutting plan and the waste tally
Board — teacher, for the build spec and the class results

sayThis.en: "Ten dollars on your card. Cardboard is two dollars a sheet. Here's exactly the size you're building. Every mistake costs another sheet, and another two dollars. Measure twice, cut once. Today that isn't a saying, it's the rules."
sayThis.es: "Ten dollars on your card. Cardboard is two dollars a sheet. Here's exactly the size you're building. Every mistake costs another sheet, and another two dollars. Measure twice, cut once. Today that isn't a saying, it's the rules."

doneWhen.en: Every team has $10 written on its card and the spec copied down.
doneWhen.es: Every team has $10 written on its card and the spec copied down.

watchFor.en: Teams treating the money as pretend. Say plainly what happens at zero: you stop building.
watchFor.es: Teams treating the money as pretend. Say plainly what happens at zero: you stop building.

description.en: Each team writes $10 at the top of a scrap-paper budget card; Cardboard costs $2 per sheet, crossed off the card at purchase; Challenge: Build structure to exact specifications (e.g., box that's 5"x5"x3"); Every mistake = buy new materials = less left on the card; Goal: Build to spec with minimal waste
description.es: Each team writes $10 at the top of a scrap-paper budget card; Cardboard costs $2 per sheet, crossed off the card at purchase; Challenge: Build structure to exact specifications (e.g., box that's 5"x5"x3"); Every mistake = buy new materials = less left on the card; Goal: Build to spec with minimal waste

description.en: Each team writes $10 at the top of a scrap-paper budget card; Paper costs $2 per sheet, crossed off the card at purchase; Challenge: Build an open-top paper tray to exact specifications (3 units by 3 units by 2 units on the measuring strip); Every mistake = buy new materials = less left on the card; Goal: Build to spec with minimal waste
description.es: Each team writes $10 at the top of a scrap-paper budget card; Paper costs $2 per sheet, crossed off the card at purchase; Challenge: Build an open-top paper tray to exact specifications (3 units by 3 units by 2 units on the measuring strip); Every mistake = buy new materials = less left on the card; Goal: Build to spec with minimal waste

sayThis.en: "Ten dollars on your card. Paper is two dollars a sheet. Here's exactly the size you're building: 3 units by 3 units by 2 units on your strip. Every mistake costs another sheet, and another two dollars. Measure twice, cut once. Today that isn't a saying, it's the rules."
sayThis.es: "Ten dollars on your card. Paper is two dollars a sheet. Here's exactly the size you're building: 3 units by 3 units by 2 units on your strip. Every mistake costs another sheet, and another two dollars. Measure twice, cut once. Today that isn't a saying, it's the rules."

sayThis.en: "Nothing gets cut until I've seen the plan. Draw the sheet, draw your cuts on it, count your pieces. Fit them so the scraps come out small."
sayThis.es: "Nothing gets cut until I've seen the plan. Draw the sheet, draw your cuts on it, count your pieces. Fit them so the scraps come out small."

doneWhen.en: Every team's cutting diagram has your approval before materials are handed out.
doneWhen.es: Every team's cutting diagram has your approval before materials are handed out.

watchFor.en: Plans with no measurements on them. Send it back once. That's cheaper than a wasted sheet.
watchFor.es: Plans with no measurements on them. Send it back once. That's cheaper than a wasted sheet.

description.en: Teams plan their cuts on paper first; Calculate how many pieces needed and measurements; Draw cutting diagram to minimize waste; Teacher approves plan before materials are distributed
description.es: Teams plan their cuts on paper first; Calculate how many pieces needed and measurements; Draw cutting diagram to minimize waste; Teacher approves plan before materials are distributed

sayThis.en: "Nothing gets torn until I've seen the plan. Draw the sheet, draw your tear lines on it, count your pieces. Fit them so the leftover bits come out small."
sayThis.es: "Nothing gets torn until I've seen the plan. Draw the sheet, draw your tear lines on it, count your pieces. Fit them so the leftover bits come out small."

description.en: Each team lays its five templates on a sheet and moves them around until every piece fits. The teacher checks the plan before the team pays for the sheet and traces.
description.es: Each team lays its five templates on a sheet and moves them around until every piece fits. The teacher checks the plan before the team pays for the sheet and traces.

sayThis.en: "Put all five templates on the sheet. Move them around until they all fit. Show me before you trace."
sayThis.es: "Put all five templates on the sheet. Move them around until they all fit. Show me before you trace."

watchFor.en: Templates hanging off the edge. Ask "Does every piece fit on the sheet?"
watchFor.es: Templates hanging off the edge. Ask "Does every piece fit on the sheet?"

doneWhen.en: Every team has shown you all five pieces fitting on one sheet.
doneWhen.es: Every team has shown you all five pieces fitting on one sheet.

sayThis.en: "Measure, mark, then cut. Every scrap goes in your own pile, not the bin — we're measuring and counting the waste at the end. I'm not going to help. That's on purpose."
sayThis.es: "Measure, mark, then cut. Every scrap goes in your own pile, not the bin — we're measuring and counting the waste at the end. I'm not going to help. That's on purpose."

doneWhen.en: Every team has a built structure and its own pile of scrap on the desk.
doneWhen.es: Every team has a built structure and its own pile of scrap on the desk.

watchFor.en: Your own urge to step in when a team cuts wrong. Don't. Note it and let them buy another sheet.
watchFor.es: Your own urge to step in when a team cuts wrong. Don't. Note it and let them buy another sheet.

description.en: Teams measure carefully, mark, and cut; Track every piece of waste on worksheet; Build structure according to specs; Teacher circulates, doesn't help—mistakes are learning.
description.es: Teams measure carefully, mark, and cut; Track every piece of waste on worksheet; Build structure according to specs; Teacher circulates, doesn't help—mistakes are learning.

description.en: Teams measure carefully with the measuring strip, mark, fold hard on each line and tear along the crease; Track every piece of waste on worksheet; Tape the pieces together according to specs; Teacher circulates, doesn't help—mistakes are learning.
description.es: Teams measure carefully with the measuring strip, mark, fold hard on each line and tear along the crease; Track every piece of waste on worksheet; Tape the pieces together according to specs; Teacher circulates, doesn't help—mistakes are learning.

sayThis.en: "Measure, mark, fold, then tear. Every leftover bit goes in your own pile, not the bin — we're measuring and counting the waste at the end. I'm not going to help. That's on purpose."
sayThis.es: "Measure, mark, fold, then tear. Every leftover bit goes in your own pile, not the bin — we're measuring and counting the waste at the end. I'm not going to help. That's on purpose."

doneWhen.en: Every team has a taped tray and its own pile of torn waste on the desk.
doneWhen.es: Every team has a taped tray and its own pile of torn waste on the desk.

description.en: Trace each template onto your sheet with a pencil, then cut on the lines. Tape the pieces together to make the box. The teacher does not help.
description.es: Trace each template onto your sheet with a pencil, then cut on the lines. Tape the pieces together to make the box. The teacher does not help.

sayThis.en: "Trace around each template. Cut right on the line, slowly. Then tape your box together. Try it yourselves — that's the challenge."
sayThis.es: "Trace around each template. Cut right on the line, slowly. Then tape your box together. Try it yourselves — that's the challenge."

watchFor.en: Your own urge to step in. Let them try, and let them buy another sheet if a piece goes wrong.
watchFor.es: Your own urge to step in. Let them try, and let them buy another sheet if a piece goes wrong.

doneWhen.en: Every team has a taped box and its own pile of waste.
doneWhen.es: Every team has a taped box and its own pile of waste.

description.en: Trace each template onto your sheet with a pencil, fold hard on each line and tear slowly along the crease. Tape the pieces together to make the tray. The teacher does not help.
description.es: Trace each template onto your sheet with a pencil, fold hard on each line and tear slowly along the crease. Tape the pieces together to make the tray. The teacher does not help.

sayThis.en: "Trace around each template. Fold on the line, press it flat, then tear slowly. Then tape your tray together. Try it yourselves — that's the challenge."
sayThis.es: "Trace around each template. Fold on the line, press it flat, then tear slowly. Then tape your tray together. Try it yourselves — that's the challenge."

doneWhen.en: Every team has a taped tray and its own pile of waste.
doneWhen.es: Every team has a taped tray and its own pile of waste.

sayThis.en: "Ruler on it. Within a quarter inch is full points. Everything gets measured, every team's."
sayThis.es: "Ruler on it. Within a quarter inch is full points. Everything gets measured, every team's."

doneWhen.en: Every structure has a measured score written on it and its scrap tallied.
doneWhen.es: Every structure has a measured score written on it and its scrap tallied.

watchFor.en: Teams measuring their own work and rounding kindly. Swap the builds so nobody inspects their own.
watchFor.es: Teams measuring their own work and rounding kindly. Swap the builds so nobody inspects their own.

description.en: Measure finished structures against specs; Award "precision points" for accuracy (within 1/4 inch = full points); Calculate waste: measure scrap pieces, tally total.
description.es: Measure finished structures against specs; Award "precision points" for accuracy (within 1/4 inch = full points); Calculate waste: measure scrap pieces, tally total.

description.en: Measure finished trays against specs with the measuring strip; Award "precision points" for accuracy (every edge on its line = full points); Calculate waste: measure scrap pieces, tally total.
description.es: Measure finished trays against specs with the measuring strip; Award "precision points" for accuracy (every edge on its line = full points); Calculate waste: measure scrap pieces, tally total.

sayThis.en: "Strip on it. Every edge on its line is full points. Everything gets measured, every team's."
sayThis.es: "Strip on it. Every edge on its line is full points. Everything gets measured, every team's."

description.en: Swap builds with another team. Lay the templates on each side and check if the edges match. Every matching side gets a point.
description.es: Swap builds with another team. Lay the templates on each side and check if the edges match. Every matching side gets a point.

sayThis.en: "Put the template on each side. Do the edges line up? Give a point for every side that matches."
sayThis.es: "Put the template on each side. Do the edges line up? Give a point for every side that matches."

watchFor.en: Teams being kind to their friends. You make the call when it's close.
watchFor.es: Teams being kind to their friends. You make the call when it's close.

doneWhen.en: Every build has its points counted and written on it.
doneWhen.es: Every build has its points counted and written on it.

sayThis.en: "How much did you spend? How much scrap have you got? Both numbers go on the board. The team that hit the spec and spent least is the team that made money."
sayThis.es: "How much did you spend? How much scrap have you got? Both numbers go on the board. The team that hit the spec and spent least is the team that made money."

doneWhen.en: Every team's spend and waste percentage is on the class graph.
doneWhen.es: Every team's spend and waste percentage is on the class graph.

watchFor.en: Waste being treated as a joke. Point at the money: every one of those scraps was part of a two-dollar sheet.
watchFor.es: Waste being treated as a joke. Point at the money: every one of those scraps was part of a two-dollar sheet.

description.en: Calculate cost: materials purchased, waste generated; If structure meets specs with minimal waste = "profit"; If excessive waste or structure doesn't meet specs = "loss"; Graph class results: waste % vs. success rate.
description.es: Calculate cost: materials purchased, waste generated; If structure meets specs with minimal waste = "profit"; If excessive waste or structure doesn't meet specs = "loss"; Graph class results: waste % vs. success rate.

description.en: Count the sheets each team bought and the waste pieces in each pile. The team that matched the templates and bought the fewest sheets did best.
description.es: Count the sheets each team bought and the waste pieces in each pile. The team that matched the templates and bought the fewest sheets did best.

sayThis.en: "How many sheets did you buy? Let's count your waste pieces. Both numbers go on the board. Who matched and bought the fewest sheets?"
sayThis.es: "How many sheets did you buy? Let's count your waste pieces. Both numbers go on the board. Who matched and bought the fewest sheets?"

watchFor.en: Waste being treated as a joke. Every piece came from a two-dollar sheet.
watchFor.es: Waste being treated as a joke. Every piece came from a two-dollar sheet.

doneWhen.en: Every team's sheets and waste pieces are counted and on the board.
doneWhen.es: Every team's sheets and waste pieces are counted and on the board.

discussionQuestions: "What was your biggest challenge in measuring precisely?"
"How much material did you waste? What did that cost?"
"If you could do it again, what would you change?"
"How does precision affect profit in real businesses?"
"Why do builders and carpenters measure so carefully?"
"What's the difference between 'good enough' and 'exact'?"
extensionIdeas: Second round with same challenge—track improvement
Design your own structure and create specs for others to build
Calculate % waste across class—what's acceptable? What's too much?
Research: how do real factories minimize waste?
Visit hardware store to price materials and understand real costs

focus: Simple folding or single-cut challenges
Visual templates with clear pictures

ell.label: English Language Learners
strategies: Show each move — ruler at zero, dot, line, cut — with your hands before you say it.
Draw the target shape on the board with the numbers on its sides.
Give the frame "I measured ___ inches. I need to cut ___."

learningDifferences.label: Students with Learning Differences
strategies: Give a pre-marked line or a template to trace, so the student practices cutting, not measuring.
Put a sticker on the ruler's zero and on the target inch mark.
Pair the student with a partner who holds the ruler still while they mark.

advanced.label: Advanced Students
strategies: Write your own build spec and trade it with another team to build.
Work out what the waste would cost if every sheet cost twice as much.
Find a cutting plan that gets the most pieces from one sheet, and prove it with a drawing.

description.en: Discuss packaging: protects product, makes it attractive, tells information. Show examples of good packaging. Explain design challenge: create package for a simple product.
description.es: Discuss packaging: protects product, makes it attractive, tells information. Show examples of good packaging. Explain design challenge: create package for a simple product.

sayThis.en: "A package does three jobs. It keeps the thing safe. It makes it look nice. It tells you what's inside. Look at this box — what does it tell you?"
sayThis.es: "A package does three jobs. It keeps the thing safe. It makes it look nice. It tells you what's inside. Look at this box — what does it tell you?"

watchFor.en: Kids reading every word on the box. Pick one thing it tells you and move on.
watchFor.es: Kids reading every word on the box. Pick one thing it tells you and move on.

doneWhen.en: The class has named the three jobs.
doneWhen.es: The class has named the three jobs.

description.en: Hold up one box. Name two jobs only: it keeps the thing safe, and it makes it look nice. Skip the job about telling you what is inside.
description.es: Hold up one box. Name two jobs only: it keeps the thing safe, and it makes it look nice. Skip the job about telling you what is inside.

sayThis.en: "A box has two jobs. It keeps the thing safe. It makes it look nice. Look at this box. Does it look nice?"
sayThis.es: "A box has two jobs. It keeps the thing safe. It makes it look nice. Look at this box. Does it look nice?"

watchFor.en: Children who all want to hold the box. Walk it around the circle once, then put it on the shelf.
watchFor.es: Children who all want to hold the box. Walk it around the circle once, then put it on the shelf.

doneWhen.en: The class has said the two jobs out loud together.
doneWhen.es: The class has said the two jobs out loud together.

description.en: Students choose a simple product to package (real or pretend): toy, craft, pretend snack. Sketch package ideas. Plan: What shape? What information? What colors? How to make it attractive?
description.es: Students choose a simple product to package (real or pretend): toy, craft, pretend snack. Sketch package ideas. Plan: What shape? What information? What colors? How to make it attractive?

sayThis.en: "Pick one thing to put in a package. It can be real or pretend. Draw some ideas. What shape? What colors? What words go on it?"
sayThis.es: "Pick one thing to put in a package. It can be real or pretend. Draw some ideas. What shape? What colors? What words go on it?"

watchFor.en: Kids who can't pick a product. Offer three: a toy, a pretend cookie, a pencil.
watchFor.es: Kids who can't pick a product. Offer three: a toy, a pretend cookie, a pencil.

doneWhen.en: Every child has picked a product and drawn at least one package idea.
doneWhen.es: Every child has picked a product and drawn at least one package idea.

description.en: Pick a product to put in a package, real or pretend: a toy, a craft or a pretend snack. Draw it with crayons and say one color you will use.
description.es: Pick a product to put in a package, real or pretend: a toy, a craft or a pretend snack. Draw it with crayons and say one color you will use.

sayThis.en: "Pick one thing to put in a package. It can be real or pretend. Draw it. What color will your package be?"
sayThis.es: "Pick one thing to put in a package. It can be real or pretend. Draw it. What color will your package be?"

watchFor.en: Kids who can't pick a product. Offer three: a toy, a pretend cookie, a pencil.
watchFor.es: Kids who can't pick a product. Offer three: a toy, a pretend cookie, a pencil.

doneWhen.en: Every child has drawn a product and said one color.
doneWhen.es: Every child has drawn a product and said one color.

description.en: Students draw detailed package design on paper: all sides, labels, how it opens. Include product name and key information.
description.es: Students draw detailed package design on paper: all sides, labels, how it opens. Include product name and key information.

sayThis.en: "Pick your best idea. Draw it again, bigger. Put the name on it. Show how it opens."
sayThis.es: "Pick your best idea. Draw it again, bigger. Put the name on it. Show how it opens."

watchFor.en: Kids starting a brand-new idea. Point back to their best one.
watchFor.es: Kids starting a brand-new idea. Point back to their best one.

doneWhen.en: Every paper has one package drawing with a name on it.
doneWhen.es: Every paper has one package drawing with a name on it.

description.en: Draw the front of your package, big. The teacher writes the name on it.
description.es: Draw the front of your package, big. The teacher writes the name on it.

sayThis.en: "Draw the front of your package. Make it big. Tell me the name and I'll write it for you."
sayThis.es: "Draw the front of your package. Make it big. Tell me the name and I'll write it for you."

watchFor.en: Kids starting a brand-new idea. Point back to the thing they picked.
watchFor.es: Kids starting a brand-new idea. Point back to the thing they picked.

doneWhen.en: Every paper has a front drawing with a name the teacher wrote.
doneWhen.es: Every paper has a front drawing with a name the teacher wrote.

description.en: Students build simple package prototype from cardboard, paper, or recycled materials. Focus on basic structure and functionality.
description.es: Students build simple package prototype from cardboard, paper, or recycled materials. Focus on basic structure and functionality.

sayThis.en: "Now build it from your box or paper. It just has to hold your thing and close."
sayThis.es: "Now build it from your box or paper. It just has to hold your thing and close."

watchFor.en: Kids decorating before it holds together. Ask "Does it close?" first.
watchFor.es: Kids decorating before it holds together. Ask "Does it close?" first.

doneWhen.en: Every child has a package that holds together.
doneWhen.es: Every child has a package that holds together.

description.en: Decorate a small box that is already made instead of building one. Use crayons and your drawing as a guide.
description.es: Decorate a small box that is already made instead of building one. Use crayons and your drawing as a guide.

sayThis.en: "Here is a box that is already made. Make it look like your drawing."
sayThis.es: "Here is a box that is already made. Make it look like your drawing."

watchFor.en: Kids coloring only one side. Turn the box and ask what goes on this side.
watchFor.es: Kids coloring only one side. Turn the box and ask what goes on this side.

doneWhen.en: Every child has a decorated box.
doneWhen.es: Every child has a decorated box.

description.en: Students present packages in small groups. Explain design choices: Why this shape? What makes it attractive? What information is important? Get peer feedback on design.
description.es: Students present packages in small groups. Explain design choices: Why this shape? What makes it attractive? What information is important? Get peer feedback on design.

sayThis.en: "In your group, show your package. Say why you picked the shape and colors. Friends, say one thing you like and one thing to try."
sayThis.es: "In your group, show your package. Say why you picked the shape and colors. Friends, say one thing you like and one thing to try."

watchFor.en: Feedback like "it's bad." Give the frame "I like ___. You could try ___."
watchFor.es: Feedback like "it's bad." Give the frame "I like ___. You could try ___."

doneWhen.en: Every child has shown a package and heard one like and one idea.
doneWhen.es: Every child has shown a package and heard one like and one idea.

description.en: In small groups, show your package and say one thing you like about it.
description.es: In small groups, show your package and say one thing you like about it.

sayThis.en: "Show your package to your group. Say: I like my package because blank."
sayThis.es: "Show your package to your group. Say: I like my package because blank."

watchFor.en: Kids grabbing each other's packages. Hands stay on your own.
watchFor.es: Kids grabbing each other's packages. Hands stay on your own.

doneWhen.en: Every child has shown a package and said one thing they like.
doneWhen.es: Every child has shown a package and said one thing they like.

discussionQuestions: Which package in your group looked most special?
Would you pay more for something in a nice package?
Why does packaging matter?

description.es: Students complete worksheet: What's your brand name? (can be your own name + "Creations"). Sketch simple logo. Choose 2-3 brand colors.

sayThis.es: "Every brand needs a name. You can use your own name plus Creations. Draw a logo you can draw fast. Pick two or three colors."

watchFor.es: Kids stuck on a name. Give the frame: your name plus Creations.

doneWhen.es: Every sheet has a name, a logo and colors picked.

description.es: Draw a logo and pick two or three colors. Tell the teacher your brand name and the teacher writes it. You can use your own name plus Creations.

sayThis.es: "Every brand needs a name. Try your name plus Creations. Tell me and I'll write it. Now draw a picture for your logo and pick two or three colors."

sayThis.es: "Fold on the lines. Tuck the flaps in. Tape only if it won't stay shut."

doneWhen.es: Every child has a box that stands up and closes.

description.es: Transfer brand name and logo to box. Use brand colors. Add decorative elements. Make it look "store quality."

sayThis.es: "Put your name and logo on the box. Use only your brand colors. Make it look like it came from a store."

doneWhen.es: Every box has decorations on all sides and a note inside.

sayThis.es: "This is clay. People have made pots from it for a very long time. Watch: I roll it, I pinch it, I smooth it. A wet finger helps. Clay stays on your plate."

Compare to factory decoration—why does hand-painted cost more?

Photography for marketing—does good photo increase perceived value?
