focus: Free decoration with crayons/markers
Focus on "making it pretty" - Simple understanding: decorated = more special
Pick a price up to $10, no calculations - Basic vocabulary: decorate, paint, special, colors, price
Guided decoration with planning
Simple before/after price comparison - Can explain "decoration makes it worth more"
Basic time tracking (how many minutes?) - Vocabulary: value, decoration, design, price, worth more
Planned decoration with intentional design
Calculate simple value added (before $5, after $10, added $5) - Track time and materials cost
Understand cost vs. value relationship - Vocabulary: value-added, profit, cost, margin, professional
Professional decoration with market research
Full cost-benefit analysis - Calculate profit margins and pricing strategy
Understand decoration as business investment - Advanced vocabulary: value chain, skill premium, profit margin, market price

ell.label: English Language Learners
strategies: Hold up the plain and decorated items side by side and say: before, after, worth more.
Put decorate, price, before and after on the board with a drawing beside each word.
Let students show value by pointing to price cards instead of explaining out loud.

learningDifferences.label: Students with Learning Differences
strategies: Offer stencils or stickers for students who find brush control hard.
Give extra decorating time, and keep time for the student.
Give a price card with $1 to $10 printed so the student circles a number instead of writing.

advanced.label: Advanced Students
strategies: Make a simple and a fancy version, and survey which one people would pay more for.
Work out what you earned per hour from your time and the value you added.
Write a price tag that explains why the item is worth the new price.

sayThis.en: "Watch three things change. Ice into water. Two colors into one new color. A flat sheet into a shape. Every time, ask yourself the same question: is the new thing worth more than what it was?"
sayThis.es: "Watch three things change. Ice into water. Two colors into one new color. A flat sheet into a shape. Every time, ask yourself the same question: is the new thing worth more than what it was?"

doneWhen.en: All three demos have a worth-more or worth-less vote recorded on the board.
doneWhen.es: All three demos have a worth-more or worth-less vote recorded on the board.

watchFor.en: Yes as the answer every time. Ask about the melted ice. Sometimes changing a thing makes it worth less.
watchFor.es: Yes as the answer every time. Ask about the melted ice. Sometimes changing a thing makes it worth less.

description.en: Three demonstrations showing materials changing form: ice melting in a plastic container (solid to liquid), stirring two paint colors together in a paper cup with a craft stick (two become one new), folding a paper square into origami (flat to 3D). Ask: Is the new thing worth more?
description.es: Three demonstrations showing materials changing form: ice melting in a plastic container (solid to liquid), stirring two paint colors together in a paper cup with a craft stick (two become one new), folding a paper square into origami (flat to 3D). Ask: Is the new thing worth more?

sayThis.en: "Wheat, flour, bread, sandwich. Four steps. The wheat costs almost nothing. The sandwich costs five dollars. Somebody did work at every arrow, and every arrow costs money."
sayThis.es: "Wheat, flour, bread, sandwich. Four steps. The wheat costs almost nothing. The sandwich costs five dollars. Somebody did work at every arrow, and every arrow costs money."

watchFor.en: Students who think the shop just charges whatever it likes. Walk back down the chain and name the work at each arrow.
watchFor.es: Students who think the shop just charges whatever it likes. Walk back down the chain and name the work at each arrow.

description.en: Show a simple value chain: wheat → flour → bread → sandwich. Each step adds value. Raw materials are cheap, finished products cost more because of the work to transform them.
description.es: Show a simple value chain: wheat → flour → bread → sandwich. Each step adds value. Raw materials are cheap, finished products cost more because of the work to transform them.

sayThis.en: "Three stations. You take the raw stuff and turn it into a finished thing. Weave it, mix it, build it. Watch the clock, because the time is the cost."
sayThis.es: "Three stations. You take the raw stuff and turn it into a finished thing. Weave it, mix it, build it. Watch the clock, because the time is the cost."

doneWhen.en: Every student has a finished item from each station with a time written on it in pencil.
doneWhen.es: Every student has a finished item from each station with a time written on it in pencil.

watchFor.en: Half-finished pieces abandoned when the timer goes. One finished thing per station beats three abandoned ones.
watchFor.es: Half-finished pieces abandoned when the timer goes. One finished thing per station beats three abandoned ones.

description.en: Rotate through 3-4 stations where students transform materials: weaving paper strips into placemats, filling envelopes with sorted beads, buttons and a piece of string to make craft kits, building simple structures from cardboard pieces and tape. Track time spent at each.
description.es: Rotate through 3-4 stations where students transform materials: weaving paper strips into placemats, filling envelopes with sorted beads, buttons and a piece of string to make craft kits, building simple structures from cardboard pieces and tape. Track time spent at each.

description.es: Students visit the stations and make one finished thing at each: a woven paper placemat, a filled craft kit, a small building of cardboard and tape. The teacher keeps time and writes each time on the finished thing.

sayThis.es: "Three stations. Take the raw stuff and turn it into a finished thing. Weave it, fill a kit, build it. I will watch the clock and write your time for you."

watchFor.en: Half-finished pieces abandoned when the timer goes. One finished thing per station beats three abandoned ones.
watchFor.es: Half-finished pieces abandoned when the timer goes. One finished thing per station beats three abandoned ones.

doneWhen.en: Every student has a finished item from each station, with a time you wrote on it.
doneWhen.es: Every student has a finished item from each station, with a time you wrote on it.

sayThis.en: "What did the raw stuff cost? What's the finished one worth? The gap is what your work added. Now think about something you own — most of what you paid was somebody's work, not the material."
sayThis.es: "What did the raw stuff cost? What's the finished one worth? The gap is what your work added. Now think about something you own — most of what you paid was somebody's work, not the material."

doneWhen.en: Every station row shows a raw cost, a finished value and the difference between them.
doneWhen.es: Every station row shows a raw cost, a finished value and the difference between them.

watchFor.es: Raw costs being guessed instead of read off the card. The numbers are on the cards.

description.en: For each station, calculate: raw material cost vs. finished product value. How much did transformation add? Introduce the concept that processing and labor add most of the cost to products we buy.
description.es: For each station, calculate: raw material cost vs. finished product value. How much did transformation add? Introduce the concept that processing and labor add most of the cost to products we buy.

description.en: Hold up the raw stuff and the finished thing from each station, and the class votes which one costs more. Read both prices off the station card, then count up together from the small price to the big one. That is what the work added. Card prices of $10 or less keep the counting easy.
description.es: Hold up the raw stuff and the finished thing from each station, and the class votes which one costs more. Read both prices off the station card, then count up together from the small price to the big one. That is what the work added. Card prices of $10 or less keep the counting easy.

sayThis.en: "Here is the stuff before. Here is the thing after. Which one costs more? Hands up. Now let's count up from the small price to the big price."
sayThis.es: "Here is the stuff before. Here is the thing after. Which one costs more? Hands up. Now let's count up from the small price to the big price."

watchFor.en: Kids guessing the prices. Point to the prices on the card and count up together on your fingers.

sayThis.en: "Pick one everyday thing. Work backwards. What was it before that? And before that? Keep going until you hit a plant, a stone or an animal. Then tell us which step added the most."
sayThis.es: "Pick one everyday thing. Work backwards. What was it before that? And before that? Keep going until you hit a plant, a stone or an animal. Then tell us which step added the most."

watchFor.es: Chains that stop at the shop. Keep asking what came before.

description.en: Build one chain together as a class. Pick a pencil or a t-shirt, ask what it was before, and before that, and draw each stage on the board. Ask which step took the most work.
description.es: Build one chain together as a class. Pick a pencil or a t-shirt, ask what it was before, and before that, and draw each stage on the board. Ask which step took the most work.

sayThis.en: "Let's pick a pencil. What was it before? Wood. And before that? A tree. Who did work at each step? Let's draw each one."
sayThis.es: "Let's pick a pencil. What was it before? Wood. And before that? A tree. Who did work at each step? Let's draw each one."

watchFor.en: The chain stopping at the store. Ask where the store got it.
watchFor.es: The chain stopping at the store. Ask where the store got it.

doneWhen.en: One class chain of three or more stages is drawn on the board.
doneWhen.es: One class chain of three or more stages is drawn on the board.

sayThis.en: "A pile of lumber is cheap. A table made from it is not. Why? And here's the one that matters — what transformation can you do that somebody would pay you for?"
sayThis.es: "A pile of lumber is cheap. A table made from it is not. Why? And here's the one that matters — what transformation can you do that somebody would pay you for?"

doneWhen.en: Every student has written an answer to both questions.
doneWhen.es: Every student has written an answer to both questions.

watchFor.en: The second question getting skipped. That's the point of the lesson. Make them answer it.
watchFor.es: The second question getting skipped. That's the point of the lesson. Make them answer it.

description.en: Write or discuss: Why does a wooden table cost more than a pile of lumber? How does transformation create value? What transformations can YOU do that add value?
description.es: Write or discuss: Why does a wooden table cost more than a pile of lumber? How does transformation create value? What transformations can YOU do that add value?

doneWhen.en: Every student has said an answer to both questions to you or a partner.
doneWhen.es: Every student has said an answer to both questions to you or a partner.

discussionQuestions: What's the difference between a physical change and a chemical change?
Why can't you reverse some transformations?
How does transformation improve a product's function or durability?
Calculate: If processing costs $5 but adds $20 of value, what's the profit from transformation?
Why do factories invest in expensive processing equipment?
What transformation adds the most value? (Hint: ones requiring specialized skills/equipment)
How is a kiln like a factory? How is it different?
extensionIdeas: Calculate transformation ROI (return on investment) for multiple products
Research industrial processes (steel making, glass blowing, textile production)
Design a new product and map its transformation chain
Visit local factory or processing facility
Compare artisanal (hand-processing) vs. industrial (machine-processing) economics

ell.label: English Language Learners
strategies: Act out each demo word as you say it — melt, mix, fold — and write the three words on the board with a picture.
Let students show their value chain as a row of drawings instead of words.
Pair each student with a partner who can read the station cost cards aloud.

learningDifferences.label: Students with Learning Differences
strategies: Give a before-and-after sheet with two boxes to draw in, not lines to write on.
Let students stay at one or two stations and finish there instead of rotating through all of them.
Let students say their reflection answer to you or a partner instead of writing it.

advanced.label: Advanced Students
strategies: Work out the added value at every station and rank the stations from most to least.
Stretch the real-world chain to six or more stages with a guessed price at each one.
Sort the demos and stations into changes that can be undone and changes that cannot, and explain why.

sayThis.es: "Pick one problem. Draw a thing that fixes it. Point to its parts. Then tell your partner: my invention solves ___."

fromScratch.costPerStudent: $0 — everything is free or from home

items: Paper — 20 sheets, one per student for the blueprint

basicClassroom.description: Students draw a blueprint on paper with a pencil and ruler, then build a prototype from box cardboard, tape, paper, craft sticks and pipe cleaners, cutting with scissors.
items: Paper — 20 sheets, one per student for the blueprint

sayThis.en: "An invention starts with something annoying. Not a giant world problem — something that annoyed you this week. Five of them on the board, then we vote."
sayThis.es: "An invention starts with something annoying. Not a giant world problem — something that annoyed you this week. Five of them on the board, then we vote."

doneWhen.en: At least five problems are on the board and three are circled by class vote.
doneWhen.es: At least five problems are on the board and three are circled by class vote.

watchFor.en: Wishes dressed as problems. "I want a robot" isn't a problem. Ask what the robot would fix.
watchFor.es: Wishes dressed as problems. "I want a robot" isn't a problem. Ask what the robot would fix.

description.en: Students brainstorm problems in classroom, at home, or in community. List 5+ problems. Vote as class on top 3 problems to focus on. Students choose which problem they want to solve.
description.es: Students brainstorm problems in classroom, at home, or in community. List 5+ problems. Vote as class on top 3 problems to focus on. Students choose which problem they want to solve.

sayThis.en: "Draw it big on your paper with a pencil. Label every part. Write what it's made of. Here's the test: if somebody else picked this up, could they build it without asking you a single question?"
sayThis.es: "Draw it big on your paper with a pencil. Label every part. Write what it's made of. Here's the test: if somebody else picked this up, could they build it without asking you a single question?"

doneWhen.en: Every blueprint has labeled parts and a materials list on it.
doneWhen.es: Every blueprint has labeled parts and a materials list on it.

watchFor.en: Drawings with no labels. Hand it to a neighbor and watch them fail to read it.
watchFor.es: Drawings with no labels. Hand it to a neighbor and watch them fail to read it.

description.en: Students draw detailed blueprint of their invention. Must include: labels for each part, materials needed, how it works. Use rulers for straight lines.
description.es: Students draw detailed blueprint of their invention. Must include: labels for each part, materials needed, how it works. Use rulers for straight lines.

description.en: Students draw detailed blueprint of their invention. Must include: labels for each part, materials needed, how it works. Use the straight edge of a piece of cardboard for straight lines.
description.es: Students draw detailed blueprint of their invention. Must include: labels for each part, materials needed, how it works. Use the straight edge of a piece of cardboard for straight lines.

description.en: Children draw their invention big on paper. They show two or three parts with a word or a picture, and what it is made of.
description.es: Children draw their invention big on paper. They show two or three parts with a word or a picture, and what it is made of.

sayThis.en: "Draw it big on your paper. Show two or three parts with a word or a picture. Could a friend tell what it does?"
sayThis.es: "Draw it big on your paper. Show two or three parts with a word or a picture. Could a friend tell what it does?"

watchFor.en: Drawings with no parts shown. Point at a part and ask what it is.
watchFor.es: Drawings with no parts shown. Point at a part and ask what it is.

doneWhen.en: Every child has a big drawing with two or three parts shown.
doneWhen.es: Every child has a big drawing with two or three parts shown.

sayThis.en: "It doesn't have to work. It has to show the idea. Cardboard and tape is fine. Today, a model of a thing counts as the thing."
sayThis.es: "It doesn't have to work. It has to show the idea. Cardboard and tape is fine. Today, a model of a thing counts as the thing."

doneWhen.en: Every student has a physical prototype on their desk.
doneWhen.es: Every student has a physical prototype on their desk.

watchFor.en: Perfectionists stuck on the first piece. Watch the clock, give a two-minute warning and mean it.
watchFor.es: Perfectionists stuck on the first piece. Watch the clock, give a two-minute warning and mean it.

description.en: Using classroom materials (cardboard, scissors, tape, paper, craft sticks, pipe cleaners), students build a simple prototype. Doesn't need to fully work, but should show the concept.
description.es: Using classroom materials (cardboard, scissors, tape, paper, craft sticks, pipe cleaners), students build a simple prototype. Doesn't need to fully work, but should show the concept.

description.en: Using free materials (box cardboard, scrap paper, tape), students build a simple prototype. Tear or fold the cardboard instead of cutting it. Doesn't need to fully work, but should show the concept.
description.es: Using free materials (box cardboard, scrap paper, tape), students build a simple prototype. Tear or fold the cardboard instead of cutting it. Doesn't need to fully work, but should show the concept.

sayThis.en: "Four things in thirty seconds. The problem. Who has it. How yours fixes it. Why it beats what people do now. Say it out loud — reading it in your head doesn't count."
sayThis.es: "Four things in thirty seconds. The problem. Who has it. How yours fixes it. Why it beats what people do now. Say it out loud — reading it in your head doesn't count."

doneWhen.en: Every student has said their pitch out loud to a partner at least once.
doneWhen.es: Every student has said their pitch out loud to a partner at least once.

watchFor.en: Silent practice. Make the room noisy on purpose.
watchFor.es: Silent practice. Make the room noisy on purpose.

description.en: Students practice their 30-second pitch: What problem does it solve? Who would use it? How does it work? What makes it better than current solutions?
description.es: Students practice their 30-second pitch: What problem does it solve? Who would use it? How does it work? What makes it better than current solutions?

sayThis.en: "Sharks, you have money and you're picky. One or two questions each, then thumbs up or thumbs down. Thumbs down is allowed. But you have to say why."
sayThis.es: "Sharks, you have money and you're picky. One or two questions each, then thumbs up or thumbs down. Thumbs down is allowed. But you have to say why."

doneWhen.en: Every inventor has pitched, taken a question and had the vote counted.
doneWhen.es: Every inventor has pitched, taken a question and had the vote counted.

watchFor.en: Everyone voting up for their friends. Require a reason for every vote and the honesty turns up.
watchFor.es: Everyone voting up for their friends. Require a reason for every vote and the honesty turns up.

description.en: Students present inventions to class (the 'sharks'). After each pitch, sharks ask 1-2 questions and vote thumbs up/down on whether they'd invest.
description.es: Students present inventions to class (the 'sharks'). After each pitch, sharks ask 1-2 questions and vote thumbs up/down on whether they'd invest.

discussionQuestions: How did you decide which problem to solve?
Why did you choose this solution over your other ideas?
Who is your customer? How many potential customers exist?
What would it cost to make? What would you charge?
What feedback did you get? Would you change your invention based on it?
Which invention presented today has the best chance of success? Why?
What's the difference between a cool idea and a marketable invention?
extensionIdeas: Research real inventors—how did they identify problems to solve?
Calculate break-even point: how many units to sell to cover development costs?
Create marketing materials for invention
Improve prototype based on feedback
Research: has anyone already invented this? How is yours different?

beforeClass.es: Put the build materials in one place so nobody hunts mid-build. Have three problems of your own ready in case the brainstorm stalls — a drawer that gets stuck, pencils that vanish, a backpack that won't stand up.

runningLongOrShort.en: Long: skip the pitch prep and go straight from build to presentations. Short: add a second prototype round after the shark feedback.
runningLongOrShort.es: Long: skip the pitch prep and go straight from build to presentations. Short: add a second prototype round after the shark feedback.

ell.label: English Language Learners
strategies: Show pictures of everyday problems — a spilled drink, an untied shoe — before the hunt so students can point instead of explain.
Give the frame "My invention solves ___" with a picture box beside it.
Let students share or pitch with a partner who can help with the words.

learningDifferences.label: Students with Learning Differences
strategies: Let students draw problems on the hunt instead of writing them.
Let students tell you their invention and write the labels they say.
When students pitch to the class, offer a quiet pitch to you alone in place of the whole class.

advanced.label: Advanced Students
strategies: Ask three classmates if they have the same problem before choosing it.
Find what people use now to solve the problem and explain why the invention is better.
Estimate what the invention would cost to make and what they would charge for it.

discussionQuestions: What's the difference between sketching an idea and creating a blueprint?
How does planning prevent waste in production?
If materials cost $10 and you make a mistake, what's the real cost? (waste + replacement)

How would you change your blueprint if you were making 100 of these instead of 1?

How is your blueprint a form of communication?

description.en: Explain market research: asking potential customers what they think before making product. Discuss: Why do businesses need to know what customers want? What questions should you ask? Introduce survey activity.
description.es: Explain market research: asking potential customers what they think before making product. Discuss: Why do businesses need to know what customers want? What questions should you ask? Introduce survey activity.

sayThis.en: "Before a business makes something, it asks people: would you buy this? That is called market research. Today you get to ask the questions."
sayThis.es: "Before a business makes something, it asks people: would you buy this? That is called market research. Today you get to ask the questions."

watchFor.en: Kids who think the maker should just decide. Ask what happens if you make twenty and nobody wants one.
watchFor.es: Kids who think the maker should just decide. Ask what happens if you make twenty and nobody wants one.

doneWhen.en: Two or three students have said why a business asks people first.
doneWhen.es: Two or three students have said why a business asks people first.

description.en: Say it plainly: before you make something, you ask people if they want it. Skip the words market research.
description.es: Say it plainly: before you make something, you ask people if they want it. Skip the words market research.

sayThis.en: "Before you make something, you ask people: would you want this? Today you get to ask."
sayThis.es: "Before you make something, you ask people: would you want this? Today you get to ask."

watchFor.en: Children answering right now instead of waiting. Say, "Hold your answer. First we learn the question."
watchFor.es: Children answering right now instead of waiting. Say, "Hold your answer. First we learn the question."

doneWhen.en: The whole class has said the question out loud: would you want this?
doneWhen.es: The whole class has said the question out loud: would you want this?

description.en: Students create 3-5 simple survey questions about a product (real or from class): Would you buy this? How much would you pay? What would make it better? What features matter most? Practice asking clearly.
description.es: Students create 3-5 simple survey questions about a product (real or from class): Would you buy this? How much would you pay? What would make it better? What features matter most? Practice asking clearly.

sayThis.en: "Write questions about your product. Start with: would you buy this? Then: how much would you pay? Read them to your partner to check they make sense."
sayThis.es: "Write questions about your product. Start with: would you buy this? Then: how much would you pay? Read them to your partner to check they make sense."

watchFor.en: Questions that push the answer, like "Don't you love it?" Rewrite one on the board as "Would you buy this?"
watchFor.es: Questions that push the answer, like "Don't you love it?" Rewrite one on the board as "Would you buy this?"

doneWhen.en: Every student has their questions written, and has read them to a partner.
doneWhen.es: Every student has their questions written, and has read them to a partner.

description.en: Students use one yes/no question about their product: "Would you buy this?" They practice asking it clearly to a partner.
description.es: Students use one yes/no question about their product: "Would you buy this?" They practice asking it clearly to a partner.

sayThis.en: "Our question is: would you buy this? Say it to your partner. Say it loud and clear."
sayThis.es: "Our question is: would you buy this? Say it to your partner. Say it loud and clear."

watchFor.en: Students changing the question to "Don't you love it?" Keep it to: would you buy this?
watchFor.es: Students changing the question to "Don't you love it?" Keep it to: would you buy this?

doneWhen.en: Every student has asked the question clearly to a partner.
doneWhen.es: Every student has asked the question clearly to a partner.

description.en: Students survey classmates about their product. Record responses: yes/no answers, price suggestions, feature preferences. Try to survey at least 5 people. Write down what they say.
description.es: Students survey classmates about their product. Record responses: yes/no answers, price suggestions, feature preferences. Try to survey at least 5 people. Write down what they say.

sayThis.en: "Ask five people. Use one pen color for yes and the other for no. Write down the price they say."
sayThis.es: "Ask five people. Use one pen color for yes and the other for no. Write down the price they say."

watchFor.en: Students asking only their best friend. Ask for two people they don't usually sit with.
watchFor.es: Students asking only their best friend. Ask for two people they don't usually sit with.

doneWhen.en: Every sheet has at least five answers on it.
doneWhen.es: Every sheet has at least five answers on it.

sayThis.en: "Ask five people. Use one crayon color for yes and the other for no. Write down the price they say in pencil."
sayThis.es: "Ask five people. Use one crayon color for yes and the other for no. Write down the price they say in pencil."

description.en: Students ask five classmates the one yes/no question and make a tally mark for each answer: one color for yes, the other color for no.
description.es: Students ask five classmates the one yes/no question and make a tally mark for each answer: one color for yes, the other color for no.

sayThis.en: "Ask five people: would you buy this? Make one mark for each answer. One color for yes. The other color for no."
sayThis.es: "Ask five people: would you buy this? Make one mark for each answer. One color for yes. The other color for no."

watchFor.en: Students asking only their best friend. Ask for two people they don't usually sit with.
watchFor.es: Students asking only their best friend. Ask for two people they don't usually sit with.

doneWhen.en: Every sheet has five tally marks on it.
doneWhen.es: Every sheet has five tally marks on it.

description.en: Students organize survey results: How many would buy? What's the most common suggested price? What features do people want? Create simple chart or graph showing results.
description.es: Students organize survey results: How many would buy? What's the most common suggested price? What features do people want? Create simple chart or graph showing results.

sayThis.en: "Count your yes marks. Count your no marks. Which price did you hear most? Draw one bar for yes and one for no."
sayThis.es: "Count your yes marks. Count your no marks. Which price did you hear most? Draw one bar for yes and one for no."

watchFor.en: Messy tallies miscounted. Show how to count in bundles of five on the board.
watchFor.es: Messy tallies miscounted. Show how to count in bundles of five on the board.

doneWhen.en: Every student has a simple chart or graph showing their yes and no counts.
doneWhen.es: Every student has a simple chart or graph showing their yes and no counts.

description.en: Students count their yes marks and their no marks. The class builds one bar graph on the board together.
description.es: Students count their yes marks and their no marks. The class builds one bar graph on the board together.

sayThis.en: "Count your yes marks. Count your no marks. Which has more? Come help build our class graph."
sayThis.es: "Count your yes marks. Count your no marks. Which has more? Come help build our class graph."

watchFor.en: Messy tallies miscounted. Count one sheet out loud together, touching each mark.
watchFor.es: Messy tallies miscounted. Count one sheet out loud together, touching each mark.

doneWhen.en: Every student has said their yes and no counts, and the class graph is on the board.
doneWhen.es: Every student has said their yes and no counts, and the class graph is on the board.

description.en: Share survey results. Discuss: What did you learn? Were you surprised? Would you change your product based on feedback? Why is it important to ask customers before making something?
description.es: Share survey results. Discuss: What did you learn? Were you surprised? Would you change your product based on feedback? Why is it important to ask customers before making something?

sayThis.en: "Tell us one thing your survey told you. Would you change your product?"
sayThis.es: "Tell us one thing your survey told you. Would you change your product?"

watchFor.en: Answers like "people liked it." Ask for the number.
watchFor.es: Answers like "people liked it." Ask for the number.

doneWhen.en: At least three students have shared a number from their survey.
doneWhen.es: At least three students have shared a number from their survey.

description.en: Look at the two bars on the board together. Ask which bar is taller. No numbers needed.
description.es: Look at the two bars on the board together. Ask which bar is taller. No numbers needed.

sayThis.en: "Look at the two bars. Which one is taller, yes or no? So do people want it?"
sayThis.es: "Look at the two bars. Which one is taller, yes or no? So do people want it?"

watchFor.en: Children picking the first bar because it is nearest. Run your finger up both bars and stop at the top of each.
watchFor.es: Children picking the first bar because it is nearest. Run your finger up both bars and stop at the top of each.

doneWhen.en: The class has said out loud which bar is taller.
doneWhen.es: The class has said out loud which bar is taller.

discussionQuestions: Did everyone say yes? What does that tell you?
What if most people said no? Should you still make it?
How does asking first help you make smart choices?

beforeClass.en: Pick the product students will ask about — a class product or their own idea. Write one sample question on the board, like "Would you buy this?" Set out paper, the two-colour pens and hardback books for students to lean on.
beforeClass.es: Pick the product students will ask about — a class product or their own idea. Write one sample question on the board, like "Would you buy this?" Set out paper, the two-colour pens and hardback books for students to lean on.

runningLongOrShort.en: Long: cut Survey Question Development to two questions and survey three people. Short: in Data Analysis, have each student add a title and labels to their graph.
runningLongOrShort.es: Long: cut Survey Question Development to two questions and survey three people. Short: in Data Analysis, have each student add a title and labels to their graph.

beforeClass.en: Pick the product students will ask about — a class product or their own idea. Write one sample question on the board, like "Would you buy this?" Set out scrap paper, a pencil, two crayons in different colors and a piece of cardboard from an old box for each student to lean on.
beforeClass.es: Pick the product students will ask about — a class product or their own idea. Write one sample question on the board, like "Would you buy this?" Set out scrap paper, a pencil, two crayons in different colors and a piece of cardboard from an old box for each student to lean on.

description.en: Each student chooses a product they want to "sell" (real or imaginary). Write it down with estimated price.
description.es: Each student chooses a product they want to "sell" (real or imaginary). Write it down with estimated price.

sayThis.en: "Pick one thing you would like to sell. It can be real or made up. Write its name and a price."
sayThis.es: "Pick one thing you would like to sell. It can be real or made up. Write its name and a price."

watchFor.en: Prices like a million dollars. Ask what they would pay for it themselves.
watchFor.es: Prices like a million dollars. Ask what they would pay for it themselves.

doneWhen.en: Every student has a product name and a price written down.
doneWhen.es: Every student has a product name and a price written down.

description.en: Each student chooses a product they want to "sell" (real or imaginary) and tells a partner its name. No price.
description.es: Each student chooses a product they want to "sell" (real or imaginary) and tells a partner its name. No price.

sayThis.en: "Pick one thing you would like to sell. It can be real or made up. Tell your partner what it is."
sayThis.es: "Pick one thing you would like to sell. It can be real or made up. Tell your partner what it is."

watchFor.en: Students who can't pick. Offer two choices, like a toy or a game.
watchFor.es: Students who can't pick. Offer two choices, like a toy or a game.

doneWhen.en: Every student has told a partner the name of their product.
doneWhen.es: Every student has told a partner the name of their product.

description.en: Create 3-question survey: "Would you buy this? How much would you pay? What features do you want?"
description.es: Create 3-question survey: "Would you buy this? How much would you pay? What features do you want?"

sayThis.en: "Write three questions at the top of your sheet. Would you buy this? How much would you pay? What features do you want?"
sayThis.es: "Write three questions at the top of your sheet. Would you buy this? How much would you pay? What features do you want?"

watchFor.en: Students adding words that push the answer, like "awesome." Keep the questions plain.
watchFor.es: Students adding words that push the answer, like "awesome." Keep the questions plain.

doneWhen.en: Every sheet has the three questions written at the top.
doneWhen.es: Every sheet has the three questions written at the top.

description.en: Students use one yes/no question: "Would you buy this?" They draw their product at the top of the sheet so people can see what they are asking about.
description.es: Students use one yes/no question: "Would you buy this?" They draw their product at the top of the sheet so people can see what they are asking about.

sayThis.en: "Our question is: would you buy this? Draw your product at the top of your sheet."
sayThis.es: "Our question is: would you buy this? Draw your product at the top of your sheet."

watchFor.en: Students changing the question. Keep it to: would you buy this?
watchFor.es: Students changing the question. Keep it to: would you buy this?

doneWhen.en: Every sheet has the product drawn at the top, and every student can say the question.
doneWhen.es: Every sheet has the product drawn at the top, and every student can say the question.

description.en: Survey 8-10 classmates (or buddy class if available). Record answers carefully.
description.es: Survey 8-10 classmates (or buddy class if available). Record answers carefully.

sayThis.en: "Ask eight to ten people. Write each answer down right away. For would you buy it, yes in one color and no in the other. Write the price and feature answers as words or numbers in either color."
sayThis.es: "Ask eight to ten people. Write each answer down right away. For would you buy it, yes in one color and no in the other. Write the price and feature answers as words or numbers in either color."

watchFor.en: Students surveying the same few friends. Ask for at least three people they don't usually talk to.
watchFor.es: Students surveying the same few friends. Ask for at least three people they don't usually talk to.

doneWhen.en: Every sheet has at least eight answers recorded.
doneWhen.es: Every sheet has at least eight answers recorded.

description.en: Students ask eight classmates the one yes/no question and make a tally mark for each answer: one color for yes, the other color for no.
description.es: Students ask eight classmates the one yes/no question and make a tally mark for each answer: one color for yes, the other color for no.

sayThis.en: "Ask eight people: would you buy this? Make one mark for each answer. One color for yes. The other color for no."
sayThis.es: "Ask eight people: would you buy this? Make one mark for each answer. One color for yes. The other color for no."

watchFor.en: Students asking the same few friends. Ask for three people they don't usually talk to.
watchFor.es: Students asking the same few friends. Ask for three people they don't usually talk to.

doneWhen.en: Every sheet has at least eight tally marks.
doneWhen.es: Every sheet has at least eight tally marks.

description.en: Count answers. Create simple bar graph showing results (how many yes/no, price preferences).
description.es: Count answers. Create simple bar graph showing results (how many yes/no, price preferences).

sayThis.en: "Count the yes and the no. Draw one bar for each. Make each bar as tall as its number. Then do the same for the prices."
sayThis.es: "Count the yes and the no. Draw one bar for each. Make each bar as tall as its number. Then do the same for the prices."

watchFor.en: Bars drawn by guess. Draw one on the board first, making a small mark for each answer as you count up out loud.
watchFor.es: Bars drawn by guess. Draw one on the board first, making a small mark for each answer as you count up out loud.

doneWhen.en: Every student has a bar graph with labeled yes and no bars.
doneWhen.es: Every student has a bar graph with labeled yes and no bars.

description.en: Students count their yes and no tallies and see which has more. The class builds one bar graph on the board: each student colors one square, in the More Yes bar or the More No bar.
description.es: Students count their yes and no tallies and see which has more. The class builds one bar graph on the board: each student colors one square, in the More Yes bar or the More No bar.

sayThis.en: "Count your yes marks. Count your no marks. Which has more? Come color one square on our class graph: More Yes or More No."
sayThis.es: "Count your yes marks. Count your no marks. Which has more? Come color one square on our class graph: More Yes or More No."

watchFor.en: Bars filled in by guess. Count the squares out loud as each one is colored.
watchFor.es: Bars filled in by guess. Count the squares out loud as each one is colored.

doneWhen.en: The class graph on the board has one square from every student, and every student has said their counts.
doneWhen.es: The class graph on the board has one square from every student, and every student has said their counts.

description.en: "Based on your data, should you make this product? What changes should you make?"
description.es: "Based on your data, should you make this product? What changes should you make?"

sayThis.en: "Look at your graph. Should you make this product? What one thing would you change?"
sayThis.es: "Look at your graph. Should you make this product? What one thing would you change?"

watchFor.en: Students ignoring a tall no bar. Ask what the biggest bar is telling them.
watchFor.es: Students ignoring a tall no bar. Ask what the biggest bar is telling them.

doneWhen.en: Every student has said or written a yes or no decision and one change.
doneWhen.es: Every student has said or written a yes or no decision and one change.

description.en: Partner share: "What did your research tell you?"
description.es: Partner share: "What did your research tell you?"

sayThis.en: "Tell your partner: my research told me ___."
sayThis.es: "Tell your partner: my research told me ___."

watchFor.en: Pairs drifting off topic. Give the sentence start and call time at one minute.
watchFor.es: Pairs drifting off topic. Give the sentence start and call time at one minute.

doneWhen.en: Every pair has finished the sentence out loud.
doneWhen.es: Every pair has finished the sentence out loud.

discussionQuestions: Did anyone's data surprise them?
What's the most popular price range?
Did anyone decide NOT to make their product after the survey? Why?
How is research different from guessing?
What if you skipped research and made 100 products nobody wanted?
extensionIdeas: Create a class "Market Research Report" poster showing all findings.

sayThis.en: "Design something and put a price on it. Then write your guess: out of ten people, how many say yes? Write the number now, because at the end you'll want to claim you knew all along."
sayThis.es: "Design something and put a price on it. Then write your guess: out of ten people, how many say yes? Write the number now, because at the end you'll want to claim you knew all along."

doneWhen.en: Every student has a sketch, a name, a price and a written prediction.
doneWhen.es: Every student has a sketch, a name, a price and a written prediction.

watchFor.en: Guesses of ten out of ten. Let them stand. The data does the arguing later.
watchFor.es: Guesses of ten out of ten. Let them stand. The data does the arguing later.

description.en: Each student designs a product (sketch + name + description + initial price) Write "hypothesis": "I think [number] out of 10 people will want to buy this"
description.es: Each student designs a product (sketch + name + description + initial price) Write "hypothesis": "I think [number] out of 10 people will want to buy this"

description.en: Each student draws a product, gives it a name and a price up to $10, and guesses how many of ten people will say yes.
description.es: Each student draws a product, gives it a name and a price up to $10, and guesses how many of ten people will say yes.

sayThis.en: "Draw a thing you want to sell. Give it a name and a price, ten dollars or less. Now guess: if you ask ten people, how many say yes? Write that number on your page."
sayThis.es: "Draw a thing you want to sell. Give it a name and a price, ten dollars or less. Now guess: if you ask ten people, how many say yes? Write that number on your page."

watchFor.en: Guesses of ten out of ten. Let them stand. The tally shows the answer later.
watchFor.es: Guesses of ten out of ten. Let them stand. The tally shows the answer later.

doneWhen.en: Every student has a drawing, a name, a price and a guess number on the page.
doneWhen.es: Every student has a drawing, a name, a price and a guess number on the page.

sayThis.en: "Five to seven questions. Ask what they'd pay, not whether they like it — liking it is free. Then test your questions on your partner. If they ask what you mean, the question is broken."
sayThis.es: "Five to seven questions. Ask what they'd pay, not whether they like it — liking it is free. Then test your questions on your partner. If they ask what you mean, the question is broken."

doneWhen.en: Every survey has at least five questions tested on a partner.
doneWhen.es: Every survey has at least five questions tested on a partner.

watchFor.en: Questions that lead the answer. "Don't you think this is great?" Rewrite one in front of the class.
watchFor.es: Questions that lead the answer. "Don't you think this is great?" Rewrite one in front of the class.

description.en: Design 5-7 questions: Would you buy? Price range? Preferred features/colors? What problems does it solve? What would make it better? Test questions on partner for clarity.
description.es: Design 5-7 questions: Would you buy? Price range? Preferred features/colors? What problems does it solve? What would make it better? Test questions on partner for clarity.

description.en: Students use one yes/no question: "Would you buy this?" They test it on a partner to check it is clear.
description.es: Students use one yes/no question: "Would you buy this?" They test it on a partner to check it is clear.

sayThis.en: "Our question is: would you buy this? Ask your partner. Did they understand it? Then your question works."
sayThis.es: "Our question is: would you buy this? Ask your partner. Did they understand it? Then your question works."

watchFor.en: Questions that push the answer, like "Don't you love it?" Keep it to: would you buy this?
watchFor.es: Questions that push the answer, like "Don't you love it?" Keep it to: would you buy this?

doneWhen.en: Every student has asked the question to a partner.
doneWhen.es: Every student has asked the question to a partner.

sayThis.en: "Ten to fifteen people. Write every answer down as you get it, including the rude ones. Especially the rude ones. Those are the useful ones."
sayThis.es: "Ten to fifteen people. Write every answer down as you get it, including the rude ones. Especially the rude ones. Those are the useful ones."

doneWhen.en: Every data sheet has at least ten responses recorded.
doneWhen.es: Every data sheet has at least ten responses recorded.

watchFor.en: Students surveying only their friends. Set a rule: at least five people you don't usually talk to.
watchFor.es: Students surveying only their friends. Set a rule: at least five people you don't usually talk to.

description.en: Survey 10-15 people (classmates, another class, or school staff) Record all answers on data sheets Note unexpected feedback or suggestions.
description.es: Survey 10-15 people (classmates, another class, or school staff) Record all answers on data sheets Note unexpected feedback or suggestions.

description.en: Students ask ten people the one yes/no question and make a tally mark for each answer on their data sheet.
description.es: Students ask ten people the one yes/no question and make a tally mark for each answer on their data sheet.

sayThis.en: "Ask ten people: would you buy this? Make one mark for each answer. Yes marks on one side. No marks on the other side."
sayThis.es: "Ask ten people: would you buy this? Make one mark for each answer. Yes marks on one side. No marks on the other side."

watchFor.en: Students asking only their friends. Ask for three people they don't usually talk to.
watchFor.es: Students asking only their friends. Ask for three people they don't usually talk to.

doneWhen.en: Every data sheet has ten tally marks.
doneWhen.es: Every data sheet has ten tally marks.

sayThis.en: "Tally it. Turn it into a bar chart. Work out the percentage. Then write your prediction next to the real number and look at the gap."
sayThis.es: "Tally it. Turn it into a bar chart. Work out the percentage. Then write your prediction next to the real number and look at the gap."

doneWhen.en: Every student has a bar graph with their prediction written beside the actual result.
doneWhen.es: Every student has a bar graph with their prediction written beside the actual result.

watchFor.en: Percentages done by feel. Work one out on the board with the whole room first.
watchFor.es: Percentages done by feel. Work one out on the board with the whole room first.

description.en: Tally all responses Create bar graphs showing: interest level, price preferences, feature preferences Calculate percentages (e.g., "60% said yes, 40% said no") Compare hypothesis to actual results.
description.es: Tally all responses Create bar graphs showing: interest level, price preferences, feature preferences Calculate percentages (e.g., "60% said yes, 40% said no") Compare hypothesis to actual results.

description.en: Students count their yes and no tallies and say which is more. They color one bar for yes and one for no, then write their guess next to the yes bar.
description.es: Students count their yes and no tallies and say which is more. They color one bar for yes and one for no, then write their guess next to the yes bar.

sayThis.en: "Count your yes marks. Count your no marks. Which is more? Color one bar for each. Was your guess close?"
sayThis.es: "Count your yes marks. Count your no marks. Which is more? Color one bar for each. Was your guess close?"

watchFor.en: Messy tallies miscounted. Count one sheet out loud together, touching each mark.
watchFor.es: Messy tallies miscounted. Count one sheet out loud together, touching each mark.

doneWhen.en: Every student has a yes bar and a no bar, with their guess written beside the yes bar.
doneWhen.es: Every student has a yes bar and a no bar, with their guess written beside the yes bar.

sayThis.en: "Change one thing because of the data, not because you felt like it. The price, a feature, or who it's for. Then write down what the data said that made you change it."
sayThis.es: "Change one thing because of the data, not because you felt like it. The price, a feature, or who it's for. Then write down what the data said that made you change it."

doneWhen.en: Every product shows a before and an after with the reason written between them.
doneWhen.es: Every product shows a before and an after with the reason written between them.

watchFor.en: Students refusing to change anything. Ask what their lowest-scoring answer was and start there.
watchFor.es: Students refusing to change anything. Ask what their lowest-scoring answer was and start there.

description.en: Based on data, adjust product: change price, add/remove features, change target customer Create "before and after" comparison showing changes made
description.es: Based on data, adjust product: change price, add/remove features, change target customer Create "before and after" comparison showing changes made

description.en: Students change one thing about their product because of the tally: the price, a color, or who it is for. They draw the product again with the change.
description.es: Students change one thing about their product because of the tally: the price, a color, or who it is for. They draw the product again with the change.

sayThis.en: "Look at your tally. Change one thing. The price, the color, or who it's for. Draw it again with the change."
sayThis.es: "Look at your tally. Change one thing. The price, the color, or who it's for. Draw it again with the change."

watchFor.en: Students not changing anything. Ask what might turn a no into a yes.
watchFor.es: Students not changing anything. Ask what might turn a no into a yes.

doneWhen.en: Every student has a before drawing and an after drawing.
doneWhen.es: Every student has a before drawing and an after drawing.

sayThis.en: "One page. The idea, the graph, what you found out, what you changed. That's a real report. Businesses pay a lot of money for that page."
sayThis.es: "One page. The idea, the graph, what you found out, what you changed. That's a real report. Businesses pay a lot of money for that page."

doneWhen.en: Every report page has all four parts filled in.
doneWhen.es: Every report page has all four parts filled in.

watchFor.en: Pages with a graph and no findings. The sentence under the graph is the report.
watchFor.es: Pages with a graph and no findings. The sentence under the graph is the report.

description.en: Complete one-page report: Product idea, survey results (graphs), key findings, product changes made based on feedback.
description.es: Complete one-page report: Product idea, survey results (graphs), key findings, product changes made based on feedback.

description.en: Students say their result out loud, like "5 said yes, 3 said no," and show their before and after drawings.
description.es: Students say their result out loud, like "5 said yes, 3 said no," and show their before and after drawings.

sayThis.en: "Tell us your numbers. How many said yes? How many said no? Show us what you changed."
sayThis.es: "Tell us your numbers. How many said yes? How many said no? Show us what you changed."

watchFor.en: Answers like "people liked it." Ask for the number.
watchFor.es: Answers like "people liked it." Ask for the number.

doneWhen.en: Every student has said their yes and no numbers out loud.
doneWhen.es: Every student has said their yes and no numbers out loud.

discussionQuestions: How many people's hypothesis was wrong? What does that teach us?
What's the risk of skipping market research?
If 8 out of 10 people want blue but you only make red, what happens?
How does research save money and materials?
What did you learn that you couldn't have guessed?
How do real companies use market research?
What's the difference between making what YOU like vs. what CUSTOMERS want?
extensionIdeas: Survey a second group and compare results (do different groups want different things?)
Calculate potential profit: "If 60% of 100 people buy at $5, and it costs $2 to make, what's your profit?"
Research real market research examples (taste tests, focus groups, beta testing)
Create survey for school cafeteria or library to improve services
Design a "bad survey" with confusing questions, then redesign it properly

beforeClass.en: Arrange in advance who the students may survey — another class, the office, the kitchen — and warn those adults it's coming. A survey with nobody to ask collapses halfway through the lesson. Set out paper, the two-colour pens and hardback books to lean on.
beforeClass.es: Arrange in advance who the students may survey — another class, the office, the kitchen — and warn those adults it's coming. A survey with nobody to ask collapses halfway through the lesson. Set out paper, the two-colour pens and hardback books to lean on.

runningLongOrShort.en: Long: cut the report to the graph and three bullet points. Short: add a second survey round after the product is adjusted.
runningLongOrShort.es: Long: cut the report to the graph and three bullet points. Short: add a second survey round after the product is adjusted.

beforeClass.en: Arrange in advance who the students may survey — another class, the office, the kitchen — and warn those adults it's coming. A survey with nobody to ask collapses halfway through the lesson. Set out scrap paper, a pencil, two crayons in different colors and a piece of cardboard from an old box for each student to lean on.
beforeClass.es: Arrange in advance who the students may survey — another class, the office, the kitchen — and warn those adults it's coming. focus: Single yes/no question surveys
Focus on counting yes vs. no
Simple tally marks in two colors: one for yes, one for no
Teacher-led graphing on board
Oral reporting ("5 said yes, 3 said no")
Basic vocabulary: survey, question, yes, no, count
2-3 simple questions
Practice writing answers neatly
Create simple bar graphs with teacher support
Compare numbers ("More people said yes than no")
Vocabulary expansion: survey, data, tally, graph, most, price, answer
3-5 questions with variety (yes/no, multiple choice, price range)
Make your own bar graph of the results
Calculate simple percentages (5 out of 10 = half)
Written analysis: "Most people want blue"
Vocabulary: market research, data analysis, results, survey, preference
5-7 detailed questions including open-ended
Create bar graphs for interest, price and features
Calculate percentages accurately (8/15 = 53%)
Written market research report with findings and recommendations
Compare hypothesis to results
Advanced vocabulary: hypothesis, percentage, data, feedback, market research

ell.label: English Language Learners
strategies: Give sentence frames: "Would you buy ___? How much would you pay for ___?"
Let students hold up their product sketch and point to it while asking.
Let students report results with numbers and fingers: "5 yes, 3 no."

learningDifferences.label: Students with Learning Differences
strategies: Cut the survey to one yes/no question with a tally box.
Pair students with a partner or adult while they collect answers.
Let students report results out loud instead of writing them.

advanced.label: Advanced Students
strategies: Add an open question, like "What would make it better?", and sort the answers into groups.
Work out what fraction or percentage said yes and compare it to a guess made before surveying.
Survey a second group, like another class, and compare the two results.

description.es: Review product plans from earlier lessons. Explain production goal: make your actual product today. Gather all materials needed. Set quality standards: careful work, attention to detail.

sayThis.es: "Today you make your product for real. Look at your plan. Get what you need. Work slow and neat — careful work is good work."

watchFor.en: Kids with no plan. Hand them the template and let them start.
watchFor.es: Kids with no plan. Hand them the template and let them start.

doneWhen.en: Every student has a plan or template and their materials on the desk.
doneWhen.es: Every student has a plan or template and their materials on the desk.

description.es: The whole class makes the same simple thing today. Show the finished one you made. Put the materials in one pile per table. No separate plans.

sayThis.en: "Today we all make this same thing. Here is mine, all done. Yours will look like this one. Work slow and neat."
sayThis.es: "Today we all make this same thing. Here is mine, all done. Yours will look like this one. Work slow and neat."

watchFor.es: Children grabbing materials before you finish talking. Materials stay in the middle of the table until you say go.

doneWhen.es: Every table has its pile of materials in the middle and every child is sitting with empty hands.

description.en: Students build their planned products using materials collected. Follow blueprints or plans. Work carefully and thoughtfully. Ask for help if stuck. Focus on quality craftsmanship. The teacher starts the timer and writes each student's finish time on the board.
description.es: Students build their planned products using materials collected. Follow blueprints or plans. Work carefully and thoughtfully. Ask for help if stuck. Focus on quality craftsmanship. The teacher starts the timer and writes each student's finish time on the board.

sayThis.en: "Build it the way your plan shows. The timer is on — hands up when you finish and I'll write your time on the board. Stuck? Try one more time, then put your hand up."
sayThis.es: "Build it the way your plan shows. The timer is on — hands up when you finish and I'll write your time on the board. Stuck? Try one more time, then put your hand up."

watchFor.en: Students who rush and are done in two minutes. Hold their product next to the plan and ask what is missing.
watchFor.es: Students who rush and are done in two minutes. Hold their product next to the plan and ask what is missing.

doneWhen.es: Every student has a built product that matches the plan, with a finish time on the board.

description.es: Children build the class item one step at a time. The teacher does a step, then the children do that step. No timer and no finish times on the board.

sayThis.en: "Watch me do step one. Now you do step one. Hands up when step one is done."
sayThis.es: "Watch me do step one. Now you do step one. Hands up when step one is done."

watchFor.es: Children racing ahead to step three. Say, "Hands flat on the desk until I show the next step."

doneWhen.es: Every child has done the last step and is holding their item up.

description.es: Students inspect their products: Does it look like the plan? Is it sturdy? Does it work as intended? Make improvements: fix weak spots, add finishing touches, smooth rough edges.

sayThis.en: "Now you are the checker. Does it look like your plan? Is it strong? Does it work? Find one thing to fix and fix it."
sayThis.es: "Now you are the checker. Does it look like your plan? Is it strong? Does it work? Find one thing to fix and fix it."

watchFor.en: "It's perfect." Ask them to find one weak spot and make it stronger.
watchFor.es: "It's perfect." Ask them to find one weak spot and make it stronger.

doneWhen.es: Every student has fixed at least one thing on their product.

description.es: Children hold their item next to the teacher's finished one and find one thing to fix. One thing only. Skip the talk about sturdy and working.

sayThis.en: "Hold yours next to mine. Find one thing to fix. Fix just that one thing."
sayThis.es: "Hold yours next to mine. Find one thing to fix. Fix just that one thing."

watchFor.es: Children who say theirs is already perfect. Point at one loose or empty spot and say, "Fix this bit."

description.es: Students show completed products. Explain: What they made, how they made it, what was challenging, what they're proud of. Display products for class to see. Discuss: What makes a quality product? How does handmade compare to factory-made?

sayThis.es: "Hold up what you made. Say what it is and one part you are proud of."

watchFor.es: Long speeches that eat the time. One sentence each, and the rest goes on display.

doneWhen.es: Every product is on display and each student has said one sentence about it.

sayThis.es: "Hold up what you made. Say one thing you like about it."

doneWhen.es: Every child has held their item up and said one thing about it.

sayThis.es: "Follow your blueprint step by step. Measure with your paper strip before you tear. Tape pieces so they hold. If something goes wrong, fix it and keep going."

watchFor.es: Tearing before measuring. Ask to see the pencil mark before the tearing starts.

description.es: Students conduct thorough quality checks: structural integrity, appearance, functionality. doneWhen.es: Every group has its materials and has counted what they cost, ten dollars or less.

watchFor.es: The Inspector waving everything through. Ask them to reject one and say why.

sayThis.es: "The timer is on. Build it like the plan. Inspector, check each one when it is done: does it match the plan? Is it strong? Is it neat?"

watchFor.es: The Inspector saying yes to everything. Ask them to find one that needs work and say why.

doneWhen.es: Every group has finished items, each one checked by the Inspector.

sayThis.es: "Two piles. Approved, and needs work. Inspector says which and says why. Nobody takes it personally — that's the job."

doneWhen.en: Every group's items are sorted into two counted piles.
doneWhen.es: Every group's items are sorted into two counted piles.

watchFor.en: Groups approving all of their own. Have one group inspect another group's pile.
watchFor.es: Groups approving all of their own. Have one group inspect another group's pile.

description.es: Quality Inspector presents finished items Class reviews: Does it match the plan? Is quality good? Would customers buy this? Separate "approved" vs. "needs improvement" items

sayThis.en: "You planned ten and made eight. You said ninety seconds and it took two minutes. That isn't failure — every factory finds this out. Now: cost per item is money spent divided by items approved. The rejects still cost you."
sayThis.es: "You planned ten and made eight. You said ninety seconds and it took two minutes. That isn't failure — every factory finds this out. Now: cost per item is money spent divided by items approved. The rejects still cost you."

doneWhen.es: Every Production Report shows planned against actual for both count and time, plus a cost per approved item.

watchFor.es: Dividing by everything made instead of everything approved. That difference is the whole lesson about waste.

description.en: Calculate actual vs. estimated production (made 8, planned 10) Calculate actual vs. estimated time (took 2 min each, estimated 1.5 min) Calculate actual cost per item (materials used ÷ items approved) Calculate "waste rate" if materials were rejected Complete Production Report form.
description.es: Calculate actual vs. estimated production (made 8, planned 10) Calculate actual vs. estimated time (took 2 min each, estimated 1.5 min) Calculate actual cost per item (materials used ÷ items approved) Calculate "waste rate" if materials were rejected Complete Production Report form.

description.es: Groups count how many they made and how many passed. They say which pile is bigger and whether they made more or fewer than their guess.

sayThis.en: "Count your approved pile. Count your needs-work pile. Which is bigger? You guessed a number at the start. Did you make more or fewer?"
sayThis.es: "Count your approved pile. Count your needs-work pile. Which is bigger? You guessed a number at the start. Did you make more or fewer?"

watchFor.en: Groups counting a piece twice. Move each piece to the side as you count it.
watchFor.es: Groups counting a piece twice. Move each piece to the side as you count it.

doneWhen.en: Every group has said how many passed, how many need work, and whether they beat their guess.
doneWhen.es: Every group has said how many passed, how many need work, and whether they beat their guess.

discussionQuestions: How did your actual production compare to your estimate?
What took longer than expected? Why?
Did quality go up or down as you got faster?
Which role was most important to success?
How did division of labor help your team?
What cost more than expected? What cost less?
If you were making 100 of these, what would you change?
How is this like the friends' experience in the workshop?

sayThis.en: "Your booth needs four things. A sign with your name. A price on everything. A story card saying how you made it and what you learned. And a cup to keep the money in. Prices come from what it cost you plus your time — not from what you wish it was worth."
sayThis.es: "Your booth needs four things. A sign with your name. A price on everything. A story card saying how you made it and what you learned. And a cup to keep the money in. Prices come from what it cost you plus your time — not from what you wish it was worth."

ell.label: English Language Learners
strategies: Put a small picture on each task card — a book stack, an airplane, a letter — and act out each task once before the timer starts.
Teach four words with gestures before the challenge: alone, help, team, done.
Let students answer the class count by pointing at the task on the board or holding up fingers.

learningDifferences.label: Students with Learning Differences
strategies: Give a shorter task list — three tasks — and count the student's results against that list.
Give quiet time checks every few minutes, or put a phone timer where the student can see it.
Offer a work spot away from the book stack if the busy stations are too much.

advanced.label: Advanced Students
strategies: Keep a time log: write the start and finish time for each task and find which one took longest.
Give each finished task a $1 value and work out the earnings for the whole challenge.
Design one more task card and predict how long it would take a classmate.
