doneWhen.es: Every student has written responses from at least five people.

watchFor.en: Research that is just asking a friend if it's a good idea. Require a number: how many said yes.
watchFor.es: Research that is just asking a friend if it's a good idea. Require a number: how many said yes.

description.en: Students conduct market research: Who are potential customers? What do they need? What exists already? Survey classmates. Analyze data to find market opportunity.
description.es: Students conduct market research: Who are potential customers? What do they need? What exists already? Survey classmates. Analyze data to find market opportunity.

description.en: Students ask five classmates "Would you buy this?" and make one tally mark on their paper for each yes.
description.es: Students ask five classmates "Would you buy this?" and make one tally mark on their paper for each yes.

sayThis.en: "Go and ask five friends: 'Would you buy this?' Make a tally mark for every yes. Your own yes doesn't count."
sayThis.es: "Go and ask five friends: 'Would you buy this?' Make a tally mark for every yes. Your own yes doesn't count."

watchFor.en: Kids asking the same friend five times. Send them to five different people.
watchFor.es: Kids asking the same friend five times. Send them to five different people.

doneWhen.en: Every student has asked five people and has a tally of the yeses.
doneWhen.es: Every student has asked five people and has a tally of the yeses.

sayThis.en: "Now the hard question. Somebody already sells something like this. Why would anyone pick yours? Cheaper, better, faster, or for a customer nobody's bothered with. Pick one and write it in a sentence."
sayThis.es: "Now the hard question. Somebody already sells something like this. Why would anyone pick yours? Cheaper, better, faster, or for a customer nobody's bothered with. Pick one and write it in a sentence."

doneWhen.en: Every plan has a one-sentence reason someone would choose it over what exists.
doneWhen.es: Every plan has a one-sentence reason someone would choose it over what exists.

watchFor.en: "Mine is just better" with nothing under it. Ask better at what, measured how.
watchFor.es: "Mine is just better" with nothing under it. Ask better at what, measured how.

description.en: Develop detailed product/service concept: What makes it unique? Why better than competition? What's the value proposition? Create product sketch or prototype plan.
description.es: Develop detailed product/service concept: What makes it unique? Why better than competition? What's the value proposition? Create product sketch or prototype plan.

description.en: Students draw their product and finish one sentence, out loud or on paper: People will pick mine because ___.
description.es: Students draw their product and finish one sentence, out loud or on paper: People will pick mine because ___.

sayThis.en: "Draw what you sell. Now think: why would a friend pick yours? Is it prettier, cheaper, or quicker? Finish the sentence: People will pick mine because ___."
sayThis.es: "Draw what you sell. Now think: why would a friend pick yours? Is it prettier, cheaper, or quicker? Finish the sentence: People will pick mine because ___."

watchFor.en: "Mine is the best" with no reason. Ask "Best how?" and let them pick one: prettier, cheaper or quicker.
watchFor.es: "Mine is the best" with no reason. Ask "Best how?" and let them pick one: prettier, cheaper or quicker.

doneWhen.en: Every plan has a picture and one reason someone would pick it.
doneWhen.es: Every plan has a picture and one reason someone would pick it.

sayThis.en: "Every cost, itemized. Then your price. Then the one that matters — how many do you have to sell before you stop losing money? That number is your break-even, and every real business owner knows theirs."
sayThis.es: "Every cost, itemized. Then your price. Then the one that matters — how many do you have to sell before you stop losing money? That number is your break-even, and every real business owner knows theirs."

doneWhen.en: Every plan shows itemized costs, a price, a margin and a break-even number for each product.
doneWhen.es: Every plan shows itemized costs, a price, a margin and a break-even number for each product.

watchFor.en: Costs that forget time, packaging or waste. Ask what happens to the ones that come out wrong.
watchFor.es: Costs that forget time, packaging or waste. Ask what happens to the ones that come out wrong.

description.en: Comprehensive financial plan for each product: itemized cost breakdown, pricing strategy, profit margin calculations, break-even analysis, sales forecasts. Create detailed budget.
description.es: Comprehensive financial plan for each product: itemized cost breakdown, pricing strategy, profit margin calculations, break-even analysis, sales forecasts. Create detailed budget.

description.en: Use one product with a cost and a price under $10. The teacher works out the profit on the board, and students copy the cost, the price and the profit onto their plan.
description.es: Use one product with a cost and a price under $10. The teacher works out the profit on the board, and students copy the cost, the price and the profit onto their plan.

sayThis.en: "Tell me what your product costs to make, and your price. Watch me on the board: the price, take away the cost, and that's the profit. Now copy the three numbers onto your plan."
sayThis.es: "Tell me what your product costs to make, and your price. Watch me on the board: the price, take away the cost, and that's the profit. Now copy the three numbers onto your plan."

watchFor.en: Kids copying numbers into the wrong spots. Label the three numbers on the board: cost, price, profit.
watchFor.es: Kids copying numbers into the wrong spots. Label the three numbers on the board: cost, price, profit.

doneWhen.en: Every plan shows a cost, a price and a profit for one product.
doneWhen.es: Every plan shows a cost, a price and a profit for one product.

sayThis.en: "Pull it together into one document, in order. Summary at the top, even though you write it last. Neat counts — if it looks careless, people assume the numbers are careless too."
sayThis.es: "Pull it together into one document, in order. Summary at the top, even though you write it last. Neat counts — if it looks careless, people assume the numbers are careless too."

doneWhen.en: Every plan has all four sections present with nothing blank.
doneWhen.es: Every plan has all four sections present with nothing blank.

watchFor.en: Sections left half-finished from earlier steps. A quick page check catches it.
watchFor.es: Sections left half-finished from earlier steps. A quick page check catches it.

description.en: Complete full written business plan with all sections: executive summary, product description, market analysis, financial projections. Professional formatting.
description.es: Complete full written business plan with all sections: executive summary, product description, market analysis, financial projections. Professional formatting.

description.en: Students put their plan on one page: the business name, a picture, the price and one sentence.
description.es: Students put their plan on one page: the business name, a picture, the price and one sentence.

sayThis.en: "Put it all on one page. Your business name at the top. A picture of what you sell. The price. One sentence: We sell ___."
sayThis.es: "Put it all on one page. Your business name at the top. A picture of what you sell. The price. One sentence: We sell ___."

watchFor.en: Pages with no price. A quick page check catches it.
watchFor.es: Pages with no price. A quick page check catches it.

doneWhen.en: Every plan has a name, a picture, a price and one sentence on one page.
doneWhen.es: Every plan has a name, a picture, a price and one sentence on one page.

sayThis.en: "Short and clear. What it is, who buys it, what you'll make. Lead with the number."
sayThis.es: "Short and clear. What it is, who buys it, what you'll make. Lead with the number."

doneWhen.en: Every plan has feedback written in pencil by at least one other person on it.
doneWhen.es: Every plan has feedback written in pencil by at least one other person on it.

watchFor.en: Presenters reading the whole plan aloud. Stop the first one at thirty seconds and set the pace.
watchFor.es: Presenters reading the whole plan aloud. Stop the first one at thirty seconds and set the pace.

description.en: Present business plans to class or small groups. Practice pitch: clear, persuasive, data-driven. Receive feedback for improvements.
description.es: Present business plans to class or small groups. Practice pitch: clear, persuasive, data-driven. Receive feedback for improvements.

description.en: Students show their one-page plan to a small group and say what they sell and the price. Listeners give a thumbs up if they would buy it and say one idea to make it better.
description.es: Students show their one-page plan to a small group and say what they sell and the price. Listeners give a thumbs up if they would buy it and say one idea to make it better.

sayThis.en: "Show your plan. Say what you sell and the price. Listeners, thumbs up if you'd buy it, and tell one idea to make it better."
sayThis.es: "Show your plan. Say what you sell and the price. Listeners, thumbs up if you'd buy it, and tell one idea to make it better."

watchFor.en: Presenters who freeze. Ask "What do you sell?" and let them point at the picture.
watchFor.es: Presenters who freeze. Ask "What do you sell?" and let them point at the picture.

doneWhen.en: Every student has shown a plan and heard one idea from a listener.
doneWhen.es: Every student has shown a plan and heard one idea from a listener.

discussionQuestions: What was the hardest part of making your business plan?
How did calculating costs change your pricing decisions?
In the story, Mr. Mason taught PRICE - COST = PROFIT. Why is this formula so important?
Why do you think Layla wanted order forms and pricing sheets written down?
What could go wrong if you DON'T make a plan first?" (Connect to Benny's mistake in CH1)
How does having clear roles prevent confusion and arguments?
extensionIdeas: Compare your business plan to a real kid business (lemonade stand, craft sale, dog walking)
Research: What business plans do adult businesses need? (Permits, insurance, marketing plans)
Create order form template like Layla made
Calculate: How many products would you need to sell to make $100 profit?

beforeClass.en: Print a real one-page business plan to hold up. Abstract structure is hard to picture; one page they can see makes it obvious. Decide who students may survey in step 2 and warn that class or adult beforehand.
beforeClass.es: Print a real one-page business plan to hold up. Abstract structure is hard to picture; one page they can see makes it obvious. Decide who students may survey in step 2 and warn that class or adult beforehand.

runningLongOrShort.en: Long: cut the presentations and have partners read each other's plans instead. Short: add a second financial pass where teams halve their price and see what breaks.
runningLongOrShort.es: Long: cut the presentations and have partners read each other's plans instead. Short: add a second financial pass where teams halve their price and see what breaks.

focus: Very simple template with pictures and fill-in-blanks
One product only
Prices from $1 to $5 counted out in paper clips
Teacher does most calculations on board, students copy
Focus on concepts: "We sell this. It costs this. We charge this."
Basic vocabulary: business, sell, cost, price, buy
Template with clear sections and sentence frames
A short list of ideas with the best one circled
Add up the materials list to get the cost
Work out profit for one item: price minus cost
Vocabulary expansion: profit, customer, materials, price, plan
Change one part of the plan after partner feedback
Multi-section template with calculation spaces
One chosen idea with costs and a profit worked out
Materials list with a cost written beside each item
Work out how many sales are needed to break even
Vocabulary: profit, break-even, materials, competition, pricing
Revise the plan using a partner's written feedback
Full written plan with all four sections filled in
Detailed cost breakdown for each product in the plan
Break-even number and sales forecast worked out
Profit margin analysis (what percentage profit?)
Advanced vocabulary: break-even, pricing strategy, target market, sales forecast, profit margin
Defend the plan to the class with data from it

ell.label: English Language Learners
strategies: Draw a small picture beside each board heading: a box for Product, a person for Customer, a dollar sign for Price.
Give the sentence frame: "Our business sells ___. It costs $___ to make. We charge $___."
Pair with a fluent speaker for the pricing and profit talk.

learningDifferences.label: Students with Learning Differences
strategies: Work one heading at a time and check it before moving to the next.
Give a ready-made cost list with round numbers, so the work is choosing, not searching.
Let students draw the product and customer parts instead of writing them.

advanced.label: Advanced Students
strategies: Work out how many sales it takes to earn back all the starting costs.
Try two prices, like $10 and $12, and compare the profit on ten sales.
Add a short plan for how customers will hear about the business.

description.es: Run the classroom store! Students rotate through roles: being cashier (taking clips, counting out change), stocking shelves, and being customers (shopping, paying). Each customer starts with 10 clips. Track sales.

sayThis.es: "The store is open! Customers, you have 10 clips. Count your clips into the cashier's hand. Cashier, count them again. When I say switch, change jobs."

discussionQuestions: What's the difference between revenue and profit?
In the story, 2 big jobs (shelf and mugs) were $63 of their $93 total. Why did Layla worry about that?
What if a customer is unhappy? How does that affect future business?
Why is it important to track EVERY transaction, not just the big ones?
If you were running a real store, what would you sell?
How did tips work in the story? Should tips go to profit or split among workers?

Compare Week 1 (this activity) to Week 2 (run the store again next week)

ell.label: English Language Learners
strategies: Write a big number and draw a coin on every price tag, so the price reads without words.
Practice three lines before the store opens: "How much is this?" "That's ___ dollars." "Thank you."
Pair with a fluent speaker for the first turn as cashier or shopkeeper.

learningDifferences.label: Students with Learning Differences
strategies: Give pre-counted clips or paper dollars that match the price of one item, so no change is needed.
Offer the stocker job to a student who finds handling money stressful.
Draw the sale steps on the board: choose, pay, count, write it down.

advanced.label: Advanced Students
strategies: Keep a running total on the log after every sale.
Use the cost of each item to find which item or department made the most profit.
Suggest one price change for next time and explain how it could change sales.

doneWhen.en: Every student has pointed at the angry face.
doneWhen.es: Every student has pointed at the angry face.

description.en: Turn to partner. Decide together: What's the BEST thing to say? What's the WORST thing to say?
description.es: Turn to partner. Decide together: What's the BEST thing to say? What's the WORST thing to say?

sayThis.en: "Turn to your partner. What is the BEST thing to say? What is the WORST thing to say? Pick one of each."
sayThis.es: "Turn to your partner. What is the BEST thing to say? What is the WORST thing to say? Pick one of each."

watchFor.en: Pairs having too much fun with the worst answer. At the halfway point, ask "Do you have your best one yet?"
watchFor.es: Pairs having too much fun with the worst answer. At the halfway point, ask "Do you have your best one yet?"

doneWhen.en: Every pair has one best answer and one worst answer ready.
doneWhen.es: Every pair has one best answer and one worst answer ready.

description.en: The teacher says two answers out loud first and the pairs pick the kind one. Skip the worst answer. Partners practice saying the kind one to each other.
description.es: The teacher says two answers out loud first and the pairs pick the kind one. Skip the worst answer. Partners practice saying the kind one to each other.

sayThis.en: "I will say two answers. One: 'I am sorry. I will fix it.' Two: 'That is not my problem.' Turn to your partner and say the kind one out loud."
sayThis.es: "I will say two answers. One: 'I am sorry. I will fix it.' Two: 'That is not my problem.' Turn to your partner and say the kind one out loud."

watchFor.en: Pairs having fun with the mean answer. Say, "We only practice the kind one," and say it with them.
watchFor.es: Pairs having fun with the mean answer. Say, "We only practice the kind one," and say it with them.

doneWhen.en: Every pair has said "I am sorry. I will fix it." out loud.
doneWhen.es: Every pair has said "I am sorry. I will fix it." out loud.

description.en: Pairs share their "best response." Teacher writes top 3 responses on board.
description.es: Pairs share their "best response." Teacher writes top 3 responses on board.

sayThis.en: "Tell us your best answer. I'll write the top three on the board. Listen for 'sorry' and 'I will fix it.'"
sayThis.es: "Tell us your best answer. I'll write the top three on the board. Listen for 'sorry' and 'I will fix it.'"

watchFor.en: Answers that blame the customer, like "You didn't tell me." Ask how the customer would feel hearing that.
watchFor.es: Answers that blame the customer, like "You didn't tell me." Ask how the customer would feel hearing that.

doneWhen.en: Three best answers are written on the board.
doneWhen.es: Three best answers are written on the board.

description.en: A few volunteers say the kind answer to the class. The teacher writes two answers on the board with a picture beside each. Not three.
description.es: A few volunteers say the kind answer to the class. The teacher writes two answers on the board with a picture beside each. Not three.

sayThis.en: "Who wants to say the kind answer to the whole class? I will write two on the board. Listen for the word sorry."
sayThis.es: "Who wants to say the kind answer to the whole class? I will write two on the board. Listen for the word sorry."

watchFor.en: Children who freeze in front of the class. Say the first words with them and let them finish.
watchFor.es: Children who freeze in front of the class. Say the first words with them and let them finish.

doneWhen.en: Two answers are written on the board and at least three students have said one out loud.
doneWhen.es: Two answers are written on the board and at least three students have said one out loud.

description.en: Quick repeat with new scenario. Faster decision-making.
description.es: Quick repeat with new scenario. Faster decision-making.

sayThis.en: "New problem. Be quick this time. Here it is. Partners, you have one minute to pick your best answer."
sayThis.es: "New problem. Be quick this time. Here it is. Partners, you have one minute to pick your best answer."

watchFor.en: Pairs copying a board answer word for word. That's fine if it fits. Ask them to add how they'd fix this problem.
watchFor.es: Pairs copying a board answer word for word. That's fine if it fits. Ask them to add how they'd fix this problem.

doneWhen.en: Two or three pairs have said a best answer for the new complaint.
doneWhen.es: Two or three pairs have said a best answer for the new complaint.

description.en: One new problem: the bookmark ripped. The whole class answers together out loud, not in pairs. No timer.
description.es: One new problem: the bookmark ripped. The whole class answers together out loud, not in pairs. No timer.

sayThis.en: "New problem. The bookmark ripped. Everybody together. Ready - I am sorry. I will fix it."
sayThis.es: "New problem. The bookmark ripped. Everybody together. Ready - I am sorry. I will fix it."

watchFor.en: A few kids saying nothing. Say it once more and have the whole class say it with you.
watchFor.es: A few kids saying nothing. Say it once more and have the whole class say it with you.

doneWhen.en: The whole class has said the answer out loud together.
doneWhen.es: The whole class has said the answer out loud together.

discussionQuestions: How would YOU feel if you ordered something and it was wrong?
What words make an unhappy customer feel better?
Is it better to argue or to fix the problem?

beforeClass.en: Choose the second complaint for Second Scenario before class, something just as simple, like a birthday card with the name spelled wrong. Put scrap paper and a pencil on each pair's desk for jotting or drawing their best and worst answer.
beforeClass.es: Choose the second complaint for Second Scenario before class, something just as simple, like a birthday card with the name spelled wrong. Put scrap paper and a pencil on each pair's desk for jotting or drawing their best and worst answer.

runningLongOrShort.en: Long: in Partner Discussion, skip the worst answer and have pairs find only the best thing to say. Short: in Second Scenario, have two pairs act out their answer for the class.
runningLongOrShort.es: Long: in Partner Discussion, skip the worst answer and have pairs find only the best thing to say. Short: in Second Scenario, have two pairs act out their answer for the class.

30.label: 30 Minutes

fromScratch.costPerStudent: $0 — everything is free or from home
fromScratch.description: Complaint cards and folded role names on scrap paper, a paper tracker for each student, and pencils. Nothing is bought.
items: Scrap paper — 32 pieces: 12 complaint cards the teacher writes (one per pair plus two extra) and 20 folded role names, Customer and Business Owner, one set per pair, free
Plain paper — 20 sheets, one per student for the response tracker
Pencils — 20, one per student for checking off the tracker

basicClassroom.costPerStudent: $0 — uses supplies the school already has
basicClassroom.description: Complaint cards and folded role names on scrap paper, a paper tracker for each student, and pencils.
items: Scrap paper — 32 pieces: 12 complaint cards the teacher writes (one per pair plus two extra) and 20 folded role names, Customer and Business Owner, one set per pair, free
Plain paper — 20 sheets, one per student for the response tracker
Pencils — 20, one per student for checking off the tracker

description.en: Teacher demonstrates WRONG way (arguing, blaming) vs. RIGHT way (listening, apologizing, solving). Exaggerate for humor and clarity.
description.es: Teacher demonstrates WRONG way (arguing, blaming) vs. RIGHT way (listening, apologizing, solving). Exaggerate for humor and clarity.

sayThis.en: "Watch me do it the wrong way first. Now watch me do it the right way. What was different?"
sayThis.es: "Watch me do it the wrong way first. Now watch me do it the right way. What was different?"

watchFor.en: The class still laughing when you start the right way. Do the good version slowly and quietly so it lands.
watchFor.es: The class still laughing when you start the right way. Do the good version slowly and quietly so it lands.

doneWhen.en: Students can name the three right moves: listen, say sorry, fix it.
doneWhen.es: Students can name the three right moves: listen, say sorry, fix it.

description.en: Pairs choose who's Customer first, who's Business Owner first.
description.es: Pairs choose who's Customer first, who's Business Owner first.

sayThis.en: "Pick who is the Customer first. The other one is the Business Owner. You'll switch later, so you both get both jobs."
sayThis.es: "Pick who is the Customer first. The other one is the Business Owner. You'll switch later, so you both get both jobs."

watchFor.en: Pairs arguing over who goes first. Settle it fast: the partner with the next birthday is the Customer.
watchFor.es: Pairs arguing over who goes first. Settle it fast: the partner with the next birthday is the Customer.

doneWhen.en: Every partner has a role name standing on the desk.
doneWhen.es: Every partner has a role name standing on the desk.

description.en: Customer reads their complaint from card. Business Owner responds. Aim for: Listen, Apologize, Solve.
description.es: Customer reads their complaint from card. Business Owner responds. Aim for: Listen, Apologize, Solve.

sayThis.en: "Customer, read your card. Business Owner, listen all the way to the end. Then say sorry and offer a fix."
sayThis.es: "Customer, read your card. Business Owner, listen all the way to the end. Then say sorry and offer a fix."

watchFor.en: Business Owners jumping in before the complaint is finished. Remind them: listen to the whole card first.
watchFor.es: Business Owners jumping in before the complaint is finished. Remind them: listen to the whole card first.

doneWhen.en: Every pair has finished one complaint with a fix offered.
doneWhen.es: Every pair has finished one complaint with a fix offered.

description.en: Partners swap roles. New scenario card. Repeat.
description.es: Partners swap roles. New scenario card. Repeat.

sayThis.en: "Switch jobs. New card. Same three moves: listen, say sorry, fix it."
sayThis.es: "Switch jobs. New card. Same three moves: listen, say sorry, fix it."

watchFor.en: Customers playing it angry for laughs. Ask them to sound like a real upset customer.
watchFor.es: Customers playing it angry for laughs. Ask them to sound like a real upset customer.

doneWhen.en: Every student has played both roles.
doneWhen.es: Every student has played both roles.

description.en: "What responses worked best? Which ones made the customer feel heard?"
description.es: "What responses worked best? Which ones made the customer feel heard?"

sayThis.en: "Which answers worked best? Customers, which one made you feel heard? What did the Business Owner say?"
sayThis.es: "Which answers worked best? Customers, which one made you feel heard? What did the Business Owner say?"

watchFor.en: The funniest answer getting picked. Ask the Customers which answer made them feel better.
watchFor.es: The funniest answer getting picked. Ask the Customers which answer made them feel better.

doneWhen.en: Two or three answers that worked are shared with the class.
doneWhen.es: Two or three answers that worked are shared with the class.

description.en: Students check off on worksheet: "I listened ☐ I apologized ☐ I offered a solution ☐"
description.es: Students check off on worksheet: "I listened ☐ I apologized ☐ I offered a solution ☐"

sayThis.en: "On your paper, check off what you really did. I listened. I said sorry. I offered a fix. Be honest."
sayThis.es: "On your paper, check off what you really did. I listened. I said sorry. I offered a fix. Be honest."

watchFor.en: Every move checked by everyone. Ask a few students to tell a partner what their fix was.
watchFor.es: Every move checked by everyone. Ask a few students to tell a partner what their fix was.

doneWhen.en: Every student has checked or left blank each of the three moves on the tracker.
doneWhen.es: Every student has checked or left blank each of the three moves on the tracker.

discussionQuestions: Was it hard to stay calm when the customer complained?
How did it feel to BE the unhappy customer?
What's the difference between 'I'm sorry' and 'It's not my fault'?
Would you shop there again if they fixed your problem nicely?
What if the customer is WRONG but still upset?
extensionIdeas: Create a class "Customer Service Rules" poster with student-generated ideas.

beforeClass.en: Write twelve short complaints on scrap-paper cards, one for each pair and two extra, mixing three kinds: something broken, something wrong, something late. For Switch & Round 2, pairs trade cards with the pair next to them. Fold paper role names, Customer and Business Owner, one set per pair. Have blank paper and a pencil ready for each student's tracker: I listened, I apologized, I offered a solution.
beforeClass.es: Write twelve short complaints on scrap-paper cards, one for each pair and two extra, mixing three kinds: something broken, something wrong, something late. For Switch & Round 2, pairs trade cards with the pair next to them. Fold paper role names, Customer and Business Owner, one set per pair. Have blank paper and a pencil ready for each student's tracker: I listened, I apologized, I offered a solution.

runningLongOrShort.en: Long: cut Class Debrief to one question: which answer made the customer feel heard? Short: after Switch & Round 2, give each pair one more card and switch roles again.
runningLongOrShort.es: Long: cut Class Debrief to one question: which answer made the customer feel heard? Short: after Switch & Round 2, give each pair one more card and switch roles again.

45.label: 45 Minutes
45.activityName: Complete Customer Service Training with Cost Analysis

fromScratch.costPerStudent: $0 — everything is free or from home
fromScratch.description: Printed observer rubrics and cost worksheets on plain paper, complaint cards and certificates on scrap paper, pencils and the board. Nothing is bought.
items: Plain paper — 48 sheets: 21 printed observer rubrics (three per group of three, 7 groups, the back used for round two), 20 cost worksheets (one per student), and 7 for the group rules
Scrap paper — 47 pieces: 42 complaint cards the teacher writes (three per group for each round) and 5 Excellent Service certificates, free
Pencils — 20, one per student for the rubric scores, the cost worksheet and the group rules
Board — teacher, for the one-becomes-ten picture, the three L's and the Tier 1 rules

basicClassroom.costPerStudent: $0 — uses supplies the school already has
basicClassroom.description: Printed observer rubrics and cost worksheets on plain paper, complaint cards and certificates on scrap paper, pencils and the board.
items: Plain paper — 48 sheets: 21 printed observer rubrics (three per group of three, 7 groups, the back used for round two), 20 cost worksheets (one per student), and 7 for the group rules
Scrap paper — 47 pieces: 42 complaint cards the teacher writes (three per group for each round) and 5 Excellent Service certificates, free
Pencils — 20, one per student for the rubric scores, the cost worksheet and the group rules
Board — teacher, for the one-becomes-ten picture, the three L's and the Tier 1 rules

sayThis.en: "Riley's mistake cost sixteen dollars in materials and left two dollars of profit. Now the worse part: an unhappy customer tells about ten people. One mistake, ten people who never come."
sayThis.es: "Riley's mistake cost sixteen dollars in materials and left two dollars of profit. Now the worse part: an unhappy customer tells about ten people. One mistake, ten people who never come."

doneWhen.en: The one-becomes-ten picture is on the board with a dollar figure beside it.
doneWhen.es: The one-becomes-ten picture is on the board with a dollar figure beside it.

watchFor.en: Bad service treated as just rude rather than expensive. Keep the number in front of them.
watchFor.es: Bad service treated as just rude rather than expensive. Keep the number in front of them.

description.en: Discuss: "Riley's mistake cost them $16 in materials and only $2 profit left. Let's calculate costs of bad service." Mini-lesson: One unhappy customer tells 10 people. Show visual of 1 person becoming 10 lost customers.
description.es: Discuss: "Riley's mistake cost them $16 in materials and only $2 profit left. Let's calculate costs of bad service." Mini-lesson: One unhappy customer tells 10 people. Show visual of 1 person becoming 10 lost customers.

sayThis.en: "Three L's. Listen — don't interrupt, even when they're wrong. Learn — ask questions until you understand. Love — fix it and mean it. Watch me do it badly first, then properly."
sayThis.es: "Three L's. Listen — don't interrupt, even when they're wrong. Learn — ask questions until you understand. Love — fix it and mean it. Watch me do it badly first, then properly."

doneWhen.en: The three L's are on the board and both versions have been acted out.
doneWhen.es: The three L's are on the board and both versions have been acted out.

watchFor.en: Laughter at the bad version drowning out the good one. Do the good version second and in silence.
watchFor.es: Laughter at the bad version drowning out the good one. Do the good version second and in silence.

description.en: Teacher models the 3 L's: LISTEN (don't interrupt), LEARN (ask questions to understand), LOVE (fix it with care) Show both defensive response and excellent response side-by-side
description.es: Teacher models the 3 L's: LISTEN (don't interrupt), LEARN (ask questions to understand), LOVE (fix it with care) Show both defensive response and excellent response side-by-side

sayThis.en: "Three of you. One complains, one runs the business, one watches with the sheet. Two minutes, then rotate. Observers — you score, you don't join in."
sayThis.es: "Three of you. One complains, one runs the business, one watches with the sheet. Two minutes, then rotate. Observers — you score, you don't join in."

doneWhen.en: Every group has three completed rubric sheets, one per role rotation.
doneWhen.es: Every group has three completed rubric sheets, one per role rotation.

watchFor.en: Observers joining the scene. Give them the sheet and a pencil and it usually holds.
watchFor.es: Observers joining the scene. Give them the sheet and a pencil and it usually holds.

description.en: Groups of 3: Customer, Business Owner, Observer Observer uses rubric to score response (Did they listen? Apologize? Solve?) 2 minutes per scenario, then switch roles.
description.es: Groups of 3: Customer, Business Owner, Observer Observer uses rubric to score response (Did they listen? Apologize? Solve?) 2 minutes per scenario, then switch roles.

description.en: Groups of 3: Customer, Business Owner, Observer. The teacher reads a simple complaint card, the Customer says it, and the Business Owner answers. The Observer gives a thumbs up for each move they saw: listen, say sorry, fix it. Then switch roles.
description.es: Groups of 3: Customer, Business Owner, Observer. The teacher reads a simple complaint card, the Customer says it, and the Business Owner answers. The Observer gives a thumbs up for each move they saw: listen, say sorry, fix it. Then switch roles.

sayThis.en: "Three of you. One is the Customer, one is the Business Owner, one watches. Watcher, give a thumbs up for each thing you see: listening, saying sorry, fixing it. Then switch."
sayThis.es: "Three of you. One is the Customer, one is the Business Owner, one watches. Watcher, give a thumbs up for each thing you see: listening, saying sorry, fixing it. Then switch."

watchFor.en: Watchers joining in the play. Remind them their job is thumbs, not talking.
watchFor.es: Watchers joining in the play. Remind them their job is thumbs, not talking.

doneWhen.en: Every student in each group has had a turn as Customer, Business Owner and Observer.
doneWhen.es: Every student in each group has had a turn as Customer, Business Owner and Observer.

sayThis.en: "Harder now. This customer is angry, or wants money back, or wants it free. Same three L's. Staying calm when they're not is the actual skill."
sayThis.es: "Harder now. This customer is angry, or wants money back, or wants it free. Same three L's. Staying calm when they're not is the actual skill."

doneWhen.en: Every group has scored all three of the harder scenarios.
doneWhen.es: Every group has scored all three of the harder scenarios.

watchFor.en: Anger played as comedy. Ask them to do it like they mean it, once.
watchFor.es: Anger played as comedy. Ask them to do it like they mean it, once.

description.en: Increase difficulty (angry customer, customer asking for refund, customer wants free replacement) Same rotation, new roles for each
description.es: Increase difficulty (angry customer, customer asking for refund, customer wants free replacement) Same rotation, new roles for each

sayThis.en: "Plate cost eight dollars. Riley made it twice, so sixteen. Profit dropped from ten to two. Now the big one — if one unhappy customer tells ten people and each would have spent twenty dollars, what did that mistake really cost?"
sayThis.es: "Plate cost eight dollars. Riley made it twice, so sixteen. Profit dropped from ten to two. Now the big one — if one unhappy customer tells ten people and each would have spent twenty dollars, what did that mistake really cost?"

doneWhen.en: Every worksheet has all the scenarios calculated, including the lost-future-business one.
doneWhen.es: Every worksheet has all the scenarios calculated, including the lost-future-business one.

watchFor.en: Students stopping at the materials number. The two hundred is the point of the exercise.
watchFor.es: Students stopping at the materials number. The two hundred is the point of the exercise.

description.en: Worksheet: "The plate cost $8 to make. Riley remade it ($8 more). Profit went from $10 to $2. How much did the mistake cost?" Calculate: "If an unhappy customer tells 10 people and each would have spent $20, how much future business did you lose?" ($200) Students complete 3-4 cost scenarios.
description.es: Worksheet: "The plate cost $8 to make. Riley remade it ($8 more). Profit went from $10 to $2. How much did the mistake cost?" Calculate: "If an unhappy customer tells 10 people and each would have spent $20, how much future business did you lose?" ($200) Students complete 3-4 cost scenarios.

description.en: The plate cost $8 to make, and Riley had to make it twice. Students draw 8 tally marks for the first plate and 8 more for the second, then count them all. The teacher draws one unhappy customer and ten friends on the board to show who hears about it.
description.es: The plate cost $8 to make, and Riley had to make it twice. Students draw 8 tally marks for the first plate and 8 more for the second, then count them all. The teacher draws one unhappy customer and ten friends on the board to show who hears about it.

sayThis.en: "The plate cost eight dollars. Riley made it two times. Draw eight tally marks for the first plate. Now eight more for the second. Count them all. How many dollars did the mistake cost?"
sayThis.es: "The plate cost eight dollars. Riley made it two times. Draw eight tally marks for the first plate. Now eight more for the second. Count them all. How many dollars did the mistake cost?"

watchFor.en: Kids losing count of the tally marks. Have them draw the marks in bundles of five.
watchFor.es: Kids losing count of the tally marks. Have them draw the marks in bundles of five.

doneWhen.en: Every student has counted 16 tally marks and can say the mistake cost $16.
doneWhen.es: Every student has counted 16 tally marks and can say the mistake cost $16.

sayThis.en: "Write two or three rules that stop the complaint happening at all. Riley's was show a drawing first. A rule beats an apology every time, because it happens before anything goes wrong."
sayThis.es: "Write two or three rules that stop the complaint happening at all. Riley's was show a drawing first. A rule beats an apology every time, because it happens before anything goes wrong."

doneWhen.en: Every group has at least two written rules, each naming a specific action.
doneWhen.es: Every group has at least two written rules, each naming a specific action.

watchFor.en: Rules that are just "be nice". A rule has to name an action and when it happens.
watchFor.es: Rules that are just "be nice". A rule has to name an action and when it happens.

description.en: Small groups write 2-3 "business rules" to prevent complaints (like Riley's "show a drawing first" rule) Examples: "Ask 3 questions before starting work," "Let customer approve samples," "Check finished work before delivering".
description.es: Small groups write 2-3 "business rules" to prevent complaints (like Riley's "show a drawing first" rule) Examples: "Ask 3 questions before starting work," "Let customer approve samples," "Check finished work before delivering".

description.en: Each group thinks of one rule that stops a complaint before it happens, like Riley's "show a drawing first" rule. Each group says its rule out loud, and the teacher writes it on the board.
description.es: Each group thinks of one rule that stops a complaint before it happens, like Riley's "show a drawing first" rule. Each group says its rule out loud, and the teacher writes it on the board.

sayThis.en: "Riley's rule was: show a drawing first. What is one rule that stops a customer getting upset? Tell me, and I'll write it on the board."
sayThis.es: "Riley's rule was: show a drawing first. What is one rule that stops a customer getting upset? Tell me, and I'll write it on the board."

watchFor.en: Rules that are just "be nice". Ask what you would do, and when.
watchFor.es: Rules that are just "be nice". Ask what you would do, and when.

doneWhen.en: Every group has one rule written on the board.
doneWhen.es: Every group has one rule written on the board.

sayThis.en: "Certificates from the observer scores, not from me. Then three votes — best problem-solver, calmest under pressure, best listener."
sayThis.es: "Certificates from the observer scores, not from me. Then three votes — best problem-solver, calmest under pressure, best listener."

doneWhen.en: Certificates are handed out and all three class votes are counted.
doneWhen.es: Certificates are handed out and all three class votes are counted.

watchFor.en: Votes going to the loudest performer. Point back at the rubric sheets.
watchFor.es: Votes going to the loudest performer. Point back at the rubric sheets.

description.en: Give "Excellent Service" certificates to students who scored highest on Observer rubrics Class votes: "Best problem-solver," "Calmest under pressure," "Best listener"
description.es: Give "Excellent Service" certificates to students who scored highest on Observer rubrics Class votes: "Best problem-solver," "Calmest under pressure," "Best listener"

discussionQuestions: Why did Riley's beautiful plate get rejected even though it was good quality?
What questions should Riley have asked BEFORE painting the plate?
How much did the mistake cost? Just the $16 in materials, or more?
Ellis fixed his birdhouse before the customer even noticed. Why was that smart?
What does 'the customer is always right' mean? Are they REALLY always right?
How can one unhappy customer hurt your business even if you fix their problem?
What's the difference between a refund, a redo, and a discount?
If you handle a complaint really well, can that customer become MORE loyal than before?
extensionIdeas: Write "apology letters" for different complaint scenarios
Research real company customer service policies (Zappos, Amazon)
Create a customer service training video for younger students
Track: How many complaints does your favorite store/restaurant handle? Interview staff.
Design a "Customer Satisfaction Survey" for a real or imaginary business
Role-play increasingly difficult scenarios (screaming customer, customer who's clearly wrong, customer asking for unreasonable demands)

beforeClass.en: Print the observer rubric on plain paper, three per group of three, and read it yourself first — the observer role collapses if the sheet isn't clear. Have the round-one complaints and the harder round-two scenarios written on scrap-paper cards, face down. Print or hand-copy a paper cost worksheet for each student, and have scrap paper ready for the certificates.
beforeClass.es: Print the observer rubric on plain paper, three per group of three, and read it yourself first — the observer role collapses if the sheet isn't clear. Have the round-one complaints and the harder round-two scenarios written on scrap-paper cards, face down. Print or hand-copy a paper cost worksheet for each student, and have scrap paper ready for the certificates.

runningLongOrShort.en: Long: cut round two to one scenario each. Short: add a round where the observer plays a second, watching customer who decides whether they'd come back.
runningLongOrShort.es: Long: cut round two to one scenario each. Short: add a round where the observer plays a second, watching customer who decides whether they'd come back.

focus: Very simple scenarios: "The colors are wrong. What do you say?"
Focus on polite language: "I'm sorry. I will fix it."
Teacher heavily models responses before student practice
Observer gives a thumbs up for each move they see
Basic vocabulary: sorry, fix, listen, customer
Slightly complex scenarios: "The customer wanted red but you gave them blue."
Introduce the 3-step response: listen, apologize, fix
Play both roles: Customer and Business Owner
Vocabulary expansion: apologize, solution, mistake, complaint, listen
Scenarios scored by an Observer using a rubric
Add clarifying questions: "Can you tell me more about what you expected?"
Handle the harder asks: refund or free replacement
Vocabulary: refund, replacement, rubric, complaint, service
Complex, emotionally charged scenarios: "The customer is yelling and demanding a refund."
Practice de-escalation techniques (staying calm, validating feelings, offering choices)
Cost analysis: Calculate financial impact of complaints and lost customers
Write two or three service rules that prevent complaints
Advanced vocabulary: complaint, profit, lost business, service policy, rubric

ell.label: English Language Learners
strategies: Act out each complaint with a face and a gesture before reading it, so the problem is clear without every word.
Give the sentence frame: "I am sorry that ___. I will ___ to fix it."
Pair with a fluent speaker who reads the complaint card first.

learningDifferences.label: Students with Learning Differences
strategies: Put a picture cue card on the desk with the three moves: listen, say sorry, fix it.
Let an anxious student watch one round first, then join as the Customer reading from a card.
Give complaints with one clear problem and one clear fix.

advanced.label: Advanced Students
strategies: Write two new complaint cards from real life for the next round.
Act as observer and write one sentence of feedback for each Business Owner.
Work out what one lost customer costs if they would have spent $5 a week for ten weeks.

fromScratch.costPerStudent: $0 — everything is free or from home
fromScratch.description: Two desk stores sell paper bookmarks, pencils and erasers, with taped paper signs and price signs on scrap paper. Customers pay with scrap-paper coins, and the teacher lists the reasons on the board.
items: Plain paper — 6 sheets, free: 4 torn into 16 strip bookmarks as store goods (8 per store), 2 for the Store A and Store B signs
Pencils and erasers — 4 of each from the classroom, 2 per store as store goods, returned afterwards
Scrap paper — about 56 pieces, free: 6 for the price signs (3 per store), 48 torn into coins (8 per customer for the teacher and about 5 volunteers), 2 for the tally marks
Tape — 1 roll, shared, to tape a sign on each store

basicClassroom.costPerStudent: $0 — uses supplies the school already has
basicClassroom.description: Two desk stores sell paper bookmarks, pencils and erasers, with taped paper signs and index-card price signs. Customers pay with paper clips, stores tally on scrap paper, and the teacher lists the reasons on the board.
items: Plain paper — 6 sheets: 4 torn into 16 strip bookmarks as store goods (8 per store), 2 for the Store A and Store B signs
Pencils and erasers — 4 of each from the classroom, 2 per store as store goods, returned afterwards
Index cards — 6, 3 per store for the matching price signs (Tier 1: 2 cards, one price sign per store)
Tape — 1 roll, shared, to tape a sign on each store
Scrap paper — 2 pieces, one per store for the tally marks
Paper clips — about 50, 8 per customer for the teacher and about 5 volunteers, collected back in
Board — teacher, for the customer counts and the list of reasons

description.en: Split class in half. Each side is a store selling the same items (pencils, erasers, bookmarks). Both stores set same prices. Emphasize: prices are identical.
description.es: Split class in half. Each side is a store selling the same items (pencils, erasers, bookmarks). Both stores set same prices. Emphasize: prices are identical.

sayThis.en: "Half of you are Store A. Half of you are Store B. You sell the same things for the same prices. Look: a bookmark is $1 here, and $1 there."
sayThis.es: "Half of you are Store A. Half of you are Store B. You sell the same things for the same prices. Look: a bookmark is $1 here, and $1 there."

watchFor.en: A store quietly lowering a price. Read both sets of price signs out loud and make them match.
watchFor.es: A store quietly lowering a price. Read both sets of price signs out loud and make them match.

doneWhen.en: Both stores have the same goods and the same price signs on the desk.
doneWhen.es: Both stores have the same goods and the same price signs on the desk.

description.en: Split the class in half. Both stores sell one thing only - bookmarks - and both cost one clip. Same thing, same price, so there is nothing to compare but the store.
description.es: Split the class in half. Both stores sell one thing only - bookmarks - and both cost one clip. Same thing, same price, so there is nothing to compare but the store.

sayThis.en: "This half is Store A. This half is Store B. You both sell bookmarks. A bookmark costs one clip here, and one clip there. Same thing, same price."
sayThis.es: "This half is Store A. This half is Store B. You both sell bookmarks. A bookmark costs one clip here, and one clip there. Same thing, same price."

watchFor.en: A store saying theirs costs less. Point at both signs and say the price is the same at both stores.
watchFor.es: A store saying theirs costs less. Point at both signs and say the price is the same at both stores.

doneWhen.en: Both stores have their bookmarks out and the same price sign on the desk.
doneWhen.es: Both stores have their bookmarks out and the same price sign on the desk.

description.en: Give stores 3 minutes to make their store different WITHOUT changing prices. Options: better signs, friendly greeting, organized display, sample item, etc.
description.es: Give stores 3 minutes to make their store different WITHOUT changing prices. Options: better signs, friendly greeting, organized display, sample item, etc.

sayThis.en: "You can't change your prices. But you can make people want to come to YOUR store. Make a better sign. Say hello. Make it neat. You have three minutes."
sayThis.es: "You can't change your prices. But you can make people want to come to YOUR store. Make a better sign. Say hello. Make it neat. You have three minutes."

watchFor.en: A store offering "two for one." That's a price change. Send them back to signs, greetings and a neat display.
watchFor.es: A store offering "two for one." That's a price change. Send them back to signs, greetings and a neat display.

doneWhen.en: Each store has made at least one change a customer can see or hear.
doneWhen.es: Each store has made at least one change a customer can see or hear.

description.en: Each store picks ONE way to be different from three the teacher reads out: a big sign, saying hello, or lining the bookmarks up neatly. One choice only.
description.es: Each store picks ONE way to be different from three the teacher reads out: a big sign, saying hello, or lining the bookmarks up neatly. One choice only.

sayThis.en: "You cannot change your price. Pick one way to be different. A big sign. Saying hello. Or making it neat. Pick one and do it now."
sayThis.es: "You cannot change your price. Pick one way to be different. A big sign. Saying hello. Or making it neat. Pick one and do it now."

watchFor.en: Stores trying all three and finishing none. Say, "Pick one," and point at the one they started.
watchFor.es: Stores trying all three and finishing none. Say, "Pick one," and point at the one they started.

doneWhen.en: Each store has done one thing a customer can see or hear.
doneWhen.es: Each store has done one thing a customer can see or hear.

description.en: Teacher and volunteers act as customers, each carrying 8 paper clips as coins. Customers choose which store to visit. Stores track how many customers they get with tally marks on scrap paper. No price changes allowed.
description.es: Teacher and volunteers act as customers, each carrying 8 paper clips as coins. Customers choose which store to visit. Stores track how many customers they get with tally marks on scrap paper. No price changes allowed.

sayThis.en: "Customers, you each have 8 clips. Pick a store and buy something. Stores, make a tally mark for every customer who comes."
sayThis.es: "Customers, you each have 8 clips. Pick a store and buy something. Stores, make a tally mark for every customer who comes."

watchFor.en: Customers going wherever their friends are. Ask one customer out loud, "What made you pick that store?"
watchFor.es: Customers going wherever their friends are. Ask one customer out loud, "What made you pick that store?"

doneWhen.en: Both stores have a tally of their customers.
doneWhen.es: Both stores have a tally of their customers.

description.en: Teacher and volunteers act as customers, each carrying 8 scrap-paper squares as coins. Customers choose which store to visit. Stores track how many customers they get with tally marks on scrap paper. No price changes allowed.
description.es: Teacher and volunteers act as customers, each carrying 8 scrap-paper squares as coins. Customers choose which store to visit. Stores track how many customers they get with tally marks on scrap paper. No price changes allowed.

sayThis.en: "Customers, you each have 8 paper coins. Pick a store and buy something. Stores, make a tally mark for every customer who comes."
sayThis.es: "Customers, you each have 8 paper coins. Pick a store and buy something. Stores, make a tally mark for every customer who comes."

description.en: The teacher and a few volunteers shop with 3 clips each, not 8. Stores drop one clip in a cup for every customer instead of making tally marks.
description.es: The teacher and a few volunteers shop with 3 clips each, not 8. Stores drop one clip in a cup for every customer instead of making tally marks.

sayThis.en: "Customers, you have three clips. Walk to the store you like and buy a bookmark. Stores, put one clip in your cup every time someone comes."
sayThis.es: "Customers, you have three clips. Walk to the store you like and buy a bookmark. Stores, put one clip in your cup every time someone comes."

doneWhen.en: Both stores have clips in their cup.
doneWhen.es: Both stores have clips in their cup.

description.en: Count customers for each store. Discuss: Which store got more customers? Why? What made you choose one store over the other? List factors on board.
description.es: Count customers for each store. Discuss: Which store got more customers? Why? What made you choose one store over the other? List factors on board.

sayThis.en: "Count your tally marks. Which store got more customers? Customers, why did you pick that store?"
sayThis.es: "Count your tally marks. Which store got more customers? Customers, why did you pick that store?"

watchFor.en: "My friend is there" as the only reason. Write it down, then ask what else they noticed.
watchFor.es: "My friend is there" as the only reason. Write it down, then ask what else they noticed.

doneWhen.en: Customer counts for both stores and a list of reasons are on the board.
doneWhen.es: Customer counts for both stores and a list of reasons are on the board.

description.en: Count each store's clips out loud together. One question: which store got more? Then ask two customers why. No list of reasons on the board.
description.es: Count each store's clips out loud together. One question: which store got more? Then ask two customers why. No list of reasons on the board.

sayThis.en: "Let's count. Store A, hold up your cup. Count with me. Now Store B. Which store got more? Who can tell me why you picked that one?"
sayThis.es: "Let's count. Store A, hold up your cup. Count with me. Now Store B. Which store got more? Who can tell me why you picked that one?"

watchFor.en: "My friend was there" as the only reason. Say that counts, then ask what else they saw at that store.
watchFor.es: "My friend was there" as the only reason. Say that counts, then ask what else they saw at that store.

doneWhen.en: Both counts are written on the board and at least two customers have said why they picked their store.
doneWhen.es: Both counts are written on the board and at least two customers have said why they picked their store.

discussionQuestions: Both stores had the same prices. Why did one store get more customers?
Did the price matter, or did something else matter more?
Would you rather buy the cheapest thing or something special that costs a little more?

beforeClass.en: Push desks together into two stores and tape a paper sign on each: Store A and Store B. Give both stores the same goods, paper bookmarks plus a few classroom pencils and erasers, and the same price signs written on index cards. Count 8 paper clips for each customer.
beforeClass.es: Push desks together into two stores and tape a paper sign on each: Store A and Store B. Give both stores the same goods, paper bookmarks plus a few classroom pencils and erasers, and the same price signs written on index cards. Count 8 paper clips for each customer.

runningLongOrShort.en: Long: end the Shopping Round once every customer has bought one thing. Short: in Discussion, ask each store for one more change they would make next time.
runningLongOrShort.es: Long: end the Shopping Round once every customer has bought one thing. Short: in Discussion, ask each store for one more change they would make next time.

beforeClass.en: Push desks together into two stores and tape a paper sign on each: Store A and Store B. Give both stores the same goods, paper bookmarks plus a few classroom pencils and erasers, and the same price signs written on scrap paper. Tear scrap paper into small squares and count 8 paper coins for each customer.
beforeClass.es: Push desks together into two stores and tape a paper sign on each: Store A and Store B. Give both stores the same goods, paper bookmarks plus a few classroom pencils and erasers, and the same price signs written on scrap paper. Tear scrap paper into small squares and count 8 paper coins for each customer.

sayThis.es: "Half the class is one store. Half is the other. You sell the same things at the same prices. Check the other store's price signs. They must match yours."

watchFor.en: Stores decorating before the goods and prices are set. Setup is goods and price signs only; making it special comes next.
watchFor.es: Stores decorating before the goods and prices are set. Setup is goods and price signs only; making it special comes next.

sayThis.en: "Three minutes to stand out. No price changes. Make a sign, a business card, a greeting, a neat display. What will make a customer pick you?"
sayThis.es: "Three minutes to stand out. No price changes. Make a sign, a business card, a greeting, a neat display. What will make a customer pick you?"

watchFor.en: Deals sneaking in, like a free bookmark with every pencil. That changes the price. Send them back to looks, service and signs.

description.es: Teacher and volunteers act as customers, each carrying 8 paper clips as coins. Customers choose which store to visit. Stores track how many customers they get with tally marks on scrap paper. No price changes allowed.

sayThis.en: "Customers, you have 8 clips each. Look at both stores, then choose where to buy. Stores, keep a tally of every customer."
sayThis.es: "Customers, you have 8 clips each. Look at both stores, then choose where to buy. Stores, keep a tally of every customer."

watchFor.en: Store workers leaving the desk to chase customers. Keep them at the store. The store has to bring customers in.
watchFor.es: Store workers leaving the desk to chase customers. Keep them at the store. The store has to bring customers in.

doneWhen.en: Both stores have a customer tally and the clips they took in.
doneWhen.es: Both stores have a customer tally and the clips they took in.

description.en: Teacher and volunteers act as customers, each carrying 8 scrap-paper squares as coins. Customers choose which store to visit. Stores track how many customers they get with tally marks on scrap paper. No price changes allowed.
description.es: Teacher and volunteers act as customers, each carrying 8 scrap-paper squares as coins. Customers choose which store to visit. Stores track how many customers they get with tally marks on scrap paper. No price changes allowed.

sayThis.en: "Customers, you have 8 paper coins each. Look at both stores, then choose where to buy. Stores, keep a tally of every customer."
sayThis.es: "Customers, you have 8 paper coins each. Look at both stores, then choose where to buy. Stores, keep a tally of every customer."

doneWhen.en: Both stores have a customer tally and the paper coins they took in.
doneWhen.es: Both stores have a customer tally and the paper coins they took in.

description.en: Count customers for each store. Discuss: Which store got more customers? Why? What made you choose one store over the other? List factors on board.
description.es: Count customers for each store. Discuss: Which store got more customers? Why? What made you choose one store over the other? List factors on board.

sayThis.en: "Count your customers. Which store got more? Customers, tell us why you chose it. I'll list every reason."
sayThis.es: "Count your customers. Which store got more? Customers, tell us why you chose it. I'll list every reason."

watchFor.en: The winning store cheering and the other store going quiet. Ask the smaller store what they would change next time.
watchFor.es: The winning store cheering and the other store going quiet. Ask the smaller store what they would change next time.

doneWhen.en: Both counts and at least four reasons are on the board.
doneWhen.es: Both counts and at least four reasons are on the board.

discussionQuestions: What would happen to profit if both stores kept lowering their prices?
What did each store change to stand out?
Would you pay more for something if it came with a guarantee or was made just for you?
How is this like the story where Neville's cheap shelf fell, but Ellis's quality work lasted?
What does 'competitive advantage' mean?

beforeClass.en: Push desks together into two stores, each with a paper sign and the same goods: paper bookmarks plus classroom pencils and erasers. Put matching index-card price signs on both. Leave spare index cards out for business cards, and count 8 paper clips for each customer.
beforeClass.es: Push desks together into two stores, each with a paper sign and the same goods: paper bookmarks plus classroom pencils and erasers. Put matching index-card price signs on both. Leave spare index cards out for business cards, and count 8 paper clips for each customer.

runningLongOrShort.en: Long: in the Differentiation Challenge, allow each store one change only. Short: halfway through the Shopping Round, swap in new customers so more students get to shop.
runningLongOrShort.es: Long: in the Differentiation Challenge, allow each store one change only. Short: halfway through the Shopping Round, swap in new customers so more students get to shop.

beforeClass.en: Push desks together into two stores, each with a paper sign and the same goods: paper bookmarks plus classroom pencils and erasers. Write matching price signs on scrap paper for both. Leave spare scrap paper out for business cards, and tear 8 scrap-paper coins for each customer.
beforeClass.es: Push desks together into two stores, each with a paper sign and the same goods: paper bookmarks plus classroom pencils and erasers. Write matching price signs on scrap paper for both. Leave spare scrap paper out for business cards, and tear 8 scrap-paper coins for each customer.

45.label: 45 Minutes

fromScratch.costPerStudent: $0 — everything is free or from home
fromScratch.description: Teams sell identical stock of paper bookmarks and pencils, collect scrap-paper coins in cups from home, and use scrap paper for packaging and loyalty cards. Profit is charted on the board, and each student writes a reflection on plain paper.
items: Plain paper — 28 sheets, free: 8 torn into strips for 6 bookmarks per team (up to 8 teams), 20 one per student to write the reflection
Pencils — 36 from the classroom: 16 as starting stock (2 per team, up to 8 teams, returned afterwards), 20 one per student for writing
Scrap paper — about 280 pieces, free: 240 torn into coins (8 per shopper for about 10 shoppers in each of 3 rounds), 40 for Round 2 packaging and loyalty cards
Paper cups — 8, one per team for the coins taken in, from home, free
Board — teacher, for sales, prices, the cost per item and the profit chart

basicClassroom.costPerStudent: $0 — uses supplies the school already has
basicClassroom.description: Teams sell identical stock of paper bookmarks and pencils, collect paper clips in cups, and use scrap paper for packaging and loyalty cards. Profit is charted on the board, and each student writes a reflection on plain paper.
items: Plain paper — 28 sheets: 8 torn into strips for 6 bookmarks per team (up to 8 teams), 20 one per student to write the reflection
Pencils — 36 from the classroom: 16 as starting stock (2 per team, up to 8 teams, returned afterwards), 20 one per student for writing
Scrap paper — about 40 pieces, shared, for Round 2 packaging and loyalty cards
Paper cups — 8, one per team for the clips taken in
Paper clips — about 240, 8 per shopper for about 10 shoppers in each of 3 rounds, kept in piles for the profit count
Board — teacher, for sales, prices, the cost per item and the profit chart

sayThis.en: "Every team is selling the same thing. Identical stock, identical start. The only way to win a customer is to take them off somebody else. That's what competition actually is."
sayThis.es: "Every team is selling the same thing. Identical stock, identical start. The only way to win a customer is to take them off somebody else. That's what competition actually is."

doneWhen.en: Every team has identical counted stock and an empty cup on the desk.
doneWhen.es: Every team has identical counted stock and an empty cup on the desk.

watchFor.en: Teams checking whether someone got more. Show them the counts out loud and settle it.
watchFor.es: Teams checking whether someone got more. Show them the counts out loud and settle it.

description.en: Split class into 6-8 competing businesses selling similar products. Each team gets identical starting inventory and an empty cup for the paper clips they take in. Explain: you must attract customers away from competitors.
description.es: Split class into 6-8 competing businesses selling similar products. Each team gets identical starting inventory and an empty cup for the paper clips they take in. Explain: you must attract customers away from competitors.

description.en: Split class into 6-8 competing businesses selling similar products. Each team gets identical starting inventory and an empty cup for the scrap-paper coins they take in. Explain: you must attract customers away from competitors.
description.es: Split class into 6-8 competing businesses selling similar products. Each team gets identical starting inventory and an empty cup for the scrap-paper coins they take in. Explain: you must attract customers away from competitors.

sayThis.en: "Round one, price only. You can't change the product, you can't advertise. All you can do is go lower than the team next to you. Off you go."
sayThis.es: "Round one, price only. You can't change the product, you can't advertise. All you can do is go lower than the team next to you. Off you go."

doneWhen.en: Every team's round-one sales and final price are on the board.
doneWhen.es: Every team's round-one sales and final price are on the board.

watchFor.en: The floor being reached in two minutes, then boredom. That's exactly the lesson — let it happen and name it.
watchFor.es: The floor being reached in two minutes, then boredom. That's exactly the lesson — let it happen and name it.

description.en: Teams can only compete on price. Customers (rotating students) shop for best deals. Track sales. Debrief: What happened to prices? (Race to the bottom.) Did anyone make profit?
description.es: Teams can only compete on price. Customers (rotating students) shop for best deals. Track sales. Debrief: What happened to prices? (Race to the bottom.) Did anyone make profit?

doneWhen.en: Every team's round-one sales and final price are on the board. Each team counts its clips from Round 1 into its own pile, and the teacher writes the number on the board.
doneWhen.es: Every team's round-one sales and final price are on the board. Each team counts its clips from Round 1 into its own pile, and the teacher writes the number on the board.

doneWhen.en: Every team's round-one sales and final price are on the board. Each team counts its paper coins from Round 1 into its own pile, and the teacher writes the number on the board.
doneWhen.es: Every team's round-one sales and final price are on the board. Each team counts its paper coins from Round 1 into its own pile, and the teacher writes the number on the board.

sayThis.en: "Now you can change the product. Add something. Bundle two together. Make a loyalty card. You don't have to be the cheapest if you're the only one who has it."
sayThis.es: "Now you can change the product. Add something. Bundle two together. Make a loyalty card. You don't have to be the cheapest if you're the only one who has it."

doneWhen.en: Every team has made at least one visible change to its product or offer.
doneWhen.es: Every team has made at least one visible change to its product or offer.

watchFor.en: Teams still just cutting prices out of habit. Ask what makes theirs different, and wait.
watchFor.es: Teams still just cutting prices out of habit. Ask what makes theirs different, and wait.

description.en: Now teams can change their product — add features, improve packaging, offer bundles, create loyalty cards. Same shopping period. Track sales and compare to Round 1.
description.es: Now teams can change their product — add features, improve packaging, offer bundles, create loyalty cards. Same shopping period. Track sales and compare to Round 1.

doneWhen.en: Every team has made at least one visible change to its product or offer. Each team counts its clips from Round 2 into a second pile, and the teacher writes the number on the board.
doneWhen.es: Every team has made at least one visible change to its product or offer. Each team counts its clips from Round 2 into a second pile, and the teacher writes the number on the board.

doneWhen.en: Every team has made at least one visible change to its product or offer. Each team counts its paper coins from Round 2 into a second pile, and the teacher writes the number on the board.
doneWhen.es: Every team has made at least one visible change to its product or offer. Each team counts its paper coins from Round 2 into a second pile, and the teacher writes the number on the board.

sayThis.en: "Everything's allowed. Price, product, service, and thirty seconds of advertising each. Tell the room why you."
sayThis.es: "Everything's allowed. Price, product, service, and thirty seconds of advertising each. Tell the room why you."

doneWhen.en: Every team has given a pitch and round-three sales are recorded.
doneWhen.es: Every team has given a pitch and round-three sales are recorded.

watchFor.en: Adverts that are only a price. Ask what else the customer gets.
watchFor.es: Adverts that are only a price. Ask what else the customer gets.

description.en: Teams can use price, differentiation, AND customer service. Introduce advertising (30-second pitches). Final shopping round. Track all transactions.
description.es: Teams can use price, differentiation, AND customer service. Introduce advertising (30-second pitches). Final shopping round. Track all transactions.

doneWhen.en: Every team has given a pitch and round-three sales are recorded. Each team counts its clips from Round 3 into a third pile, and the teacher writes the number on the board.
doneWhen.es: Every team has given a pitch and round-three sales are recorded. Each team counts its clips from Round 3 into a third pile, and the teacher writes the number on the board.

doneWhen.en: Every team has given a pitch and round-three sales are recorded. Each team counts its paper coins from Round 3 into a third pile, and the teacher writes the number on the board.
doneWhen.es: Every team has given a pitch and round-three sales are recorded. Each team counts its paper coins from Round 3 into a third pile, and the teacher writes the number on the board.

sayThis.en: "Profit for each round, not sales. Chart all three. Round one you probably sold loads and made nothing. Look at which round made you money and what you were doing differently."
sayThis.es: "Profit for each round, not sales. Chart all three. Round one you probably sold loads and made nothing. Look at which round made you money and what you were doing differently."

doneWhen.en: Every team has three profit figures charted, one per round.
doneWhen.es: Every team has three profit figures charted, one per round.

watchFor.en: Sales counts being treated as success. Keep pulling it back to profit.
watchFor.es: Sales counts being treated as success. Keep pulling it back to profit.

description.en: Calculate profit/loss for each round. Chart class results. Discuss: Which strategy worked best? Why do some businesses succeed while others fail? What made customers switch? Use the cost per item the teacher writes on the board: clips taken in − cost of the items sold = profit.
description.es: Calculate profit/loss for each round. Chart class results. Discuss: Which strategy worked best? Why do some businesses succeed while others fail? What made customers switch? Use the cost per item the teacher writes on the board: clips taken in − cost of the items sold = profit.

description.en: Calculate profit/loss for each round. Chart class results. Discuss: Which strategy worked best? Why do some businesses succeed while others fail? What made customers switch? Use the cost per item the teacher writes on the board: paper coins taken in − cost of the items sold = profit.
description.es: Calculate profit/loss for each round. Chart class results. Discuss: Which strategy worked best? Why do some businesses succeed while others fail? What made customers switch? Use the cost per item the teacher writes on the board: paper coins taken in − cost of the items sold = profit.

description.en: Work one round at a time with real clips. Take the team's pile for that round. Give back 1 clip for each item the team sold, because each item cost 1 clip. Count the clips that are left. That is the profit. The teacher draws that many dots in the team's row for that round on the board. Talk: Which round left the most clips? What were you doing then?
description.es: Work one round at a time with real clips. Take the team's pile for that round. Give back 1 clip for each item the team sold, because each item cost 1 clip. Count the clips that are left. That is the profit. The teacher draws that many dots in the team's row for that round on the board. Talk: Which round left the most clips? What were you doing then?

sayThis.en: "Take your Round 1 pile. You sold 3 things, so give me back 3 clips. Now count what is left. That is your profit. Now do Round 2, then Round 3."
sayThis.es: "Take your Round 1 pile. You sold 3 things, so give me back 3 clips. Now count what is left. That is your profit. Now do Round 2, then Round 3."

watchFor.en: Children counting every clip they took in as profit. Hold up the clips that paid for the items and ask, "Are these still yours?"
watchFor.es: Children counting every clip they took in as profit. Hold up the clips that paid for the items and ask, "Are these still yours?"

doneWhen.en: Every team has dots on the board for all three rounds and can point to the round with the most.
doneWhen.es: Every team has dots on the board for all three rounds and can point to the round with the most.

description.en: Work one round at a time with real paper coins. Take the team's pile for that round. Give back 1 paper coin for each item the team sold, because each item cost 1 paper coin. Count the paper coins that are left. That is the profit. The teacher draws that many dots in the team's row for that round on the board. Talk: Which round left the most paper coins? What were you doing then?
description.es: Work one round at a time with real paper coins. Take the team's pile for that round. Give back 1 paper coin for each item the team sold, because each item cost 1 paper coin. Count the paper coins that are left. That is the profit. The teacher draws that many dots in the team's row for that round on the board. Talk: Which round left the most paper coins?
