description.en: Show what actually sold. Teams count how many they sold and how many are left, and say if their order was too big or too small. They say one thing to change next time.
description.es: Show what actually sold. Teams count how many they sold and how many are left, and say if their order was too big or too small. They say one thing to change next time.

sayThis.en: "Here is what sold. Count what you sold. Count what is left. Was your order too big, too small, or just right? What will you change next time?"
sayThis.es: "Here is what sold. Count what you sold. Count what is left. Was your order too big, too small, or just right? What will you change next time?"

watchFor.en: Blame on bad luck. Point at last year's chart on the board.
watchFor.es: Blame on bad luck. Point at last year's chart on the board.

doneWhen.en: Every team has said sold, left over, and one change for next time.
doneWhen.es: Every team has said sold, left over, and one change for next time.

sayThis.en: "Biggest season, hardest to call. New option: buy in bulk and each item costs less — but if it doesn't sell, you've lost more. Cheaper per item is not the same as cheaper."
sayThis.es: "Biggest season, hardest to call. New option: buy in bulk and each item costs less — but if it doesn't sell, you've lost more. Cheaper per item is not the same as cheaper."

doneWhen.en: Every team has a holiday order with a written yes or no on the bulk deal.
doneWhen.es: Every team has a holiday order with a written yes or no on the bulk deal.

watchFor.es: Every team taking the bulk deal automatically. Ask what happens if the season is quiet.

description.es: Holiday demand is highest but hardest to predict. Teams make ordering decisions with higher stakes. Introduce bulk discount option: order more at lower cost per item, but risk more waste.

description.es: The holiday is the busiest time, but it is hard to guess. Each team chooses to order a small pile or a big pile and says what could go wrong with each.

sayThis.en: "Holidays are busy. Do you want a small pile or a big pile? What goes wrong if you get a big pile and nobody comes? What goes wrong if you get a small pile and lots of people come?"
sayThis.es: "Holidays are busy. Do you want a small pile or a big pile? What goes wrong if you get a big pile and nobody comes? What goes wrong if you get a small pile and lots of people come?"

watchFor.en: Every team picking the big pile. Ask what happens if the holiday is quiet.
watchFor.es: Every team picking the big pile. Ask what happens if the holiday is quiet.

doneWhen.en: Every team has picked a small or a big pile and said one thing that could go wrong.
doneWhen.es: Every team has picked a small or a big pile and said one thing that could go wrong.

sayThis.en: "Sales drop. Two choices. Order less and stay safe, or discount the leftover holiday stock and pull in bargain hunters. Selling at a discount still beats selling nothing."
sayThis.es: "Sales drop. Two choices. Order less and stay safe, or discount the leftover holiday stock and pull in bargain hunters. Selling at a discount still beats selling nothing."

doneWhen.en: Every team has a summer order and a decision on clearing old stock.
doneWhen.es: Every team has a summer order and a decision on clearing old stock.

watchFor.en: Refusal to mark anything down. Ask what unsold stock is worth in a year.
watchFor.es: Refusal to mark anything down. Ask what unsold stock is worth in a year.

description.es: Demand drops. Teams must decide: order less (safe), or stock sale items to attract bargain hunters? Introduce clearance pricing for leftover holiday inventory.

description.en: Summer is slow. Teams choose: order a small pile, or sell leftover holiday things for less money so more people buy them.
description.es: Summer is slow. Teams choose: order a small pile, or sell leftover holiday things for less money so more people buy them.

sayThis.en: "Summer is slow. Fewer people come. Do you order a small pile? Or do you sell your leftover things for less money so people buy them? Selling for less is better than not selling."
sayThis.es: "Summer is slow. Fewer people come. Do you order a small pile? Or do you sell your leftover things for less money so people buy them? Selling for less is better than not selling."

watchFor.en: Teams who never want to lower a price. Ask what happens to things nobody buys.
watchFor.es: Teams who never want to lower a price. Ask what happens to things nobody buys.

doneWhen.en: Every team has a summer order and has said what they will do with leftovers.
doneWhen.es: Every team has a summer order and has said what they will do with leftovers.

sayThis.en: "Add all three seasons. Revenue, costs, profit, each season as its own bar. The winner isn't whoever had the best season — it's whoever survived the worst one."
sayThis.es: "Add all three seasons. Revenue, costs, profit, each season as its own bar. The winner isn't whoever had the best season — it's whoever survived the worst one."

doneWhen.en: Every team's chart shows revenue, cost and profit for all three seasons.
doneWhen.es: Every team's chart shows revenue, cost and profit for all three seasons.

watchFor.en: Charts with revenue only. Costs have to be on there or the bars lie.
watchFor.es: Charts with revenue only. Costs have to be on there or the bars lie.

description.es: Calculate total yearly profit across all three seasons. Create a simple bar chart on paper showing revenue, costs, and profit by season. Compare across teams. Crown the best retail manager.

description.en: Teams draw one bar for each season on their paper showing how many items they sold, with no money math. The class compares which season sold the most.
description.es: Teams draw one bar for each season on their paper showing how many items they sold, with no money math. The class compares which season sold the most.

sayThis.en: "Draw a bar for each season. Make it tall if you sold a lot and short if you sold a little. Which season was tallest?"
sayThis.es: "Draw a bar for each season. Make it tall if you sold a lot and short if you sold a little. Which season was tallest?"

watchFor.en: Bars that do not match the count. Count the items again, then draw.
watchFor.es: Bars that do not match the count. Count the items again, then draw.

doneWhen.en: Every team's paper shows three bars, one for each season.
doneWhen.es: Every team's paper shows three bars, one for each season.

sayThis.en: "Which season was hardest to predict, and why? Then one forecasting tip you'd give someone doing this next year."
sayThis.es: "Which season was hardest to predict, and why? Then one forecasting tip you'd give someone doing this next year."

doneWhen.en: Every student has written one forecasting tip.
doneWhen.es: Every student has written one forecasting tip.

watchFor.en: Tips that are just try harder. Ask what they'd actually look at first.
watchFor.es: Tips that are just try harder. Ask what they'd actually look at first.

description.en: Discuss: Which season was hardest to predict? What would you do differently next year? How do real stores use data to make these decisions? Write one forecasting tip you learned on a scrap of paper.
description.es: Discuss: Which season was hardest to predict? What would you do differently next year? How do real stores use data to make these decisions? Write one forecasting tip you learned on a scrap of paper.

discussionQuestions: How accurate were your predictions compared to actual demand?

ell.label: English Language Learners
strategies: Draw a picture on each product card (pencil, eraser, bookmark) so students can order without reading the name.

description.en: Teams complete comprehensive "Slow Season Action Plan" in pencil on a sheet of paper: **PART 1: Understanding the Problem** Current situation (how much money coming in now vs. busy season?) How long will slow season last? Do we have reserve funds? How much? **PART 2: Survival Strategies** What can we PREPARE for next busy season? (build inventory, make products, plan marketing) What can we IMPROVE right now? (fix equipment, reorganize, train skills) What can we LEARN to get better? (take classes, practice, research) What RELATIONSHIPS can we strengthen? (call past customers, thank people, ask for referrals) Can we offer a DIFFERENT product for this season? (pivot: pool company offers spa cleaning, pumpkin farm hosts winter events) **PART 3: Budget Planning** Use reserve funds: Yes or No? How much? Cut expenses: What can wait? Investments worth making: What will help later?

discussionQuestions: What's the difference between a failing business and a business in slow season?
Why is giving up during slow season a bad idea?
How can slow times actually be GOOD for a business?
What does 'the roots are growing underground' mean for business? (Frances's garden metaphor)
Why did Ms. Rivera call? How did something the team did in November help them in January? (relationship building)
What's an emergency fund and why do businesses need one?
Can you think of businesses in our community that have slow seasons? What do they do?
How is 'slow season' different from 'no one wants your product'?

discussionQuestions: **Financial Analysis:** Which business made the most profit? Why do you think that happened?
**Product Performance:** If you could only sell ONE product, which would you choose and why?
**Strategic Thinking:** The friends in the story chose Option B — stay the same size. Would you make the same choice? Why or why not?
**Personal Growth:** How did you grow as a person, not just as a business owner?
**Partnership Reflection:** What made a good business partner? How did you handle disagreements?
**Future Planning:** If you ran your business for another six months, what would you change?
extensionIdeas: Invite parents/families to attend expo as "investors"

Develop actual year-long plan similar to friends in story (Spring/Summer/Fall/Winter goals)
Research real young entrepreneurs and their stories
Create "Business Advice" book for next year's students

beforeClass.en: Pull together whatever sales data exists from earlier chapters and have it on the desks. Bring spare figures for anyone whose records went missing — nobody should sit out the final lesson because of a lost worksheet. If your class ran no businesses earlier, write one made-up season on the board for every team, such as: sold 20 bookmarks at $1 each, spent $6 on paper.

ell.label: English Language Learners
strategies: Post a picture timeline of this season's activities so students can point to what they did.
Give frames for the talk: "My business is ___. I learned ___."
Let students draw and label instead of writing full sentences.

learningDifferences.label: Students with Learning Differences
strategies: Give a poster outline with the sections already boxed.
Let a student present to the teacher or one partner instead of a crowd.
Use happy, proud and frustrated face cards drawn on scrap paper for the reflection instead of writing.

advanced.label: Advanced Students
strategies: Compare their results with another team's and explain what made the difference.
Serve as investor judges and write one question for each booth.
Write a four-season plan for the business with one goal for each season.
